# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC)

![](images/32a9cd19d7fd1276fcd924135bc06f3bfedbb7a0c682168f5b6a88961dfde399.webp)

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

This diagnosis judges whether the Evaporative Leak Check Module operation is normal or not, and whether the evaporative emission system has leak and clogging or not.

To purge the canister, after driving, perform the five hours soaking after ignition switch OFF in order to stabilize the evaporative gas status. \*After 5 or 7 or 9.5 hours passed, ECM is activated by soaking timer, and the leak check is started.

Judges whether the Evaporative Leak Check Module operation is normal or not, by measuring the reference pressure status via reference orifice (0.02 inch orifice). Judge as malfunction if the reference pressure is out of specified range. Then, judge whether there is a leak or not, by comparing the pressure (leak pressure) when the reference pressure and the evaporative emission system are in negative pressure condition. Judge as system leak in the evaporative emission system if the leak pressure is higher than reference pressure. Judge as clogging of pipe if the leak pressure becomes lower than the reference pressure within the specified amount of time.

0.02 inch leak and 0.04 inch leak can be distinguished by measuring the leak pressu The diagnosis results are stored inside ECM uñtil the engine is started again.

\*: When the test conditions are not met in 5 hours, perform diagnosis at elapsed time of 7 hours. When the test conditions are not met in 7 hours, perform diagnosis at elapsed time of 9.5 hours.

![](images/6a140166d3bfd1d49c69c456ef2dcff7dca7b745839c6414424b6ce1d1cdd795.webp)

# 2. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION

Evaporative Leak Check Module consists of the pressure sensor, the reference orifice (diameter of 0.02 inch), the vacuum pump which introduces the negative pressure into evaporative emission system, and the switching valve which switches the passage to introduce the negative pressure.

![](images/2b1ca6eb98c461ebf5cc7b346ac3ca5d7a673a8765364815394b3f262da01baf.webp)

(4) Pressure sensor Intake manifold

# Mode D (Clogging of pipe diagnosis and leak pressure measurement)

# Clogging of pipe

Purpose: Measure the time required for the evaporative emission system to reach the target negative pressure by the vacuum pump, and detect the clogging of pipe trouble.

Judge as clogging of pipe malfunction if the evaporative emission system reaches to the target negative pressure within the specified time.

# Leak pressure measurement

Purpose: Measure the pressure (leak pressure) when the evaporative emission system becomes the negative pressure by the vacuum pump.   
Store the pressure as a leak pressure while the following conditions are met.

Final ignition timing diagnosis

Judge as NG when the main relay does not turn to OFF after turning OFF the ignition switch and ECM keeps operating for more than the predetermined time.

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Detect the drain filter clogging by the pressure change during purge introduction. Judge as drain filter clogging malfunction if the pressure in the evaporative emission system piping suddenly decreases by the purging.

# 2. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION

![](images/80c8a6ec5564402cc644d069519ad76f48901425d77d4b7e978fdfc12ed21326.webp)

EN-08957

(1) Leak check valve ASSY (5) Vacuum pump )Fuel tank   
(2) Switching valve (6) Drain filter (10) Canister   
(3) Reference orifice (0.02 inch ori- (7) Purge control solenoid valve fice)   
(4) Pressure sensor Intake manifold

# 3.  EXECUTION CONDITION

![](images/071ea79eb5a5c1963f8037da48d25093643d975427ae980212230b961ac6edbf.webp)

# 4.GENERAL DRIVING CYCLE

Perform the diagnosis continuously when purging is performed after 20000 ms have passed since the engine started.

# 5. DIAGNOSTIC METHOD

![](images/9c9f393c6fdd3680d46f93cbc9f6b773c6433c0e5dc9d59f6bff3c952e6f4553.webp)

Calculate the difference between the Evaporative Leak Check Module pressure sensor output value of 5 seconds ago and the value at the present moment, and if the value is greater than the judgment value, detect as filter clogging trouble and judge as malfunction.   
Judge as NG when the following conditions are established.

# Judgment value

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Judge as NG when the status enters into any one of the followings. Although starter signal input is present in уCM, the engine does not start (diagnosis 1) Although starter signal input is present i ECM, starting takes more time than it should (diagnosis The engine stops immediately after starting except by operating the ignition switch (diagnosis

# Diagnosis 1

# 3. GENERAL DRIVING CYCLE

Perform the diagnosis continuously after the enable conditions have been established.

# 4. DIAGNOSTIC METHOD

Diagnosis 1   
If the duration of time while the following conditions are met is longer than the time indicated, judge as NG. Judgment Value

![](images/6355763487536cb2adb4f6aa7f09247d2ab733199518f4012cc57e536eaabdea.webp)

# Judgment Value

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

To detect malfunctions, the diagnostic uses a predictive model, individual cylinder fuel control, and the primary oxygen sensor measurement. The diagnostic does not directly attempt to separate the primary oxygen sensor measurement into individual cylinder contributions, but uses a predictive model to do so. Individual cylinders STFT are independently adjusted to obtain the moving 720 degree average lambda of all four cylinders using feedback from primary oxygen sensor. If any individual cylinder's STFT is different than the average of the other cylinder's STFT by a calibratable amount, that cylinder will be identified as failing.

# Monitor Method

This diagnostic monitor performs a functional check of the fuel system to determine an air-fuel ratio cylinder imbalance, as required by the regulations in Section (e)(6.2.1)(c). This method uses a parameter caled "imbalance value" which is calculated for each cylinder. The “imbalance value” is the difference between the individual STFT of the specific cylinder and the average value of the individual STFT of the other three cylinders. These imbalance values are compared to each other in order to determine the "imbalanced cylinder", which is the cylinder with the maximum “imbalance value”. A diagnostic value is calculated for the “imbalanced cylinder". When this diagnostic value is more than the predetermined threshold (lean malfunction) or less than the predetermined threshold (rich malfunction), a DTC for the most imbalanced cylinder is determined. DT oalaccliner follwig.

P219C: Cylinder 1 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance P219D: Cylinder 2 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance P219E: Cylinder 3 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance P219F: Cylinder 4 Air-Fuel Ratio Imbalance

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

Malfunction Criteria   
Rich malfunction (negative) Diagnostic value < Threshold   
or   
Lean malfunction (positive) Diagnostic value > Threshold   
Diagnostic value = “Imbalance value n” of the “Imbalanced cylinder”   
(n: Cylinder number (#1 or #2 or #3 or #4))   
Imbalance value n' = iSTFTn – Average (other 3 iSTFTs)   
For example: Imbalance value #1 = iSTFT # 1 − (iSTFT # 2+ iSTFT # 3 + iSTFT # 4) /3.   
Imbalanced cylinder: The cylinder with maximum (ABS (Imbalance value #1, #2, #3, #4)) is selected iSTFT: Individual cylinder STFT (Refer to the following about the detail)   
Individual Cylinder STFT (iSTFT n (k))   
Individual cylinder STFT (= iSTFT n (k) are calculated by integral control and individual cylinder  deviation u(k) converges to target (no deviation).   
STFT n(k) = iSTFT n (k-1) + C(tgt - u(k))   
iSTFT n (k) = Individual cylinder STFT   
u(k): Estimated individual cylinder  deviation\*   
tgt: Target (No deviation = zero)   
: Control gain (negative value)

Estimated individual cylinder  deviation "u(k)" is calculated by model (as described below). Estimation Model for individual cylinder  deviation (u(k))

Subaru developed a model for estimating individual cylinder  deviation\* by the output signal of the primary oxygen sensor (mounted on the collector section of the exhaust manifold). This estimation model makes it possible to control cylinder A/F individually. The estimation model is designed as follows.

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Detect the stuck of rear oxygen sensor voltage in lean state.   
When rear oxygen sensor voltage remains below the threshold value for predetermined time, diagnosis interrupts target air fuel ratio for control and raises output voltage.   
Judge as NG detecting the stuck in lean state when rear oxygen sensor voltage remains below the threshold value even after the interrupt control.

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Detect malfunction of soaking timer IC by the five diagnoses below.

![](images/a4cfb7a78614155829c91003ca97770a6271061c0ea5311f991a694e4404c0e8.webp)

This is an example of ELCM monitor execution at soak time of 5 hours.

![](images/26d5ee0e379a0505649572dfc8bd854f2595ba3c9a462f5bcc5292bd9671fc65.webp)

This is an example of ELCM monitor execution at soak time of 9.5 hours.

![](images/30ed69937e7406465e4592d681827b24e86f19565fcd5d80c691fb1eae97d520.webp)

# 2. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION

The soaking timer IC is built into the ECM.

# 3.  EXECUTION CONDITION

![](images/7af64e4ac7154aaacc27de7922425dd920378eaf9108e4a4f4d5fd6e7ab5a8ad.webp)

# 4.GENERAL DRIVING CYCLE

Perform the diagnosis only once when the ignition switch is OFF and when the ignition switch is ON after the soaking of one hour or more.

# EN(H4DO)(diag)-584

# 5.  DIAGNOSTIC METHOD

# <Timer diagnosis>

Start the count up operation of counters in ECM and in soaking timer IC when the engine is started. Judge as timer malfunction if the difference between the counter in ECM and counter in soaking timer IC exceeds the allowable limit when the ignition switch is OFF.

![](images/be505b4e621fb95d56e1dbec3daab5c7922a2945410399df8a1e17e0206c7d9c.webp)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/f5884934dca907126041e8d7ec7a5f3dd678f243df4841cf4ed076f6fd6b7183.webp)

# <Full count diagnosis>

Reset the counter in soaking timer IC and start the count up operation.   
Judge as full count diagnosis malfunction if counter in soaking timer IC is not \$3FF (1023 count) after 4 seconds.

![](images/614a1e1c98735689c240b12a24241b206181a9b7c4ca8d780686184f7d2c2aa2.webp)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/5538464b9e3efb038186790949d85425c1597785e915fad8b08fee61ada45ee0.webp)

# <Soaking timer IC setting diagnosis>

When setting the activation setting time to soaking timer IC, compare the writing value to soaking timer IC with read out value. Judge as malfunction if the values do not match 3 times in a row.

![](images/f89641eae8feb162e5717fbd012a11f4a4968fd7ae4c5043a844f382e0363611.webp)

EN-10766

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/43040f6355e967d711759447525a867b1eb0774dd7d131a08471e6c064492686.webp)

# <Timer diagnosis (during soaking)>

Wake-up at the predetermined interval until 5 or 7 or 9.5 hours have passed after the ignition switch is OFF, and compare the counter in soaking timer IC with the counter in ECM.

Judge as malfunction if the counter in soaking timer IC is counted up to maximum value (1023 count) when the counter in ECM is 1636 ms, or if the counter in soaking timer I is not counted up to maximum value (1023 count) when the counter in ECM is 2456 ms.

![](images/b2d09546a0cee1d7c650908924eba64135943a536d93d2caecb8faf60877f9e7.webp)

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/551f96b2edfe05c30c2d371a5e8869eaa716447393c40897cb37a9fae651a228.webp)

# <Wake-up diagnosis>

Store the number of wake-up activation when the ECM wakes up by the soaking timer IC. Next time when the ignition switch is ON, if the number of wake-up activation does not reach the predetermined value even though the counter in soaking timer IC operates 1 hour or more, judge as wake-up malfunction.

![](images/ee20bc6b3e0953791e289e71df5bcbf696d22dac864fd73c7a11ded9d57b249c.webp)

This service manual has been prepared to provide SUBARU service personnel with the necessary information and data for the correct maintenance and repair of SUBARU vehicles.

This manual includes the procedures for maintenance, disassembling, reassembling, inspection and adjustment of components and diagnostics for guidance of experienced mechanics.

Please peruse and utilize this manual fully to ensure complete repair work for satisfying our customers by keeping their vehicle in optimum condition. When replacement of parts during repair work is needed, be sure to use SÜBARU genuine parts.

All information, illustration and specifications contained in this manual are based on the latest product information available at the time of publication approval.

# c: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following:

1Always wear work clothes, a work cap, and protective shoes. Additionall, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc. Place "NO OPEN FLAMES" signs near the working area. Prepare a container and cloth to prevent scattering of fuels when performing work where fuels can be spilled. If the oil spils, wipe it off immediately to prevent from penetrating into flor or flowing out for environmental protection. Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts. When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement. Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from batery. Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle. Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, instaltion, disassembly or assembly. Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt. Al removed parts, if to be eusedshould be renstalledn the riginal posiions with attention to the correct directions, etc. Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required. Always inspect for fuel leaks after removing/instaling the fuel system components. Follow allgovernment and local regulations concerning disposal of refuse when disposing fuel.

# Throttle Body

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover.

(1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A).   
(2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> 3) Drain approximately 3.0 L (3.2 US qt, 2.6 Imp qt) of coolant. <Ref. to CO(H6DO)-13, DRAINING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, En iE COOlant.   
4) Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot.   
5) Remove the bolt (B) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.

![](images/f3fb70b340e52934f79a3846b751ecaa2bb70237000d9c56a0f37c95e7a793ea.webp)

![](images/0dbb1cda7bb85f3a738812d181fbc9291d48fdc6a8b98909f70f8e5cae33a13b.webp)

6) Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the left side wheel apron.

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/ff96a7ae780a384c56b9c8bcc7bbe80b886ae65157e20b927d2d23ddffd04e5c.webp)

7) Disconnect the connector (A) from the throttle position sensor, and disconnect the preheater hose (B) from the throttle body.   
8 Remove the throttle body from the intake manifold.

![](images/84a841c82a384eaa30f38aefea7c74a1d44f30306b2ab781a0ec1081b4ab4df1.webp)

# Throttle Body

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the throttle body to the intake manifold.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 8 Nm (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)   
Connect the connector (A) to the throttle position sensor, and connect the preheater hose (B) to the throtle   
body.

![](images/dd0b2df4d955ab07de9412fcca75a7bd1b2f12be78f162f6acc5af7c9447fb16.webp)

3) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>   
4) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
5) Fill engine coolant. <Ref. to CO(H6Dэ)-14, FILLING OF ENGINE COOLANT, REPLACEMENT, Engine   
Coolant.   
6) Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

# 1.  THROTTLE SENSOR (METHOD WITH CIRCUIT TESTER)

1 Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents. While pressing the section (A) shown in the figure, move the lock lever (B) in the direction of the arrow to disconnect the connectors from the ECM in numerical order as shown in the figure.

![](images/fb5272c1e8576a36fa0596b0ba8979b1089ce059509c1c43487951b948979b6e.webp)

Attach the ST between the ECM, engine harness and the bulkhead wiring harness. <Ref. to EN(H6DO)(di   
ag)-6, CAUTION, General Description.>   
ST 18460AA050 CHECK BOARD   
4 Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
5) Turn the ignition switch to ON. (Engine OFF)

6) Measure the voltage between ECM connector terminals using ST.

![](images/a957ddfde4afa2069046ccc6c274a6a5a0b5e2a7a8430964da75d2e455cebb6b.webp)

(A) To the check board connector (ECM connector)

![](images/fca297b554e18b722b87597b2798fdf77b985d9630400caa35c53e2c270a7b1d.webp)

7) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

# 2. THROTTLE SENSOR (METHOD WITH SUBARU SELECT MONITOR)

1) Turn the ignition switch to ON. (Engine OFF) Read the throttle opening angle signal and voltage of throttle sensor using Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(HGDO)(diag)-53, DISPLAY CURRENT ENGINE DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.>

![](images/df1caa549d8697ec450837a27c47a0e619102fd37e2c77e9c7665b51f4281ada.webp)

# 3. OTHER INSPECTIONS

1) Check that the throttle body has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Check that the preheater hose has no cracks, damage or loose part.

# Intake Manifold

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover.

(1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A).   
(2) Carefully pull up the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. 2) Release the fuel pressure. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-95, RELEASING OF FUEL PRESSURE, PROCEDURE, Fuel.>   
) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> 4 Open the fuel filer lid and remove the fuel filler cap.

![](images/50f727a1f1f062bc83ea5dee01624e6b528957ed08a8cff3434ca0d2557e5165.webp)

NOTE:

This operation is required to release the inner pressure of the fuel tank.   
5) Disconnect the brake booster vacuum hose.

![](images/9e5c5b49985e642d3b8c03fbb25ad5e6e41fa278e3801a3ce8aee24b5e82fed0.webp)

6) Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot.

7) Remove the bolt (B) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.

![](images/b8c5b0083f6d121127727618ddfaa2bbef9014500fa6c0aac539c8ac4dc590d1.webp)

Remove the air intake boot from the throtle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the left side wheel apron.

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/43ac327631a510e907d75492e6a6be6d8d419652a16d9c1d58e4072a14af0327.webp)

9) Remove the fuel injector. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-62, REMOVAL, Fuel Injector.>

10) Disconnect the engine harness connector.

![](images/bfb7c9cffbce96f63de3ee080e3f4e25080e140016b245d17e94c52eb7fb1c4c.webp)

11) Disconnect the connector (A) from the throttle body, and remove the throttle body from the intake manifold.

NOTE: Do not disconnect the preheater hose.

# Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). () Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions () while moving it forward.

![](images/686284985313fcfb1b7a3058d794c6a5bca6ccf4842578e3ce3fb3f0bcdf6138.webp)

Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> 3) Disconnect the connector (A) from the manifold absolute pressure sensor, and remove the manifold absólute pressure sensor from intake manifold.

![](images/306bbb3ff102a92e078d8fc81298391ea109bbc3873755cdc7f13abe66038841.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the manifold absolute pressure sensor to the intake manifold, and connect the connector to th manifold absolute pressure sensor.

# Tightening torque: 6.4 Nm (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.   
Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the manifold absolute pressure sensor has no deformation, cracks or other damages. Connect dry-cell battery positive terminal to terminal No. 3 and dry-cell battery ground terminal to terminal No. 2, circuit tester ground terminal to terminal No. 2 and the circuit tester positive terminal to terminal No. 1.

NOTE:

Use new dry-cell batteries.   
Using a circuit tester, check that the initial voltage of each dry-cel battery is 1.6 V or more.And also check that the voltage of three batteries in series is between 4.8 V and 5.2 V.

For power supply, 5 V DC constant voltage power source can also be used.

![](images/1d91bedb83868666296229b73818a2f3ae91625642304c0fb53065befdb782be.webp)

FU-08642

3) Connect the Mighty Vac to the pressure port (A) of manifold absolute pressure sensor.

![](images/3b32a38c08828de623e005a46430f85bb31156e8e3d3ae3ceec33eee6dd526dd.webp)

4) Check the voltage when generating vacuum and positive pressure using Mighty Vac.

# CAUTION:

Do not apply vacuum of less than —88 kPa (−0.9 kg/cm², –12.8 psi). Doing so may damage the manifold absolute pressure sensor.

NOTE:

When vacuum occurs at the pressure port of manifold absolute pressure sensor, the voltage will drop from the value as in step 3). When positive pressure occurs, on the other hand, the voltage will rise.

![](images/268f5247491abdb9b5a184b4db1244f5802fd2796f264aee61c5ca0a06d8663f.webp)

# 14.Front Oxygen (A/F) Sensor

# A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> Lift up the vehicle.   
3) Disconnect the connector (A) of the front oxygen (A/F) sensor.   
4 Remove the clip (B) securing the front oxygen (A/F) sensor harness. (LH side only)   
5 Apply spray-type lubricant (004301003) or equivalent to the threaded portion of front oxygen (A/F) sensor, and leave it for one minute or more.   
6) Remove the front oxygen (A/F) sensor.

# CAUTION:

When removing the front oxygen (A/F) sensor, wait until exhaust pipe cools, otherwise it will damage the exhaust pipe.

# B: INSTALLATION

CAUTION:

If lubricant is spilt over the exhaust pipe, wipe it off with cloth to avoid emission of smoke or causing a fire.

1) Before instaling front oxygen (A/F) sensor, apply anti-seize compound only to the threaded portion of fror oxygen (A/F) sensor to make the next removal 'easier.

# CAUTION:

Never apply anti-seize compound to the protector of front oxygen (A/F) sensor.

Anti-seize compound: NEVER-SEEZ NSN, JET LUBE SS-30 or equivalent ) Install the front oxygen (A/F) sensor.

Tightening torque: 21 NбН (2.1 kgf-m, 15.5 ft-lb)   
3) Connect the connector (A) of front oxygen (A/F) sensor.   
4) Install the clip (B) securing the front oxygen (A/F) sensor harness. (LH side only)

LH side

Lower the vehicle. Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the front oxygen (A/F) sensor has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Measure the resistance between front oxygen (A/F) sensor terminals.

# 16.Engine Control Module (ECM)

# A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> While pressing the section (A) shown in the figure, move the lock lever (B) in the direction of the arrow to disconnect the connectors from the ECM in numericál order as shown in the figure. 3) Remove the ECM from the ECM bracket.

When the ECM of model with immobilizer has been replaced, be sure to perform the registration of immobilizer system.   
For model Without keyless access with push button start, refer to the Type B in "REGISTRATION MANUAL FOR IMMOBILIZER".   
:Except for Canada model with keyless access with push button start, refer to the Type D in "REGISTRATION MANUAL FOR IMMOBILIZER".   
For Canada model with keyless access with push button start, refer to the Type E in "REGISTRATION MANUAL FOR IMMOBILIZER”.

NOTE:

When replacing the ECM, be careful not to use the ECM of wrong specification to avoid any damage on the fuel injection system.

5) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

21.Fuel

A: PROCEDURE

1. RELEASING OF FUEL PRESSURE

WARNING: Place "NO OPEN FLAMES" signs near the working area.

CAUTION:   
Be careful not to spill fuel.   
1) Remove the fuse of fuel pump from main fuse box. 2) Start the engine and run it until it stalls.   
3) After the engine stalls, crank it for five more seconds.   
4) Turn the ignition switch to OFF.   
) Install the fuse of fuel pump to the main fuse box.

![](images/55ff874c110c557ee17180a8e1bd211b8ec81e6fbb274b102f69d37bf04c59e8.webp)

2.  DRAINING FUEL (WITH SUBARU SELECT MONITOR)

# WARNING:

Place “NO OPEN FLAMES” signs near the working area.

CAUTION: Be careful not to spill fuel.

NOTE:

If the fuel pump cannot be driven, refer to the procedures for draining from the fuel filer hose. <Ref. to FUHGDO7, DRAINING FUEL (THROUGH THE FUEL FILLER HOSE), PROCEDURE,Ful. Be careful not to let the battery run-out.   
Be aware that the fel may remain in the fuel tank ater ding the fuel   
1) Release the fuel pressure. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-95, RELEASING OF FUEL PRESSURE, PROCEDURE, Fuel.>   
) Remove the clip (A) securing the fuel delivery tube. 3 Attach the ST to the fuel pipe assembly, and push the ST in the direction of arrow mark to disconnect the fuel delivery tube ().   
ST 42099AE000 QUICK CONNECTOR RELEASE

# CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill fuel.   
Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth. 4) Connect ST to the fuel delivery tube.   
ST 18471AA000 FUEL PIPE ADAPTER   
5) Connect the gasoline proof hose to ST and put the end of the hose in the container. 6) Drive the fuel pump and drain the fuel using Subaru Select Monitor.

![](images/90f6c672bc72404f518122af82bfbb53c2d13dfe1541830092705e115ac00e14.webp)

# CAUTION: Be careful not to spill fuel.

NOTE:

For detailed operation procedures of Subaru Select Monitor 4, refer to “Application help" 7) Install the related parts in the reverse order after draining the fuel.

# CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill fuel.   
Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth.   
Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface of the pipe.   
Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

# 31.Fuel System Trouble in General A: INSPECTION

![](images/38f69aad2435220d38e64de7109a00a0b3d4d262889c2b91b043ec2f3c3868fe.webp)

NOTE:

When the vehicle is left unattended for an extended period of time, water may accumulate in the fuel tank.   
Fill fuel fully to prevent the problem.

In snow-covered areas, mountainous areas, sking areas, etc. where ambient temperatures drop to 0°C (32F) or lessthroughout the winter season, use a water removing agent in the fuel system to prevent freezing fuél system and accumulating water.

When water is accumulated in fuel filter, fil the water removing agent in the fuel tank.   
Before using water removing agent, follow the cautions noted on the bottle.

# General Description

# A: COMPONENT

# 1. CANISTER, PURGE CONTROL SOLENOID VALVE, EGR CONTROL VALVE, EGR PIPE AND DRAIN FILTER

For the components of the canister, purge control solenoid valve, EGR control valve, EGR pipe and drain fil ter, refer to FU (H6DO). <Ref. to FÜ(H6DO)-3, COMPONENT, General Description.>

# B: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following: 1. Always wear work clothes, a work cap, and protective shoes. Additionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. 3. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc.   
Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated   
parts.   
When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and   
replacement.   
Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery.   
Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle.   
Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly.   
Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.   
Al removed parts, ito be reused, should be reinstalled in the original positions with attention to the correct   
directions, etc.   
Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required.   
Be sure to tighten the fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

# C:  PREPARATION TOOL

# 1. GENERAL TOOL

# Front Catalytic Converter

# A: REMOVAL

The front and rear catalytic converters are integrated into the front exhaust pipe;therefore, refer to “Front Ex.   
haust Pipe" for the removal procedure. Ref to EX(H6DO-6, REMOVAL, Front Exhaust Pipe.

# B: INSTALLATION

The front and rear catalytic converters are integrated into front exhaust pipe as one unit; therefore, refer to Front Exhaust Pipe" for installtion procedure.Ref. to EX(H6DO)-7, INSTALLATiON, Front Exhaust Pipe

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check the connections and welded parts for exhaust leaks.   
Make sure there are no holes or rusting.

# 3Rear Catalytic Converter

A: REMOVAL

The front and rear catalytic converters are integrated into the front exhaust pipe; therefore, refer to "Front Ex haust Pipe" for the removal procedure.Ref. to EX(H6DO-6, REMOVAL, Front Exhaust Pipe.

# B: INSTALLATION

The front and rear catalytic converters are integrated into front exhaust pipe as one unit; therefore, refer to Front Exhaust Pipe" for installtion procedure.Ref. to EX(H6DO-7, INSTALLATiON, Front Exhaust Pipe.

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check the connections and welded parts for exhaust leaks.   
Make sure there are no holes or rusting.

# 5 Purge Control Solenoid Valve

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pull up the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

![](images/c93e38b284b4606af1cbdc7ec865bc45f3e1b51f1ffaf30609b229d614eb3a9c.webp)

) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.   
Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot.   
4) Remove the bolt (B) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.

![](images/97ebbf7269530ea9b1a75db4e9609fba967ef923838e81afb13b5cd22eded109.webp)

FU-20197

Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the lefi side wheel apron.

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/93f5bed08f7ebddded1fde98590bf42bff57adc03b35fe4b0aeff3653896f95a.webp)

6) Disconnect the connector (A) and vacuum hose (B) from the purge control solenoid valve, and remove the purge control solenoid valve.

![](images/be479fc55353cc43ba2c86ac91fa00cb9cb493b6bb274e852ae9be9fbdad9104.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Installthe purge control solenoid valve, and connect the connector and vacuum hose to the purge control sólenoid valve.

NOTE: Connect the vacuum hose as shown in the figure.

![](images/7b720b2fca4d99280048e45dfae4c4fb187f1701e6af717145d0cb6f14a60e01.webp)

To intake manifold To fuel pipe

# Tightening torque: 19 NбН (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)

) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.> Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents. Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

# 1.  PURGE CONTROL SOLENOID VALVE

1) Check that the purge control solenoid valve has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Measure the resistance between the purge control solenoid valve terminals.

![](images/39e21797ae441dabc1ab5415a8fff9d53b619999ee9daafd478ed2db03f21e16.webp)

![](images/cd4fbd94e5c069925b243ed1c7d11038fd888aab69c1124500ddb496c6d3f063.webp)

3) Check that air does not come out from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/b25c3c6efbbfbe10f474bbda7900558521978b6ac08501416417011cdb331d90.webp)

4) Connect the battery positive terminal to the terminal No. 1 and the battery negative terminal t the terminal No. 2. Check that air is discharged from (B), when supplying air to (A).

![](images/6a104be7a13d1bdf2645717e87e5e293cd2db0d8d6561ea178a493acafb7860f.webp)

# 2. OTHER INSPECTIONS

Check the vacuum hose for cracks, damage or looseness.

# EGR Control Valve

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

![](images/8454d77f8ce1b616c5fcb7bd5b8fe8e989f5b28ad356641e1eece67783fd8df2.webp)

) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.   
Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot.   
4) Remove the bolt (B) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.

![](images/69c2590045c2d57ad3b7a903cc80ca9edb8d9f469e0976a0e9d5fe5c96d54352.webp)

FU-20197

Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the lef side wheel apron.

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/cfd5a7202ffeb80a485e2857a2ad682e273481e4c0d0873bf26ac4e483acb494.webp)

6) Remove the EGR pipe A. <Ref. to EC(H6DO)-25, EGR PIPE A, REMOVAL, EGR Pipe.>   
7) Disconnect the connector (A) from EGR control valve, and remove the EGR control valve.

![](images/e97b7cc6060952bdd57f1e929e2b2aa807e9629055e7a73847ce8ee98ba50fe4.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the EGR control valve, and connect the connector to the EGR control valve. NOTE:   
Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 19 NбН (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)

2) Install the EGR pipe A. <Ref. to EC(H6DO)-28, EGR PIPE A, INSTALLATION, EGR Pipe.>   
3) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H6Dэ)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>   
4) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the EGR control valve has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Measure the resistance between EGR control valve terminals.

![](images/822b6678f65146613171b1f861758e307b1cee89769b2ee9b1b531a52bf74707.webp)

![](images/99049e501d528b7601dc4009a301d8c2f5716054793405ae0d974327f76a6ea3.webp)

# 7 EGR Pipe

# A: REMOVAL

# 1. EGR PIPE A

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.   
Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pull up the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

![](images/59fdcbd15a369fe7e864608ef249b0ba4b9713a134323c0bf65db72eb5048b48.webp)

3) Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot.   
4) Remove the bolt (B) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.

![](images/6c221ca554ee8894f5b3815f1d52812f624f70dade2b08f8b42ad1c0a204d797.webp)

FU-20197

Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the lef side wheel apron.

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/b23541c4f7dc154cc1864354029425e17fb28e24ef680f5c0a997a4fcdcff4bd.webp)

6 Lift up the vehicle.   
7) Remove the under cover. <Ref. to El-29, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>   
8) Remove the bolts securing the EGR pipe A to the cylinder head.

![](images/17358e00657fa615cafa7b06b3f13232937cb109f8a1702574b836e28cf5e5b3.webp)

9) Lower the vehicle.

10) Remove the bolts securing the EGR pipe A to the EGR control valve, and pull out the EGR pipe A up ward.

![](images/56c2f5c3bd3f46d990b9587c4276ffaad90a2ac0357749831bc8cf5ed290f613.webp)

# 2 EGR PIPE B

1) Remove the intake manifold. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-24, REMOVAL, Intake Manifold.>   
2) Remove the EGR pipe B from the intake manifoid.

![](images/551ac5c0206787af90df68f7b11fdd9665eda76d47ebb210050465968ade4408.webp)

FU-08680

# B: INSTALLATION

# 1. EGR PIPE A

1) Temporarily attach the EGR pipe A to the cylinder head and the EGR control valve. NOTE:   
Use a new gasket.   
2) Tighten the bolts securing the EGR pipe A to the EGR control valve.   
Tightening torque: 6.4 Nm (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)   
3) Lift up the vehicle.   
4) Tighten the bolts securing the EGR pipe A to the cylinder head.

Tightening torque: 6.4 NбН (0.7 kgf-m, 4.7 ft-lb)

) Install the under cover. <Ref. to EI-29, INSTALLATION, Front Under Cover.>   
6) Lower the vehicle.   
7 Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-11, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>   
Install the collector cover.   
9) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

EGR PIPE B

1) Install the EGR pipe B to the intake manifold.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 19 NбН (1.9 kgf-m, 14.0 ft-lb)   
2) Install the intake manifold. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-31, INSTALLATION, Intake Manifold.>   
C: INSPECTION   
Check that the EGR pipe has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

# 11.Leak Check Valve Assembly

A: SPECIFICATION

Refer to “Canister for removal and installation ofthe leak check valve assembly. <Ref. to EC(H6DO)-5, REMOVAL, Canister.> <Ref. to EC(H6DO)-11, INSTALLATION, Canister.>

B: INSPECTION

# 1. CHECK SWITCHING VALVE

1) Check the resistance between switching valve terminals.

![](images/feb93a19ad36cc583322f99cc8ac4c6a6a021f6ee272a14206c9d0892dedcb15.webp)

![](images/93ac94393c3413804b7e6a5402919bf90394ade4e382fcb581b5b1264ee4fa85.webp)

2) Check that air is discharged from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/1955f9127cac5c63b997cf00e5d8129a3b748f902959bb2d88428e5087ca8bea.webp)

3) Connect the battery positive terminal to the terminal No. 5 and the batery negative terminal to the terminal No. 1. Check that air does not come out from (B) when air is blown into (A).

NOTE:

The purpose of this inspection is to check the valve movement, and it would be successif a large change of flow can be checked resulting from valve opening/closing. Therefore, it does not indicate a malfunction if a small amount of flow from (B) is detected when the valve is opened.

![](images/93e0569b15af5e2724e8aa8b42630997ae22b23567f18bcc52e94d6749a0525c.webp)

# 2.CHECK VACUUM PUMP

1) Connect the batery positive terminal to terminal No. 3 and the battery ground terminal to terminal No. 4.   
and inspect the vacuum pump operation.

CAUTION: Do not operate the vacuum pump for 5 minutes or more.

![](images/dbf1ce459945a1dc21f419bb695dc094ed7fa7a199296584b149c0418621085d.webp)

# 3.CHECK PRESSURE SENSOR

1) Connect dry-cell battery positive terminal to terminal No. 6 and dry-cel battery ground terminal to terminal No. 8, circuit tester positive terminal to terminal No. 7 and the circuit tester ground terminal to terminal No. 8.

NOTE:

Use new dry-cell batteries.   
Using circuit tester, check that the initial voltage of a single dry-cell battery is 1. V or more. And also check that the voltage of three batteries in series is between 4.8 V and 5.2 V.

For power supply, 5 V DC voltage source can also be used.

![](images/70d7d4ad244c5c9428e57d8a1e65a1c98dee6c18f97bf50d414b74eb4453a4e7.webp)

2) Check the voltage at a normal atmospheric pressure.

NOTE:

The atmospheric pressure at higher altitude is lower than normal. Therefore, the voltage is lower than the standard válue.

![](images/460dd403b188f5479b72f5d4e70a888887fcf8dcb6ebf7d4b2ec1e06988b2a28.webp)

Connect the battery positive terminal to terminal No. 3 and the battery ground terminal to terminal No. 4, and check that there is a voltage drop from the voltage measured in step 2) when the vacuum pump is operated.

![](images/030ca4157666b8a19f370d842762375c33d8174cd3c7a19f0875c76ade1f1d5f.webp)

# 4.  OTHER INSPECTIONS

Check that the leak check valve assembly has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

# 12.PCV Valve

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION: Do not remove unless the PCV valve is broken.

1) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pull up the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

![](images/c63a18b04112d2ef226cff96bd886908d4a7ca4457404b48225e5a039d8370a5.webp)

2) Remove the battery. <Ref. to SC(H6DO)-58, BATTERY, REMOVAL, Battery.>   
3) Disconnect the PCV hose.

![](images/003cb402fb38233505c092bbabd869858e376a1a7392bd6653ba85fede844125.webp)

4) Remove the PCV valve from rocker cover.

![](images/37509a0483f4d8115bbc63d7c1150a67ff7a4e62e9428485218988a19edbc9f0.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the PCV valve to the rocker cover.

NOTE: Apply liquid gasket to the bolt threads of PCV valve.

Liquid gasket: THRуE BOND 1324 (Part No. 004403042) or equivalent

Tightening torque: 25 NбН (2.5 kgf-m, 18.4 ft-lb)

2) Connect the PCV hose.   
3) Install the battery. <Ref. to SC(H6DO)-59, BATTERY, INSTALLATION, Battery.>   
4) Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

# 1. PCV VALVE

1) Check that the PCV valve has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Check that air is discharged from (B) when air is blown into (A).

![](images/8055a9a3f1d15932eb23efc3bfc1f2da50bece29070bab32d4f1f8ed33b4de16.webp)

EC-02816

# B: CAUTION

Prior to starting work, pay special attention to the following:

1. Always wear work clothes, a work cap, and protective shoes. Additionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary. Protect the vehicle using a seat cover, fender cover, etc. 3. Prepare the service tools, clean cloth, containers to catch grease and oil, etc. Vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts. When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement. Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle. Remove contamination including dirt and corosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly. Keep the removed parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt. Al removed parts, ito be reused, should be rinstalled in the original positions with attention to the correct directions, etc.' •Bolts, nuts and washers should be replaced with new parts as required. Be sure to tighten the fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

# Air Cleaner Element

# A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> 2) Remove the air intake duct. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-12, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.> 3 Disconnect the connector (A) from the mass air flow and intake air temperature sensor, and remove the clip (B) from the air cleaner case (rear).

![](images/b38968314ef5ebb8c1d9167a155538a4fea6cbe1faab88807cf0770646142ad2.webp)

4) Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air intake boot to the air cleaner case (rear), and then remove the clip () from the air cleaner'case (front).

![](images/f8c8cab1278fc44915bc220ccf5c16d4a32691146b073bc7828946106e5b08ff.webp)

5) Remove the air cleaner case (rear) and air cleaner element.

![](images/8ebcc96476718d84218dda656b558bd1195a50a0c394563378efd4411bf1d9b8.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Set the air cleaner case (rear) and air cleaner element to the air cleaner case (front).

# CAUTION:

Be sure to use SUBARU genuine air cleaner element depending on the engine type when replacing the air cleaner elements. Using other air cleaner element may affect the enine performance.

NOTE:

Install the air cleaner element as shown in the figure.

![](images/e453dfb9fb773c3f126ea33d0fe7ae5708c57b9902b929b7f743780039aaab1b.webp)

Upside )Downside (Air cleaner case (front) side (Aircleaner case (rear) side

# Air Cleaner Element

Check that there is no dirt or dust within the air cleaner case. If any dirt or dust is found, clean it. When setting the air cleaner case (rear), align the protrusion of the air cleaner case (rear) to the air cleaner case (front) to insert.

![](images/9c19650c8275025f4e36757a956e7bbdd3706e5c399011652b9b79aa61bef339.webp)

) Install the clips (B) to the air cleaner case (front), then tighten the clamp A) securing the air intake boot to the air cleaner case (rear).

Tightening torque: 3 Nm (0.3 kgf-m, 2.2 ft-lb)

![](images/41db491c3013e004f7851995257a4b2adb4cfb40bdbe24190bd1ac02767ba443.webp)

3) Connect the connector (A) to the mass air flow and intake air temperature sensor, and install the clip (B) tó the air cleaner case (rear).

![](images/b8f6f5387b03d01ba4e35e0ef41cc3ab046bfa9ae513c37bda8cf44fbe9ff7b9.webp)

4) Install the air intake duct. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-12, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Duct.>   
5) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the air cleaner element has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Check the air cleaner element for excessive dirt.

# Air Cleaner Case

# A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> ) Remove the air cleaner element. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-4, REMOVAL, Air Cleaner Element.>   
3) Remove the bolts securing the air cleaner case (front) to the vehicle body.   
4) Remove the air cleaner case (front).

NOTE: The protrusion of the air cleaner case (front) is inserted in the cushion of the air cleaner case bracket.

![](images/c6dfab122485840747ed52854bb6ea6859dca8728a399bf5c846f6a50d6e966c.webp)

5) Remove the air cleaner case bracket from the vehicle.

![](images/8bc9698f2d5903a612b51cbac085878c0c7e27eb8f95eefa92e25bc546d7ebb2.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the air cleaner case bracket to the vehicle.

Tightening torque: 7.5 NбН (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-lb)

) Instal the air cleaner case (front) to the vehicle body and air cleaner case bracket.   
NOTE:   
Make sure that the protrusion of the air cleaner case (front) is inserted in the cushion of the air cleaner case bracket.

Tightening torque: 6 Nm (0.6 kgf-m, 4.4 ft-lb)

![](images/d9ab4f452230164cda7c54acb9d5e01a2dcd808d84df6eec5524ab5606e3eff5.webp)

3) Install the air cleaner element. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-5, INSTALLATION, Air Cleaner Element.>   
4) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the air cleaner case has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Check that the air intake boot has no cracks, damage or loose part.

# Air Intake Boot

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the collector cover.

(1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A).   
(2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. Loosen the clamp (A) securing the air cleaner case (rear) to the air intake boot.   
3) Loosen the clamp (B) securing the throttle body to the air intake boot.   
4) Loosen the bolt (C) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.   
5) Disconnect the blow-by hose (D) from the air intake boot, and remove the air intake boot.

![](images/832d7bc2b861cefbbdf34a482e1df45d0107f29903afa5a102070fe2deb2a889.webp)

CAUTION: Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/4e6816118dd38d6e4d18f906f8691e75d70b8beff8d67a45797a5c375a664109.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the air intake boot and connect the blow-by hose (D) to the air intake boot.   
2 Tighten the clamp (B) securing the throttle body to the air intake boot.   
3) Tighten the bolt (C) securing the air intake boot to the collector cover bracket.   
4) Tighten the clamp (A) securing the air cleaner case (rear) to the air intake boot.

Tightening torque: T1: 3 Nm (0.3 kgf-m, 2.2 ft-lb) T2: 6.5 Nm (0.7 kgf-m, 4.8 ft-lb)

![](images/ef7f179e07bbe83771f5d59e35838bdd6fe9d3c4b12b03117fe19555f995c0f3.webp)

5) Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the air intake boot has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Inspect that no foreign objects are mixed in the air intake boot.

# Air Intake Duct

# A: REMOVAL

Remove the clip which secures the air intake duct, and remove the air intake duct.

![](images/d14d0a26bf36d606fb8c98f33cc760038d06dd608a1617102952b306c560c41c.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

Install the air intake duct, and install the clips securing the air intake duct.

# C: INSPECTION

1) Check that the air intake duct has no deformation, cracks or other damages.   
2) Inspect that no foreign objects are mixed in the air intake duct.

# 6Resonator Chamber

A: REMOVAL

The resonator chamber and air cleaner case are integrated into one unit; therefore, refer to "Air Cleaner Case” for removal procedure. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-8, REMOVAL, Air Cleaner Case.>

# B: INSTALLATION

The resonator chamber and air cleaner case are integrated into one unit; therefore, refer to "Air Cleaner Case" for installation procedure. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-9, INSTALLATION, Air Cleaner Case.>

# C: INSPECTION

Check that the resonator chamber has no deformation, cracks or other damages.

Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle. Remove or installthe engine in an area where chain hoists liting devices, earevilable for ready use. When lifing up the vehicle, make sure to support the vehicle at the jack-up points. •Be careful not to let any oil or grease contact the clutch disc or flywheel. # Compression

# A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

After warming-up, engine becomes very hot. Be careful not to burn yourself during measurement.

NOTE:

Before checking the compression pressure, the compression condition of each cylinder can be confirmed   
as a guide by using the compression measurement mode in Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(H6DO)(di  
ag)-88, OPERATION, Active Test.   
In the compression measurement mode, the compression condition is judged by each cylinder speed. The   
high speed cylinder has low compression pressure and low speed cylinder has high compression' pressure.   
1) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pull up the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

![](images/94441a4d615acb95d56b9169b928d55aac8bc0705d143681c30d608f49adf460.webp)

2) After warming-up the engine, turn the ignition switch to OFF.   
3) Make sure that the battery is fully charged.   
4) Check the starter motor for satisfactory performance and operation.

5) Remove the fuse of fuel pump from main fuse box.

![](images/df8b3790aaddfeeb0a841637d8e24105c71fdf7733a6f3c015ad69d5ff1ee96a.webp)

6) Start the engine and run it until it stalls.   
7) After the enine stalls, crank it for five more seconds.   
8) Turn the ignition switch to OFF.   
Remove all spark plugs. <Ref. to G(H6DO-5, REMOVAL, Spark Plug.   
Insta he battery.Ref to SCGDO-5 BATTERY, INSTALLATION, Battery.   
11) Install the compression gauge to the spark plug hole.

NOTE: When using a screw-in type compression gauge, the screw should be less than 18 mm (0.71 in) long.

![](images/b2e1b60431ba89f83805ba55714bf9accef3004b5831d3df3b10edc1d9e2d83e.webp)

12) Depress the accelerator pedal to full throttle.

13) Crank the engine by the starter motor, and read the maximum value on the gauge when the needle of gauge is steady.

NOTE:

Perform at least two measurements per cylinder, and make sure that the values are correct.   
If the compression pressure is out of standard, check or adjust the pistons, valves and cylinders.   
compression pressure (350 r/min and fully open throttle): Standard 1,128 — 1,471 kPa (11.5— 15.0 kg/cm², 164 — 213 psi) Difference between cylinders 49 kPa (0.5 kg/cm², 7 psi) or less   
14) After inspection, instáll the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

# Idle Speed

# A: INSPECTION

1) Before checking the idle speed, check the following item:

(1) Check the air cleaner element is free from clogging, ignition timing is correct, spark plugs are in good condition, and hoses are connected properly.   
(2) Check the malfunction indicator light does not illuminate. Warm up the engine.   
Read the engine idle speed using Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(H6DO)(diag)-53, DISPLAY CURRENT ENGINE DATA, OPERATION, SUbaRU SElect MONitOr.

NOTE:

Idle speed cannot be adjusted manually, because the idle speed is automatically adjusted.   
If idle speed is out of standard, refer to the General Diagnosis Table under "Engine Control System”. <Ref.   
to EN(H6DO)(diag)-2, Basic Diagnostic Procedure.> ( Check the idle speed when no-loaded. (Headlight, heater fan, rear defroster, radiator fan, A and etc. are OFF)

Idle rpm (no load and select lever in "P” or “N” range): Standard 700±100 r/min (2) Check the idle speed when loaded. (Turn the A/C switch to ON and operate the compressor for at leást one minute before measurement.)

Idle speed (A/C ON and select lever in "P" or "N” range): Standard 700 — 910±100 r/min

# 4Ignition Timing

# A: INSPECTION

CAUTION: After warming-up, engine becomes very hot. Be careful not to burn yourself at measurement.

# 1.  METHOD WITH SUBARU SELECT MONITOR

1) Before checking the ignition timing, check the following item: (1) Check the air cleaner element is free from clogging, spark plugs are in good condition, and hoses are connected properly. (2) Check the malfunction indicator light does not illuminate.   
Warm up the engine.   
Read the ignition timing using Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to EN(H6DO)(diag)-53, DISPLAY CURRENT   
ENGINE DATA, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.> NOTE:   
If ignition timing is out of standard, check the ignition control system. Refer to “Engine Control System”. <Ref. to уN(H6DO)(ЙБЗ)-2, Basic Diagnostic Procedure.>

Ignition timing [BTDC/{r/min}]: Standard 15±8/700

# 2.  METHOD WITH TIMING LIGHT

1) Before checking the ignition timing, check the following item: (1) Check the air cleaner element is free from clogging, spark plugs are in good condition, and hoses are connected properly. (2) Check the malfunction indicator light does not illuminate.   
Warm up the engine.   
Stop the engine, and turn the ignition switch to OFF.   
4 Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. 5 Disconnect the ground terminal rom battery sensor. Ref to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents. 6) Remove the air intake duct. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-12, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.>   
7 Remove the air cleaner case and the air cleaner element. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-8, REMOVAL, Air Cleaner Case.> <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-4, REMOVAL, Air Cleaner Element.>   
) Connect the timing light to the power wire of #1 ignition coil.

10) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> 11 Start the engine, turn the timing light to the crank pulley, and check the ignition timing through the chain cover gauge.

If ignition timing is out of standard, check the ignition control system. Refer to “Engine Control System”. <Ref. to уN(H6DO)(ЙБЗ)-2, Basic Diagnostic Procedure.>

# Intake Manifold Vacuum

# A: INSPECTION

1) Warm up the engine.

) Remove the collector cover. (1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A). (2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward.

# Engine Oil Pressure

# A: INSPECTION

1) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents. 2 Remove the oil pressure switch from the oil pan upper. <Ref. to LÜ(H6DO)-18, REMэVAL, Oil Pressure Switch.>   
3) Attach the oil pressure gauge to the oil pan upper.

![](images/6a589f4e9b6e10fdfbd82e16f5ab6068a76daef5181de44a6ec32fd8121acda5.webp)

4 Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents. ) Refill the engine oil. <Ref. to LU(H6Dэ)-11, REPLACEMENT, Engine Oil.> 6 Start the engine, and check the oil pressure.

NOTE:

If the oil pressure is out of specification, check oil pump, oil flter and lubrication line. <Ref. to LU(H6DO)- 31, Engine Lubrication System Trouble in General.> if the oil pressure warning light is ON and oil pressure is within specification, check the oil pressure switch. <Ref. to LÜ(H6DO)-8, Oil Pressure System.> <Ref. to LU(H6DO)-18, Oil Pressure Switch.>

Engine oil pressure (at oil temperature of 80°C (176°F)): Standard 100 kPa (1.0 kg/cm², 15 psi) or more (at 700 r/min) 500 kPa (5.1 kg/cm², 73 psi) or more (at 5,000 r/min)

7) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

# 7 Fuel Pressure

# A: INSPECTION

1) Remove the collector cover.

(1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A).   
(2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. 2) Release the fuel pressure. <Ref. to FU(H6DO)-95, RELEASING OF FUEL PRESSURE, PROCEDURE, Fuel.>   
3) Open the fuelfiller lid and remove the fuel filler cap.

![](images/07c71ced3f46887f2ff580d4727fbb05719b68dd2890b096bc545a5a5314948f.webp)

NOTE:

This operation is required to release the inner pressure of the fuel tank.   
4) Disconnect the fuel delivery tube from the fuel delivery pipe, and connect the fuel pressure gauge.

# CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill fuel.   
Catch the fuel from the tubes using a container or cloth. (1) Remove the clip (A) securing the fuel delivery tube.

(2) Attach ST to the fuel pipe assembly and push ST in the direction of arrow mark to disconnect the quick connector of the fuel delivery tube (B).

# ST 42099AE000 QUICK CONNECTOR RELEASE

![](images/5702e1921ffdad4d9971ca3ffad9810ac7a0afff893efe2da72826d17ce30d3f.webp)

(3) Connect the fuel pressure gauge with ST1 and ST2.

# CAUTION:

Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. I necessary, clean the seal surface of the pipe.   
Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

NOTE: ST1 is a SUBARU genuine part. ST1 42075AG690 FUEL HOSE ST2 18471AA000 FUEL PIPE ADAPTER

![](images/cc08417fe25b5f17fbdfa7dba7bba42aefb90b4cc5bb8fe50913371075f67179.webp)

A)Fuel pipe assembly side BFuel delivery tube side

5) Start the engine.

6) Check the fuel pressure after warming up the engine.

NOTE:

The fuel pressure gauge registers 10 to 20 kPa (0.1 to 0.2 kg/cm², 1 to 3 psi) higher than standard values during high-altitude operations. Check or replace the fuel pump and fuel delivery line if the fuel pressure is out of the standard.

Fuel pressure: Standard 340 — 400 kPa (3.5 — 4.1 kg/cm², 49.3 — 58 psi)

7) After inspection, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

# CAUTION:

Before removing the fuel pressure gauge, release the fuel pressure. Be careful not to spill fuel. Catch the fuel from hoses and tubes using a container or cloth. Check that there is no damage or dust on the quick connector. If necessary, clean the seal surface of the pipe. Make sure that the quick connector is securely connected.

NOTE:

When disconnecting the ST1 or fuel delivery tube, install the ST3 to the fuel pipe assembly or to ST2, and press the ST3 in the direction of arrow to disconnect the ST1 or the quick connector of the fuel delivery tube. ST1 42075AG690 FUEL HOSE   
ST2 18471AA000 FUEL PIPE ADAPTER   
ST3 42099AE000 QUICK CONNECTOR RELEASE

# Valve Clearance

A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

If engine oil is spilt onto the exhaust pipe, wipe it off with cloth to avoid emission of smoke or causing a fire.

NOTE:

Inspection of valve clearance should be performed while engine is cold.

1) Remove the collector cover.

(1) Carefully pull up the rear of collector cover at two positions (A).   
(2) Carefully pullup the front of collector cover at two positions (B) while moving it forward. 2) Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> Lift up the vehicle.   
Remove the under cover. <Ref. to El-29, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.   
Lower the vehicle.

![](images/94ef2219269feac41e3d5211968777d746c60d0a388a73e67afdf53d1fe60e69.webp)

(4) Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body and the air cleaner case (rear), and move it to the left side wheel apron.

# CAUTION:

Be careful not to allow the air intake boot to contact the air conditioner pipe.

![](images/719a8bb503b2086fff8c1f259f6d46fc443a180fe0a3c6a7c10cfe51f35f11d3.webp)

(5) Remove the air cleaner case. <Ref. to IN(H6DO)-8, REMOVAL, Air Cleaner Case.>

![](images/64f0cd2f73f5d8910326db20ad5a96c5808bc2e64ec176713a7eadf16b627c20.webp)

(7) Disconnect the connector of oil pressure switch.   
(8) Remove the ignition coil. <Ref. to IG(H6DO)-15, REMOVAL, Ignition Coil.> (9) Remove the rocker cover (RH). <Ref. to Mу(H6DO)-112, REMOVAL, Camshaft.> When inspecting valve clearances for #2, #4 and #6   
(1) Remove the battery. <Ref. to SC(H6DO)-58, REMOVAL, Battery.>   
(2) Disconnect the connector (A) and terminal (B) from the generator.   
(3) Disconnect the connector (C) and connector (D) from the A/C compressor. (4) Remove the harness cover (у) from the collector cover bracket.   
(5) Remove the clip (F) from the fuel pipe protector (LH).

![](images/45274cd46cfb8617015c55236dea7bd830d1262785a71c997b2205bf86959a23.webp)

(7) Disconnect the PCV hose from rocker cover (LH).

(8) Remove the fuel pipe protector (LH).

![](images/54cb223cd2d972c0b8b178316f1c4f79f79c822287e67c1a85be69d5ee0ba304.webp)

(9) Remove the ignition coil. <Ref. to IG(H6DO)-15, REMOVAL, Ignition Coil. (10) Remove the rocker cover (LH). <Ref. to Mу(H6DO)-112, REMOVAL, Camshaft.>

8) Turn the crankshaft clockwise until the camshaft is set to position shown in the figure.

![](images/f4237951b83854aa29c0734aed5bed59afacc5d1a582d99259af93248dbaaa35.webp)

ME-08175

Valve clearance (intake side) Valve clearance (exhaust side)

) Measure the clearance of intake valve and exhaust valve using thickness gauge (A).

NOTE:

Measure it within the range of ±30° from specified position shown in the figure.   
Insert a thickness gauge in a direction as horizontal as possible with respect to the valve lifter.

Valve clearance (inspection value): Intake 0.20+0.04 −0.06 mm (0.0079+0.0016 −0.0024 in) Exhaust 0.35±0.05 mm (0.0138±0.0020 in)

If the measured value is not within specification, take notes of the value in order to adjust the valve cle ance later on.

# B: ADJUSTMENT

1. INTAKE SIDE

1) Remove the engine from the vehicle. <Ref. to ME(H6DO)-42, REMOVAL, Engine Assembly.>

) Install the camshaft. <Ref. to ME(H6DO)-113, INSTALLATION, Camshaft.>

11) Install the timing chain assembly. <Ref. to ME(H6DO)-96, INSTALLATION, Timing Chain Assembly.> 1 Measure allvalve clearance again at this time. If the valve clearance is not within the adjustment value, repeat the procedure from step 3).

13) After adjustment, install the related parts in the reverse order of removal.

Zefer to “Camshaft”" when installing the rocker cover. <Ref. to ME(H6DO)-113, INSTALLATION, Camshaft.>

# 2  EXHAUST SIDE

CAUTION:

When reusing the V-belt, wipe off dust and water with cloth.   
Do not use the V-belt if there is any oil, grease or coolant on the belt.   
Be careful not to rub the belt end surface with bare hands; exposed core may cause injury.   
Wipe off any dust, oil and water on the groove of each pulley with cloth.

# CAUTION:

After installing the V-belt, check the V-belt tension and adjust it if necessary by loosening the nuts and tensioner pulley, then reinstall the belt.

3) Tighten the nut (A).

Tightening torque: 20 Nm (2.0 kgf-m, 14.8 ft-lb)

![](images/43bc009599623362b7d75dd19aae87015c560e13400006e2d1d850ff92fd82d0.webp)

)Crank pulley ( A/C compressor pulley D Tensioner pulley Generator pulley

5) Install the collector cover.

# C: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

Check and adjust the V-belt tension so that it is within the specified range. Using the belt with a tension out of the specified range may result in a fault such as the following: f the Vbelt tension is higher, unexpected force is generated at the power steering oil pump, generator and crankshaft bearing, causing abnormal noise due to abnormal wear of the bearing. If tension of the V-belt is too low, slipping of the V-belt and crank pulley occurs and crank pulley becomes abnormally hot by friction heat. If this condition repeatedly occurs, the V-belt may abnormally wear, causing abnormal noise, V-belt damage or crank pulley damage.

1) Replace the V-belt, if cracks, fraying or wear is found.   
2) Inspect the V-belt tension, and adjust if necessary.

V-belt tension (with sonic belt tension gauge): When installing new parts 1080 — 1230 N (110 — 125 kgf, 243 — 277 Ibf) 337 — 360 Hz (frequency) At inspection 570 — 720 N (58 — 73 kgf, 128 — 162 Ibf) 245 — 275 Hz (frequency)

NOTE:   
For inspection using sonic belt tension gauge, input of seting value may be needed. Belt distance (SPAN) between measuring point to pulley: 163 mm (6.42 in) V-belt weight (WEIGHT): 14.9 g (0.033 Ib)/m   
•V-belt width (WIDTH): 6 mm (0.24 in)/#R

# E: INSPECTION

# 1.CYLINDER HEAD

1) Make sure that there are no cracks or other damages. Perform visual check, and use liquid penetrant tester on the important sections. Check that there are no marks of gas leaking or water leaking on gasket installing surface.

2) Set the cylinder head on ST.   
ST 18250AA010 CYLINDER HEAD TABLE   
Check for warpage at mating surface between the cylinder block and cylinder head using a straight edge (л) and thickness gauge (B). If the warpage exceeds limit, replace the cylinder head.

Warping limit: 0.020 mm (0.0008 in)

Standard height of cylinder head: 124±0.05 mm (4.88±0.0020 in)

NOTE:   
Uneven torque for the cylinder head bolts can cause warpage. When reinstalling, pay special attention to the torque so as to tighten évenly.

Inspect the intake and exhaust valve seats, and correct the contact surfaces with a valve seat cutter if they are defective or when valve guides are replaced.

# Contacting width of valve seat W:

Standard Intake 1.0 mm (0.039 in) Exhaust 1.5 mm (0.059 in)

# 3. VALVE GUIDE

1 Check the clearance between valve guide and valve stem. The clearance can be checked by measuring the outer diameter of valve stem with a micrometer and the inner diameter of valve guide with a caliper gauge respectively.

Standard Intake 0.030 — 0.057 mm (0.0012 — 0.0022 in) Exhaust 0.040 — 0.067 mm (0.0016 — 0.0026 in)

) If the clearance between valve guide and valve stem exceeds the standard, replace the valve guide or valve itself, whichever shows the greater amount of wear or damage. See the following procedure for valve guide replacement.

Valve guide inner diameter: 5.500 — 5.512 mm (0.2165 — 0.2170 in)

Valve stem outer diameters: Intake 5.455 — 5.470 mm (0.2148 — 0.2154 in) Exhaust 5.445 — 5.460 mm (0.2144 — 0.2150 in) (1) Place the cylinder head on ST1 with the combustion chamber upward so that valve guides fit the holes in'ST1.

# E: INSPECTION

# 1. CYLINDER BLOCK

1 Visually check for cracks or damage. Use liquid penetrant tester on the important sections for checking.   
Check thát there are no marks of gas leaking or water leaking on gasket instaling surface.   
Check the oil passages for clogging.   
Inspect the cylinder block surface that mates with cylinder head for warping by using a straight edge. If the warpage exceeds limit, replace the cylinder block.

Warping limit: 0.020 mm (0.0008 in)

Standard height of cylinder block: 202 mm (7.95 in)

# CYLINDER AND PISTON

1) The cylinder bore size is stamped on the front upper face of the cylinder block.

Measurement should be performed at a temperature of 20°C (68°F).   
Standard sized pistons are classified into two grades, “A" and "“B". These grades should be used as guide lines in selecting á standard piston.

Standard diameter: A: 92.005 — 92.015 mm (3.6222 — 3.6226 in) B: 91.995 — 92.005 mm (3.6218 — 3.6222 in)

![](images/16b02b4778e8ef05a385edbcb818c37995c00aa3e986518ba90b6d621f86fcc3.webp)

(AMain journal size mark   
(BCylinder bore size mark   
(Cylinder block (RH) – (LH) combination mark 2) Measure inner diameter of each cylinder.   
Measure the inner diameter of each cylinder in both the thrust and piston pin directions at the heights as shown in the figure, using a cylinder bore gauge.

NOTE:

Measurement should be performed at a temperature of 20°C (68°F).

Calculate the cylindricality of cylinder liner by using the following formula

![](images/eeeb41e5b53b7dc817a67f66bb32b64235f9c063892d331fbc6878ec22345e78.webp)

![](images/9bed6391ac9c089b06446c91d4c8887c84ba78ecc40760ac7819950c7fd76318.webp)

Cylindricality: Limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in)   
Out-of-roundness: Limit 0.030 mm (0.0012 in)

![](images/202af7ef55255f8b61b6f1ccaab45e6f609bc239141e00b93b6a5da697e17fa0.webp)

When the piston is to be replaced due to general or cylinder wear, select a suitable sized piston by measúring the piston clearance.

# Cylinder Block

4) Measure outer diameter of each piston.

Measure the outer diameter of each piston at the height as shown in the figure. (Thrust direction) NOTE:

Measurement should be performed at a temperature of 20°C (68°F).

Piston grade point H: 37.3 mm (1.4685 in)

Piston outer diameter: Standard A: 92.005 — 92.015 mm (3.6222 — 3.6226 in) B: 91.995 — 92.005 mm (3.6218 — 3.6222 in) 0.25 mm (0.0098 in) oversize 92.245 — 92.265 mm (3.6317 — 3.6325 in) 0.50 mm (0.0197 in) oversize 92.495 — 92.515 mm (3.6415 — 3.6423 in)

![](images/3c985a979b2100f3353a6b691ce8f2a7403099bfcd14aeaef07cc2968882fbc8.webp)

5) Calculate the clearance between cylinder and piston.

NOTE:

Measurement should be performed at a temperature of 20°C (68°F).

Clearance between cylinder and piston at 20°C (68°F): Standard −0.010 — 0.010 mm (−0.0004 — 0.0004 in)

6 Boring and honing: (1) If any of the measured value of cylindricality, out-of-roundness or cylinder-to-piston clearance is out of standard or if there is any damage on the cylinder wall rebore it to replace with an oversize piston.

CAUTION:   
When any of the cylinders needs reboring, al other cylinders must be bored at the same time, and replaced with oversize pistons.

(2) If the cylinder inner diameter exceeds the limit after boring and honing, replace the cylinder block. NOTE: Immediately after reboring, the cylinder diameter may differ from its real diameter due to temperature rise. Thus, when measuring the cylinder diameter, wait until it has cooled to room temperature.

Cylinder inner diameter boring limit (diameter): To 92.515 mm (3.6717 in)

# Cylinder Block

# 3.  PISTON AND PISTON PIN

1) Check the piston and piston pin for damage, cracks or wear. Replace if faulty.   
2) Check the piston ring groove for wear or damage. Replace if faulty.   
3) Make sure that the piston pin can be inserted into the piston pin hole with a thumb at 20°C (68°F). Replace if faulty.

Clearance between piston pin hole and piston pin: Standard 0.004 — 0.008 mm (0.0002 — 0.0003 in)

![](images/0b400af88636d5eef21029a4800b97cda33918d5b51818409a03eb0fac6dbff8.webp)

4) Check the snap ring installation groove (A) on the piston for burr. If necessary, remove bur from the groove so that the piston pin can lightly move."

![](images/f6b6851495c8862340181a003dcf71cfca3232dc9c825bfda27e3b7cf3530611.webp)

5) Check the piston pin snap ring for distortion, cracks and wear.

# 4.  PISTON RING

1) If the piston ring is broken, damaged or worn, or if its tension is insufficient, or when the piston is replaced, réplace the piston ring with a new part of the same size as piston.

NOTE:

The top ring and second ring have the mark to determine the direction for installing. When installing the ring to piston, face marks to the top side.   
il ring consists of the upper rail, expander and lower rail When installing to the piston, be careful of the direction of each rail.

(A) Top ring (B) Second ring (C) Oil ring (a) Upper rail (b) Expander (c) Lower rail

) Squarely place the piston ring and oil ring in cylinder, and measure the piston ring gap with a thickness gauge.

![](images/42e794d3988b34602400ef866cad3ac08453ef45f266e5d346693cd4db0ca99e.webp)

![](images/f82d715b658803c37d2ee9eaccea0de86d8c41aa017f8e7593bedef05da459ad.webp)

3) Fit the piston ring straight into the piston ring groove, then measure the clearance between piston ring and piston ring groove with a thickness gauge.

NOTE: Before measuring the clearance, clean the piston ring groove and piston ring.

![](images/f5cd2b174cdee204bd4bc5983dab1affb94ea204ad4a1c43933d45e4b2e14fb1.webp)

![](images/ba5525f93b1c2dd0f578a9f88edc3647fadbce3ad2ec557134c289efda16559d.webp)

# 5. CONNECTING ROD

1) Replace the connecting rod, if the large or small end thrust surface is damaged. Check for bend or twist using a connecting rod aligner. Replace the connecting rod if the bend or twist exceeds the limit.

# Limit of bend or twist per 100 mm (3.94 in) in length: 0.10 mm (0.0039 in)

![](images/122526b2bf85ba4b55179e174b4dbb8b6f7b823961e9f76bba91a42cf398d24a.webp)

A) Thickness gauge (B Connecting rod

) Install the connecting rod with bearings attached to the crankshaft, and using a thickness gauge, measure the thrust clearance. If the thrust clearance exceeds the standard or uneven wear is found, replce the connecting rod.

Connecting rod thrust clearance: Standard 0.070 — 0.330 mm (0.0028 — 0.0130 in)

![](images/17fa940490b38f3b4f764b88e827b87df267010f60f0a627a15ee03ab56da6a0.webp)

4) Inspect the connecting rod bearing for scar, peeling, seizure, melting, wear, etc. Measure the oil clearance on each connecting rod bearing using plastigauge. If any oil clearance is not within the sndard, replace the deetive bearing with anew part of sandard sie or undersizeasnecessary.

Connecting rod oil clearance: Standard 0.016 — 0.043 mm (0.0006 — 0.0017 in)

![](images/ff3b44d845d79a999a4130a0b5408c2393204b93d7c8627627ad52f7a5cb012f.webp)

6) Inspect the bushing at connecting rod smal end, and replace with a new part if worn or damaged. 7 Measure the piston pin clearance at connecting rod smal end. If the measured value is not within the standard, replace it with a new part.

Clearance between piston pin and bushing: Standard 0 — 0.022 mm (0 — 0.0009 in)

![](images/82f4317f38b6fdb5fce61e228e37cfbc78c7b983962099869dddf42ab545f83e.webp)

![](images/0a5d0c405c8639df1f044e4dd09d1be92560b63c58cb0eaadbc2c86cad46a6f7.webp)

8) The replacement procedure for the connecting rod small end bushing is as follows. (1) Remove the bushing from connecting rod with ST and press. (2) Press the bushing with the ST after applying oil on the periphery of new bushing.   
ST 18350AA000 CONNECTING ROD BÜSHING REMOVуR AND INSTALLER (3) Make two 3 mm (0.12 in) holes in the pressed bushing to match the pre-manufactured holes on the connecting rod, then ream the inside of the bushing.   
(4) After completion of reaming, clean the bushing to remove chips.

![](images/653950263ce33cc2f036c4ea09837d5a7a33c6066fffe533eab0d8f684ab6479.webp)

# 6. CRANKSHAFT AND CRANKSHAFT BEARING

1 Clean the crankshaft completely, and check it for cracks using liquid penetrant tester. If defective, replace the crankshaft.   
Check the crankshaft for bend, and repair or replace if needed. If it exceeds the limit, correct or replace it. NOTE:   
If a suitable V-block is not available, using the #1 and #7 crankshaft bearings on cylinder block, position the crankshaft on cylinder block Then, measure the crankshaft bend using a dial gauge.

Crankshaft bend limit: 0.035 mm (0.0014 in)

![](images/83e650d694dc2837ce74083d065ccf6d0e0c22b7b4a0645da972e778f3247a5f.webp)

3) Inspect the crank journal and crank pin for wear. If they are not within the standard, replace the bearing with a suitable (undersize) one, and replace or grind to correct the crankshaft as necessary. When grinding the crank journal or crank pin, finish them to the specified dimensions according to the undersize bearing to be used.

Crank pin: Out-of-roundness Limit 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) Cylindricality Limit 0.006 mm (0.0002 in) Grinding limit (dia.) To 51.734 mm (2.0368 in)

Crank journal: Out-of-roundness Limit 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) Cylindricality Limit 0.006 mm (0.0002 in) Grinding limit (dia.) Тo 63.742 mm (2.5095 in)

![](images/38607fb87a1a0045d50d2cb5b3bb57a1485eb95382f2532d8748fba2c4fd74cc.webp)

![](images/c02b9e4809c3aa141ae92eeb0ef7cff53b36d8100103275b52c35c0b7aef7895.webp)

# ME(H6DO)-164

# Cylinder Block

4) Use a thickness gauge to measure the thrust clearance of crankshaft at center bearing. If clearance exceeds the standard, replace the bearing.

Crankshaft thrust clearance: Standard 0.040 — 0.212 mm (0.0016 — 0.0083 in)

![](images/74c10b96608f7d5a23aa20873c37b4e4c5fd6d5684b9e59245dd265fa8da6144.webp)

5) Inspect individual crankshaft bearings for signs of flaking, seizure, melting and wear. ) Measure the oil clearance on each crankshaft bearing using plastigauge. If the measured value is out of standard, replace the defective bearing with an undersize one, and replace or grind to correct the crankshaft as necessary.

Crankshaft oil clearance: Standard 0.010 — 0.030 mm (0.0004 — 0.0012 in)
