# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Detect instantaneous open in ignition switch input circuit to ECM.   
Judge as NG if out of specification.

# 2. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION

ECM monitors the voltage of the ignition switch input circuit. Judge as ignition switch ON when the voltage is the specified value or more.

# 3. EXECUTION CONDITION

![](images/373aec6146f9b2331bc087d553bc01610a1cd16268f3e296a117e9fa7a3ec77e.webp)

# 4.GENERAL DRIVING CYCLE

Perform the diagnosis continuously after the enable conditions have been established.

# 5. DIAGNOSTIC METHOD

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established within the predetermined time. Judgment Value

![](images/7e771b7e408762c92dfd58540dcec776d1c6d40727918d5d46b6806c7d157148.webp)

Time Needed for Diagnosis: 5000 ms Malfunction Indicator Light Illumination: Illuminates as soon as a malfunction occurs.

# GK:DTC P2610 ECM/PCM ENGINE OFF TIMER PERFORMANCE

# DTC DETECTING CONDITION:

Detected when two consecutive driving cycles with fault occur.

# CAUTION:

After servicing or replacing faulty parts, perform Clear Memory Mode <Ref, to EN(H6DO)(diag)-87, OPERATION, Clear Memory ode, and Inspectin Mode Ref. o EN(H6DO(diag-71, PROCEDURE Inspection Mode.>.

![](images/2d05018c1dc2d0646cb1f5c7b54a7a88cf930e488fb933b2f859ca78491f457d.webp)

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

Detect malfunction of soaking timer IC by the five diagnoses below.

![](images/33f14ef6ab0bc8427b8580e619c00bdacf14a24f109e764bb795fb43ed492994.webp)

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

![](images/8ae02a91a941a8af6eb6b6c63db2143ca6896885c08c85cb18f9492477fa734d.webp)  
This is an example of ELCM monitor execution at soak time of 5 hours.

![](images/30b3e780e2c708582e32ade135cf723ff0074106a238eca3df77a5883f3a2003.webp)  
This is an example of ELCM monitor execution at soak time of 9.5 hours.

# 2. COMPONENT DESCRIPTION

The soaking timer IC is built into the ECM.

# 3.  EXECUTION CONDITION

![](images/d8b2326375248a4a310fc76405cde3b67f47eaba15b99f963db17f62db6eece1.webp)

# 4.GENERAL DRIVING CYCLE

Perform the diagnosis only once when the ignition switch is OFF and when the ignition switch is ON after the soaking of one hour or móre.

# 5.  DIAGNOSTIC METHOD

# <Timer diagnosis>

Start the count up operation of counters in ECM and in soaking timer IC when the engine is started. Judge as timer malfunction if the difference between the counter in ECM and counter in soaking timer IC exceeds the allowable limit when the ignition switch is OFF.

![](images/05c646eaf4e4268696119f7d8dc90a08776622dd1a9085924f05e58052aee059.webp)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/a2d4c170e8fcfbd6440c9b6c8baa482790da62c66d91a0962ddb8a357ff3c1ef.webp)

# <Full count diagnosis>

Reset the counter in soaking timer IC and start the count up operation.   
Judge as full count diagnosis malfunction if counter in soaking timer IC is not \$3FF (1023 count) after 4 seconds.

![](images/6853b6d563b5ae24c5a3565a123cb7c33b042311865b9ca0ff457476fe564746.webp)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/eeb357f508694701bf349f74d22a3eb69df5d39f7c4b2d0f8fd72a6eea439566.webp)

# <Soaking timer IC setting diagnosis>

When setting the activation setting time to soaking timer IC, compare the writing value to soaking timer IC with read out value. Judge as malfunction if the values do not match 3 times in a row.

![](images/2b5a2dabcf812320a7d6bf8382f7b9799bf00a0a591ed9515c57ebae58f1c3dd.webp)

EN-10766

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/c436c4afa6e035bd14515d3d7a7d928090df6dd5fa12deab28319f5c32f00b1f.webp)

# <Timer diagnosis (during soaking)>

Wake-up at the predetermined interval until 5 or 7 or 9.5 hours have passed after the ignition switch is OFF, and compare the counter in soaking timer IC with the counter in ECM.

Judge as malfunction if the counter in soaking timer IC is counted up to maximum value (1023 count) when the counter in ECM is 1636 ms, or if the counter in soaking timer I is not counted up to maximum value (1023 count) when the counter in ECM is 2456 ms.

![](images/900d247b20f08ba47425d0ff78087ee55ed4e0f56bcde0ea67b9dd38ddd95ff3.webp)

# Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) ENGINE (DIAGNOSTICS)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/8ad0ee380b46e7197e8d96a0c0103311ef333ca936cb7ef7f1de1e7cca9504b6.webp)

# <Wake-up diagnosis>

Store the number of wake-up activation when the ECM wakes up by the soaking timer IC. Next time when the ignition switch is ON, if the number of wake-up activation does not reach the predetermined value even though the counter in soaking timer IC operates 1 hour or more, judge as wake-up malfunction.

![](images/d1459594c0ce431cca34cd5e894bea7939c88802a928ea6cc551622652b29327.webp)

Judge as NG when the following conditions are established. Judgment Value

![](images/4afa8502f0a82f08211084764a9442c4b0317f4395d17e4c6b906f9753b81bea.webp)

Time Needed for Diagnosis: Approx. 5 — 9.5 hours   
Malfunction Indicator Light illumination: Illuminates when malfunction occurs in 2 continuous driving cycles.

This service manual has been prepared to provide SUBARU service personnel with the necessary information and data for the correct maintenance and repair of SUBARU vehicles.

This manual includes the procedures for maintenance, disassembling, reassembling, inspection and adjustment of components and diagnostics for guidance of experienced mechanics.

Please peruse and utilize this manual fully to ensure complete repair work for satisfying our customers by keeping their vehicle in optimum condition. When replacement of parts during repair work is needed, be sure to use SÜBARU genuine parts.

All information, illustration and specifications contained in this manual are based on the latest product information available at the time of publication approval.

# B: CAUTION

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation or disassembly.   
Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.

Before removal, installtion or disassembly, be sure to clarify the failure. Avoid unnecessary removal, installation, disassembly and replacement.

Use SUBARU genuine fluid, grease etc. or equivalent. Do not mix fluid, grease, etc. of different grades or manufacturers.

Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Place shop jacks or rigid racks at the specified points.

Apply grease onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation.

Before installing O-rings or snap rings, apply suffcient amount of grease to avoid damage and deformation.

Before securing a part in a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocks, aluminum plate or cloth between the part and the vise.

Before disconnecting electrical connectors, be sure to disconnect the negative terminal from battery.

Make sure that the door open alarm will not sound when the door is opened in the “P" range after the ignition switch is turned to OFF.

If the door open alarm sounds, check if the rod COMPL is inserted in the wrong direction.

17) Remove the bolts from ST (SPECIAL TOOL” FB).

![](images/3780bdcabe04fabfacec485be348b50f16bd1a13d962772573b897bbfda2505e.webp)

18) Remove the bolt and nut to remove ST (SPECIAL TOOL FB).

![](images/f5480e99f6a63e4c431bacba1697d045211294b90cf1497409c1ed9d654f57bd.webp)

19) Temporarily attach the front engine mounting with bolts.

![](images/6b487177e7afe560cad94e6e9df0be2934d15c78be1008c1631ebbd5e8129743.webp)

20) Install the bolt and nut to the front engine mounting.

![](images/9499f150216ac918b1d46c713e1fde2334f856014d502c88f59b027c10b25c5b.webp)

21) Tighten the bolts and nuts of front engine mounting.

Tightening torque: T1: 25 Nm (2.5 kgf-m, 18.4 ft-lb) T2: 45 Nm (4.6 kgf-m, 33.2 ft-lb)

![](images/e6f7e41b6c8b871c3face28564859cdc2108dcd97b285aa4a098e2b8658d2a78.webp)

ST2 18360AA040 HANGER

![](images/aad168dc47129fbc046f11a05ffb50c5a8e7e0250d69599d467a93b725977b33.webp)

![](images/ea99a191b2037cc9fbce18e71d2271f6faa1a97398607395be88df43bb53387d.webp)

29) Make sure the gears can be shifted acurately into each gear.

# CVT(TR580)-23

# C: CAUTION

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation or disassembly Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.

Do not place the valve cover with it inner side facing up until itis installd, to prevent intrusion of foreign natter into the control valve body.

Before removal, installtion or disassembly, be sure to clarify the failure. Avoid unnecessary removal, installation, disassembly and replacement.

When disassembling the case and otherlight alloy parts, use a plastic hammer to force it apart. Do not pry apart with screwdrivers or other tools.

Vehicle components are extremely hot after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

Use SUBARU genuine CVTF and recommended grease. Do not mix CVTF, grease etc. of different grades r manufacturers.

Be sure to tighten bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Apply CVTF onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation.

Replace deformed or damaged snap rings with new parts

Before installing O-rings or oil seals, apply sufficient amount of CVTF or gear oil to appropriate locations n order to avoid damage and deformation.

Be careful not to incorrectly instal or fail to instal O-rings, snap rings and other such parts.

:Before securing a part on a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocks, aluminum plate, or cloth between the part and the vise.

Avoid damaging the mating surface of the case.

Before applying liquid gasket, completely remove the old liquid gasket.

After removing the sensors, breather hose and plugs, plug the holes to avoid foreign materials intruding as lecessary.

During disassembly or assembly, be sure to use nylon gloves or paper towels. Do not use cloth gloves or vaste cloth.

Be careful of handing the oil seal, O-ring and gasket. If the contact surface of them is damaged, oil leakage may occur.

When pressing-in the oil seal, make sure that the oil sealip portion and outer surface are not damaged or tilted.

When replacing the taper roller bearing, replace the outer race and inner race as a set.

When replacing the hypoid gear, replace the hypoid gear and drive pinion shaft as a set.

Replace the bolts if the seating surface or the thread surface is excessively rusted.

# CVT(TR580)-42

# Differential Gear Oil

# A: INSPECTION

Check that there is no leakage of differential gear oil from the converter case.

# B: ADJUSTMENT

NOTE:

Immediately after removing the overflow drain plug, remaining gear oil (approx. 8 cc) may come out of the overflow pipe. This is not included in the specified amount. When removing the overflow drain plug, make sure the gear oil flows out of the overflow drain plug hole by filling with gear oil.

1 Lift up the vehicle.   
2 Remove the under cover - front.   
Remove the filler plug.

# AWD ON/OFF Switching Mode A: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Follow the messages displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor when working Perform as necessary in 'FWD mode.   
When switched to FWD, AWD light illuminates.

# B: PROCEDURE

CAUTION:

Do not turn the power of the Subaru Select Monitor OFF during work, and do not disconnect the data link connector.

On completing the work in FWD, switch back in AWD.

1) Shift the select lever to “P” range.   
2) Connect the Subaru Select Monitor to data link connector.   
3) Turn the ignition to ON. (For model with push button ignition switch, press the push button ignition switch twice without depressing brake pedal.)   
4) Turn off allswitches causing an electrical load, such as headlights, A/C, seat heater and rear defogger. 5) Select «DЙБЗОПУЙУе in the «SФБТФе screen of Subaru Select Monitor.   
6 On «Vehicle УЕМЕГФЙПОе display, input the vehicle information and select «CПОЖЙТНЕДе.   
7 On «Main Menu display, select Each System.   
On «Select SЩУФЕНе display, select «Transmission Control SЩУФЕНе.   
On «Select FХОГФЙПОе display, select «Work SХРРПТФе.   
10) Select «AWD ON/OFF switching НПДЕе in the «Work SХРРПТФе screen.   
11 Follow the messages displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor screen when working.   
Switching completes successfuly if any of the following messages is displayed.   
When switching from AWD to FWD: «Switched to FF.To return to AWD, perform basic mode БЗБЙО.е

When switching from FWD to AWD: «Switched to AWD. To return to FF, perform basic mode БЗБЙО.е

NOTE:

Ifcommunication error occurs during switching mode, start in the "AWD ON/OFF switching mode" again. Ifoperation is interrupted before the successful end message is displayed, perform the «AWD ON/OFF switching НПДЕе from the beginning until confirming the operation is successfully ended. If this mode fails to complete successfully, the cause is as follows.

Select lever is not in "P" range.   
Engine is running.   
For detailed operation procedures, refer to "Application help".

# CVT(TR580)-47

# Road Test

# A: INSPECTION

1. GENERAL PRECAUTION

Road tests should be conducted to properly diagnose the condition of CVT.

CAUTION: Always observe the local traffic laws when performing the test.

# 2. D RANGE SHIFT FUNCTION

Make sure that the engine speed is 1,100 — 1,400 r/min while driving on the level road at 50 km/h (31 MPH) after accelerating from halting up to 1/4 of accelerator opening angl. Then stop the vehicle. Check normal gear change has occurred while the vehicle speed changes from à constant speed to zero.

# 3. KICK-DOWN FUNCTION

Check if engine speed wil rise by operating the accelerator opening angle to the fullfrom a constant speed of 50 km/h (31 MPH) or more.

# 4. ENGINE BRAKE OPERATION

Drive in “6th speed of manual mode" [70 — 80 km/h (43— 50 MPH)], and shift down from 6th to 5th. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "6" "5" At the same time, check the engine brake in 5th gear. Drive in "5th speed of manual mode" [60 —70 km/h (37—43 MPH)], and shift down from 5th to 4th.Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "5" "4" At the same time, check the engine brake in 4th gear. Drive in "4th speed of manual mode [50—60 km/h (31—37 MPH)], and shift down from 4th to 3rd.Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "4" "". At the same time, check the engine brake in 3rd gear. Drive in "3rd speed of manual mode" [40 —50 km/h (25—31 MPH)], and shift down from 3rd to 2nd. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches “3" → "2". At the same time, check the engine brake in 2nd gear.   
Drive in "2nd speed of manual mode” [20 — 30 km/h (12— 19 MPH)], and shift down from 2nd to 1st. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "2"  "1" At the same time, check the engine brake in 1st gear.

# 5. LOCK-UP FUNCTION

When the accelerator is lightly depressed while driving on a flat road in “D" range, check that rpm does not change abruptly.

# 6. P RANGE OPERATION

Stop the vehicle on an uphill grade of 5% or more and shift to the "P" range and apply the parking brake Check that the vehicle does not move when the parking brake is released.

# 7.  NOISE AND VIBRATION

Check for noise and vibration during driving at a constant speed, accelerating, decelerating and manual shiff operation.

# 8. OIL LEAKAGE

After the driving test, inspect for leakage of CVTF and differential gear oil from the transmission body.

# 6 Stall Test

# A: INSPECTION

CAUTION: Make sure no other person is around the vehicle during stall test measurement.

NOTE:

Stalltest is extremely important in diagnosing the condition of CVT and engine. The test is necessary to measure the engine stall speeds inR" and " range.

Purposes of the stall test:

Operational check of forward clutch and reverse brake   
Operational check of the torque converter assembly   
Engine performance check   
1) Place wheel chocks at the front and rear of all wheels and engage the parking brake.   
Turn the A/C OFF.   
Using the Subaru Select Monitor, check if the throttle valve operates when you depress the accelerator pedal REf to EN(H4DO(di)-59, DISPLAY OF ENGINE FREEZE FRAME DATA, OPERATION, SUbaru Select Monitor.>   
Check the engine oil level. <Ref. to LU(H4DO)-8, Engine Oil.>   
Check the coolant level. <Ref. to CO(H4DO)-15, Engine Coolant.>   
6) Adjust the CVTF level. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-39, ADJUSTMENT, CVTF.>   
7 Increase the CVTF temperature to 60 — 80°C (140 —176°F) with the engine running and the select lever shifted to "N or "P" range.   
Shit he select lever to D" range.   
Depress the accelerator pedal to the full while fully depressing the foot brake pedal with your left foot. 1 When the engine speed stabilizes, quickly record the engine speed and release accelerator pedal. Shift thé select lever to “N” range. Let the engine idle for one minüte or more to cool it down.

11) Shift to “R” range and perform the same stall test.

NOTE:

Do not perform a stalltest for over 5 seconds at a time. (From closed throttle, full open throttle to stall speed reading.) Failure to follow this instruction will cause the engine oil and CTF to deteriorate and the clutch and brake to be adversely affected.   
Be sure to cool down the engine for at least one minute after each stall test with the select lever set in the "P" or "N" range and with the idle speed of 1,200 r/min or less.   
If the stall speed is higher than the specified range, attempt to finish the stall test in as short a time as possible, in order to prevent the CVT from sustaining damage.

Stall speed standard: D rànge: 1,900 — 2,700 r/min R range: 1,800 — 2,600 r/min

# CVT(TR580)-49

# 7Time Lag Test

# A: INSPECTION

NOTE:

When the select lever is shifted while the engine is idling, there willbe a certain time elapse or lag before shock is felt. This symptom helps to check the condition of forward clutch and reverse brake.

Perform the test at normal operation CVTF temperature of 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F).   
Be sure to allow one minute or more interval between tests.   
Make three measurements and take the average value.   
1 Apply the parking brake.   
2 Start the engine. Check the idle speed. (A/C OFF)   
) Shift the select lever from "N" to "D" range. Using a stop watch, measure the time elapsed from shifting the léver until the shock is felt.

# Time lag standard:

1.5 seconds or less

If “N” → “D” time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressure) is too low.   
Forward clutch worn   
Forward clutch piston malfunction   
Control valve body malfunction   
Learning incomplete   
4) In the same manner, measure the time lag when shifting from “N” range to “R” range.

Time lag standard: 1.5 seconds or less

If “N” → “R" time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressure) is too low. Reverse brake worn   
Reverse brake piston malfunction   
Control valve body malfunction   
Learning incompléte

And then release the accelerator pedl. Shift the select lever to “N" range. Let the engine idle for one minute or more to cool it down.

NOTE:

Do not continue the stalltest for 5 seconds or more at a time (from fully closed throttle, fully open throtle to secondary pressure (line pressure) reading). Failure to follow this instrction will cause the engine oil and CVTF to deteriorate and the clutch and brake to be adversely affected.

After performing the secondary pressure line pressure) test, be sure to cool down the engine for at leas one minute with the select lever set in “P” or “N” range and with the idle speed at 1,200 r/min or less.

Under each condition, check that the measured pressure matches almost total with actual secondary pressure.

When both measured pressure and actual secondary pressure are out of specification, judge as contro valve malfunction.

The value at stallis for reference because the pressure changes under different conditions or circumstances.

The value at idling is steady because it is not affected by any condition or circumstance.

When the engine is started with the select lever in the “P" range and the secondary pressure at idling is measured without shifting the select lever, the value may be higher than the standard. Shift the select lever to the “D” or “R” range, then measure the value.

# 11.Transmission Mounting System

# A: REMOVAL

1.  TRANSMISSION REAR CROSSMEMBER AND REAR CUSHION RUBBER

1) Disconnect the ground cable from battery. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> NOTE:

For model with battery sensor, disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor.   
2 Lift up the vehicle.

3) Remove the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-12, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.>   
4) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/b845d162b18335e6d2b36bdd1a4f8f8ddf21c56274c937faa573d9b02116f407.webp)

) Set the transmission jack under the transmission. Make sure that the support plate of transmission jack does not touch the oil pán.   
6) Remove the transmission rear crossmember.

![](images/7ac164bb2d240dcc6420970cd7ad580b0af701719c880538df209a332f0afe94.webp)

7) Remove the rear cushion rubber.

![](images/eeebfe2f3d8115a51ee7f2231cde6ab1fc362a66f397b02577074217c337d90a.webp)

# 2.  MAIN MOUNTING BRACKET & MAIN CUSHION RUBBER

Refer to “MECHANICAL (H4DO)" for removal procedures. <Ref. to ME(H4DO)-69, MAIN MOUNTINC BRACKET & MAIN CUSHION RUBBER, REMOVAL, Engine MoUntiNg.

# B: INSTALLATION

# 1. TRANSMISSION REAR CROSSMEMBER AND REAR CUSHION RUBBER

1) Attach the rear cushion rubber to the transmission.

Tightening torque: 40 NбН (4.1 kgf-m, 29.5 ft-lb) 2) Install the crossmember.

Tightening torque: T1: 35 NбН (3.6 kgf-m, 25.8 ft-lb) T2: 75 Nm (7.6 kgf-m, 55.3 ft-lb)

![](images/45d0e578ef01871ad3517a4e352794fc4e84f16377ff6e0c2434ce52db401710.webp)

3) Remove the transmission jack.   
4) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 NбН (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

5) Install the center exhaust pipe. <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-13, INSTALLATION, Center Exhaust Pipe.

# 13.Differential Side Retainer Oil Seal

# A: INSPECTION

Check for leakage of gear oil from differential side retainer oil seal part. If there is an oil leak, inspect the front drive shaft and replace the oil seal.

CAUTION:

•Immediately after the vehicle has been running or after idling for a long time, the differential gear oil will be hot. Be careful not to burn yourself. Be careful not to spillthe differentiál gear oil on exhaust pipe to prevent it from emitting smoke or fire. If differential gear oil is spilled on the exhaust pipe, wipe it off completely.

1) Lift up the vehicle, and remove the front wheels.   
After pulling off the cotter pin and removing the castle nut, use a puller to remove the tie-rod end.

(ACotter pin (BTie-rod end (Castle nut

8 Remove the stabilizer link. <Ref. to FS-34, REMOVAL, Front Stabilizer.> Disconnect the balljoint and housing. 10) Pull out the front drive shaft from transmission using a crowbar.

Oil seal has an identification mark (R, L. When installing oil seals, do not confuse the left and right.

specmcation: Approx. 0.8 V   
6 Check "secondary pressure sensor voltage" with engine stopped and ignition switch turned on by using   
Subaru Select Monitor. <Ref. to CVT(diag)-18, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.>

Specification: Approx. 0.5 V

# 19.Oil Pan and Strainer

A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Directly after the vehicle has been running or the engine has been idling for a long time, the CVTF is hot. Be careful not to burn yourself.   
Be careful not to spil CVTF on the exhaust pipe to prevent it from emitting smoke or causing a fire. If the CVTF adheres, wipe it off completely.

1) Lift up the vehicle.   
2 Remove the under cover - front.   
3) Clean the transmission exterior.   
4 Remove the CVTF drain plug to drain CVTF.   
5 Remove the oil pan.

# CAUTION:

Be careful not to allow foreign matter such as dust or dirt to enter the oil pan.

![](images/c0bcfd3100567c4c40ef6177934962f4f4472f37227740a01fc6136240ee8919.webp)

6) Remove the magnet.   
7) Remove the oil strainer.

![](images/aea3996b6795d0a00836eef594206315d27cde17ad13f450ce567bdcffb8eb13.webp)

CVT00633

8) Remove the O-ring from oil strainer.

![](images/5f6b639a9e75442b5014f077f366ebaddde8be1fbd19801f8e86e0b9896c4db4.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Clean the mating surface of oil pan and transmission case.   
) Install the O-rings.

NOTE: •Use new O-rings. Apply CVTF to the O-rings. 3) Install the oil strainer.

Tightening torque: 9 NбН (0.9 kgf-m, 6.6 ft-lb)

4) Clean the magnet.   
5) Attach the magnet at the specified position of the oil pan.   
6) Apply liquid gasket all around the oil pan mating surface seamlessly.

Liquid gasket: THRуE BOND 1217B (Part No. K0877YA020) or equivalent

![](images/0742b73de1a8e521b80b751978771820e755b31b66c6a6c6c3978215032c56dd.webp)

7 Instal the oil pan by equally tightening the bolts.

Tightening torque: 5 Nm (0.5 kgf-m, 3.7 ft-lb)   
8) Install the under cover - front.   
9) Refill CVTF and adjust the level. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-40, REPLACEMENT, CVTF.>

# C: INSPECTION

Check each part for damage or dust.   
Check oil strainer for clogging.

# DIAGNOSIS:

It does not switch to X mode.

# CAUTION:

Note that the system performs the following controls when switching to X mode.

If the ignition switch is in ON position before starting engine, switching to X mode is not available.

Replace any faulty CVTF cooler hoses, CVTF cooler pipes and clamps found in the inspection below.

1) Check that there are no CVTF or engine coolant leaks from the connections.

# 30.Torque Converter Assembly

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-64, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
2) Pull out the torque converter assembly horizontally.

CAUTION: Do not scratch the inside of engaging parts.

![](images/63acf70e77cc1aa488bad32d320337704eddad5e682c0e5d4b1327ab5212dd7e.webp)

3) Remove the O-ring from the input shaft.

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the O-ring to the input shaft.

NOTE: •Use new O-rings. Apply CVTF to the O-rings.

While holding the torque converter assembly by hand, carefully install t into the torque converter case.

NOTE:

Apply CVTF to the oil seal lip.   
Do not damage the oil seal and O-ring.

Engage the splines while gently rotating the torque converter assembly by hand, and securely insert the assembly. 4) Measure depth “A”, from converter case end surface to drive plate contacting surface.

Standard (reference): 6.8 mm (0.268 in) or less

![](images/04cc96fb45e00df0363f4edac99e4f97a3bb5e17bc5e0dfa8327031ce1b257da.webp)

5) Install the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-80, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmission Assembly.

# C: INSPECTION

Check the protrusion of torque converter center (front boss) is not deformed or damaged.   
Check the ring gear and exterior for break or damage.

# 31.Preparation for Overhaul

A: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Before disassembling and assembling the transmission, follow the following procedures to prepare.

# B: PROCEDURE

1) Clean the transmission exterior. 2) Attach the ST on the transmission assembly. ST 18632AA000 STAND ASSY

![](images/6086a1a04f0159dcea8247d361c867530a95be545635629f79b7445a3cf27b3a.webp)

3) Remove the torque converter assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-199, Torque Converter Assembly.:   
4) Remove the transmission case cover on the transmission upper side.

NOTE: Install using the following tightening torque.

Tightening torque: 8 №m (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)

![](images/6c4d8a897666f88ca2711bde32a119f9b2b567605a8caa6ebea51d2d57b2572c.webp)

5) Place the transmission assembly on end.

6When completely overhauling the transmission, refil approx. 10 L (2.6 US qt, 8.8 Imp qt) of CVTF through the transmission right side plug, and install the plug. Then, install the transmission case cover.

# CAUTION:

Always use specified CVTF. Using other fluid will cause malfunction. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-4, HY DRAULIC CONTROL AND LUBRICATION, SPECIFICATION, GeNRal DeSCriPiON.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 50 NбН (5.1 kgf-m, 36.9 ft-lb)

![](images/25f9e66a8ac6e507ce94225a5186c8f6cf063a38d0f1a3cc06d402b43b62c868.webp)

# 32.Extension Case

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-64, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
) Remove the extension case and transmission hanger.

NOTE: The total number of extension case mounting bolts is 13.

![](images/81d53029906642cbbfcb0397834785baa06f69be11e91497975435c57f9e9c36.webp)

1) Clean the mating surface of extension case and transmission case.   
Select the transfer drive gear shim. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-262, ADJUSTMENT, Reduction Drive Gear.   
) Select the transfer driven gear shim. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-218, ADJUSTMENT, Transfer Clutch.> 4) Attach the selected transfer drive gear shim to extension case with vaseline.   
5) Attach the selected transfer driven gear shim to extension case with vaseline.   
6) Install the O-ring to the transmission case.

# NOTE:

•Use new O-rings.   
Apply CVTF to the O-rings.

9) Install the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-80, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmissior Assembly.>

# C: DISASSEMBLY

1) Remove the dust cover from extension case.   
2) Remove the extension case oil seal from the extension case. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-101, REPLACEMENT, Differential Side Retainer Oil Seal.>   
3) Remove all plugs.

# D: ASSEMBLY

1) Press-fit the dust cover into extension case.   
2) Install the extension case oil seal to extension case. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-101, REPLACEMENT, Differential Side Retainer Oil Seal.>   
3) Install al plugs.

NOTE:

Use a new O-ring or a gasket.   
Apply CVTF to the O-rings.

Check there is no leak of CVTF from the joint between extension case and transmission case.

NOTE:

When replacing the extension case, select the transfer drive gear shim and transfer driven gear shim. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-262, ADJUSTMENT, Reduction Drive Gear.> <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-218, ADJUSTMENT, Transfer Clutch.>

# E: INSPECTION

Inspect the drive plate facing for wear and damage.   
Driven plate for discoloration (burned color)   
Make sure the snap ring is not worn and the return spring has no permanent distortion, damage, or defor mation.   
Check the lip seal for damage.   
Inspect the extension end play, and adjust it to within the standard value. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-218, ADJUSTMENT, Transfer Clutch.>   
1) Before measuring clearance “A" between snap ring and driven plate, place same thickness shims on both sides to prevent the plate from tilting.

When clearance “A" exceeds the limit for use, replace the drive plate and driven plate as a set, and select the pressure plate within the initial specified value.

Initial standard: 0.7 — 1.1 mm (0.028 — 0.043 in)

Limit thickness: 1.45 mm (0.057 in)

![](images/f02261c2624beab2f572d69627c3581639f823d1d987943fad0134b4ad046518.webp)

3) Check for tight corner braking phenomenon when the vehicle is moved forward with the steering fully turned. If tight corner braking occurs, perform the following procedures.

(1) With the steering wheel held at full turned position, drive the vehicle in "D" range and with vehicle speed at approx. 5 km/h (3 MPH) in both clockwise and counterclockwise directions for approx. ten times each, while repeating acceleratión and braking intermittently. () If the tight corner braking phenomenon stil persists, drive the vehicle again in a circle for several laps.

ST 499575400 GAUGE

T mm = A - B- 1.0

T: Moving distance of reduction drive gear   
A: Depth from the ST upper face to the reduction drive gear end surface B: Depth from the ST upper face to the reduction drive gear end surface 1.0 mm (0.039 in): Thickness of spring retainer

Ref. to CVT(TR580)-141, INSTALLATION, Control Valve Body. 28) Install the air breather hose. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-195, INSTALLATION, Air Breather Hose. 29 Install the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-80, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>

# C: INSPECTION

Check the surface of primary and secondary pulley cones for damage or wear.   
Check the primary and secondary pulley for damage.   
Check the bearing for seizure or wear.   
Apply CVTF to bearing and rotate the bearing to check for noise or dragging etc.

# D: ADJUSTMENT

# 1 procedure In replacement of primary And secondary pulley, or in rePLACEMENT OF PRIMARY PULLEY, SECONDARY PULLEY AND VARIATOR CHAIN

1) Measure depth “Lp" from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.   
ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/f4cf1f751cd5efb05c7fef70629fbe8d84434b15875fcfaa4151b54b7423c54a.webp)

Measure the depth “Ls" from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.

![](images/2ccc8ce62c99c9629ba0ff99e06ea6cce8233b759621e3852a19cd68044f1a51.webp)

3) Calculate the following formula.   
Calculation formula:   
T (mm) = B − A + Lp − Ls − 28.602   
[T (in) = B - A + Lp − Ls -1.126]   
T: Pulley alignment   
A: Specified primary pulley dimension   
B: Specified secondary pulley dimension   
Lp: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface Ls: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface 28.602 mm (1.126 in): Constant

![](images/f6dca7096f8805410b6adbbe4ddd5de650b4c1b69f6786a4c50db86a8480ab69.webp)

4) Select one to two shims so that the total thickness meets the value obtained from step 3).

![](images/b3cb543f9a547dcd3a4b71ee6979f632f4a4b0065ef42240f51ac253162ff68b.webp)

# 2. PROCEDURE WHEN REPLACING ONLY DRIVE PINION RETAINER OR REVERSE BRAKE

1) Clean the mating surface of current drive pinion retainer and converter case. Measure and record the shim thickness that is attached on the current reverse brake housing. Using the current drive pinion retainer, measure depth "Lp1" from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.

ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/c892cca6aef415e73000d95c84d7b7785ac6b3ea17137d465d52ad95bc341045.webp)

4) Using the current drive pinion retainer or current reverse brake housing, measure the depth “Ls1" from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average. ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/8860caa77209487f1e91409aece08e00ebb644507b923c92f0bcb6d5d70363e4.webp)

5) Calculate the “LD1” using the following formula and record it.   
Calculation formula:   
LD1 mm (in) = Ls1 − Lp1   
LD1: Height from the primary pulley bearing catch surface to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Lp1: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface   
Ls1: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface   
Using the new drive pinion retainer or new reverse brake housing, measure the depth “Lp2" from the S upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average. ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/a04c2b345172375786471d29d8ee27435a6bb5f38be7ed94797b80834447a8cf.webp)

# Primary Pulley and Secondary Pulley

7 Using the new drive pinion retainer or new reverse brake housing, measure the depth “Ls2" from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average. ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/cab87dcb98ee60ad9a8daa7ae6c4e870631edd6bef8bc9a73e4c89a020bde88b.webp)

8) Calculate the “LD2” using the following formula and record it.   
Calculation formula:   
LD2 mm (in) = Ls2 − Lp2   
LD2: Height from the primary pulley bearing catch surface to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Lp2: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface   
Ls2: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Calculate the recorded values of "“LD1" and “LD2" to obtain the positive number to select the shims. Calculation formula: T1 mm (in) = LD1 − LD2 or T2 mm (in) = LD2 – LD1   
T1, T2: Difference between new drive pinion retainer or new reverse brake housing and current drive pinion retainer or current reverse brake housing   
LD1: Calculated value of current drive pinion retainer or current reverse brake housing   
LD2Calculated value of new drive pinion retainer or new reverse brake housing

![](images/86a20ade4e83732994b2b3af98a7f06979ee87f96e15319b86cba129631e7e5a.webp)

![](images/64daa3cfff47c593ca33559ffd6e26946092ce449f30faed97f1629cd32ce715.webp)

6) Place the driven plate, drive plate and retaining plate neatly in this order on surface table.   
7) Set the dial gauge to retaining plate, and read its scale.

NOTE:

The value, which is read in the gauge at this time, is zero point.   
8) Scale and record the weight “Z" of a flat board which will be put on retaining plate.

NOTE:

Use a stiff board which does not bend against load as a flat board to be put on retaining plate.   
•Use a flat board weighing less than 29 N (3.0 kgf, 6.5 lb).

9) Put the flat board on retaining plate.

![](images/cb204f09ac80e8355b24e655de5972bc2300bd2df1204cdcb8e59f22d65aed7c.webp)

10) Using the following formula, read the push/pull gauge and calculate “N". N = 29 N (3.0 kgf, 6.5 Ib) - Z   
29 N (3.0 kgf, 6.5 Ib): Load applied to clutch plate   
Z: Flat board weight

11) Press the center of retaining plate by applying a force of "N” using push/pull gauge, and then measure and record the compression amount “A”.

NOTE: Measure at four points with a 90° interval and calculate the average.

![](images/c05f88ea00d6f12ea350890d1cec0347b76d5d6643dfd958950e7bda3556860e.webp)

(A)Drive plate (B) Driven plate Retaining plate

12) Installthe dish plate, drive plate, driven plate, retaining plate and snap ring to the reverse brake housing. NOTE:   
Install the dish plate in the correct direction.

![](images/c3f0295d2fea443d08aadc01e7649b3ce4ee97fcb332e877f5a0a122d8752f75.webp)

13) Measure and record the clearance “B between the retaining plate and snap ring.

![](images/4ac837869622236502fd5ed342738dbe4bac2725c5880c3de3e98f1fe2398c99.webp)

14) Piston stroke calculation   
Calculate with A and B dimensions recorded before. I it exceeds the limit, replace with a new drive plate and adjust within the initial standard value.   
S mm (in) = A + B   
S: Piston stroke   
A: Compression amount of drive plate and dish plate   
B: Clearance between retaining plate and snap ring

Initial standard: 2.3 — 2.7 mm (0.091 — 0.106 in)

Limit thickness: 2.9 mm (0.114 in)

![](images/0d6e485c7766e5a6fe1c6517fd0e350625a0d573f04154aa832c1455b0798027.webp)

# E: INSPECTION

Inspect the drive plate facing for wear and damage.   
Check the driven plate for discoloration (burnt color.   
Check for worn snap ring, fatigue or damaged return spring or deformed spring retainer.   
Make sure the clearance between rtaining plate and snap ring of reverse brake is within the limit If it ex ceeds the limit, replace with a new drive plate and select and adjust the retaining plate within the initial standard value.<Ref. to CVT(TR580)-295, ASSEMBLY, Reverse Brake Assembly.

# 1.  FORWARD CLUTCH ASSEMBLY

1) Install the forward clutch piston to forward clutch drum.

AT-06486

4Compress the return spring using the ST to installthe snap ring. ST1 18762AA010 COMPRуSSOR SPECIAL TOOL ST2 398673600 COMPRESSOR

6) Place the driven plate, drive plate and retaining plate neatly in this order on surface table.   
7) Set the dial gauge to retaining plate, and read its scale.

NOTE:

The value, which is read in the gauge at this time, is zero point.   
8) Scale and record the weight “Z" of a flat board which will be put on retaining plate.

NOTE:

Use a stiff board which does not bend against load as a flat board to be put on retaining plate.   
Use a flat board weighing less than 52 N (5.3 kgf, 11.7 Ib).

9 Put the flat board on retaining plate.

![](images/83549c925465318cf80263038657bc749e82104524bdd6ecb8d4aefb2d27d9e7.webp)

10) Using the following formula, read the push/pull gauge and calculate “N”.   
N = 52 № (5.3 kgf, 11.7 Ib) - Z   
52 N (5.3 kgf, 11.7 Ib) : Load applied to clutch plate   
Z: Flat board weight   
11) Press the center of retaining plate by applying a force of "N” using push/pull gauge, and then measure and record the compression amount “A".

NOTE: Measure at four points with a 90° interval and calculate the average.

![](images/ce117ba53002785b03859e150c8a8e0a24d5925ba6fbec141b1e25fd1da8b678.webp)

(A) Driven plate (B) Drive plate Retaining plate

12) Instal the dish plate, drive plate, driven plate, retaining plate and snap ring to the forward clutch carrier. NOTE:   
Install the dish plate in the correct direction.

![](images/3eb13ba7f00664e51d62357184fd79fec0ef39004c30ec1bff7af97d0ccd4c51.webp)

13) Measure and record the clearance “B between the retaining plate and snap ring.

![](images/41e631881361eb670ebea6ca7a4e415435d30363deda13aca4e182c0823c042d.webp)

AT-06492

14) Piston stroke calculation   
Calculate with A and B dimensions recorded before.   
If it exceeds the limit, replace with a new drive plate and adjust within the initial standard value. S mm (in) = A + B   
S: Piston stroke   
A: Compression amount of drive plate and dish plate   
B: Clearance between retaining plate and snap ring   
Initial standard: 1.0 — 1.4 mm (0.040 — 0.055 in)   
Limit thickness: 1.6 mm (0.063 in)

![](images/2406ec732f1a074ac59255e715bb01b3bee643f86c324490481a65daf2ea4b67.webp)

# 2. PLANETARY CARRIER ASSEMBLY

1) Install the balance oil guide.   
) Install the snap ring.

# 3. INTERNAL GEAR

1) Install the thrust gear plate.   
2) Install the snap ring.

# E: INSPECTION

Check the forward clutch drum, internal gear, sun gear and forward clutch piston lip for wear or damage. Inspect the drive plate facing for wear and damage.   
Check the driven plate for discoloration (burnt color).   
Check for worn snap ring fatigue or damaged return spring or deformed spring retainer.   
Make sure the clearance between retaining plate and internal gear of forward clutch is within the limit t exceeds the standard, replace the forward clutch. <Ref. to CVT(TR580)-312, ASSEMBLY, Forward Clutch Assembly.>

A: Front roller bearing width   
B: Rear roller bearing width   
C: Spacer width   
D: Height from end face of rear roller bearing inner race to surface plate E: Depth from end face of front roller bearin inner race to end face of ST 15 mm (0.591 in): Thickness of ST

ST2 927130000 EXTENSION DRIVE SHAFT

# CAUTION:

Tighten the lock nut while directly aligning ST2 and torque wrench.   
Ifthe starting torque is not within the specified range, select the drive pinion washer, and repeat the step until the starting torque is within the specified range.   
When a thicker drive pinion washer is selected, the starting torque decreases. When a thinner drive pinion washer is selected, the starting torque increases.

ST2 499787700 WRENCH

![](images/d98e06d676a1600a9744dfd59fb48a02bcb7b09321e4b65f763f16d6929f978e.webp)

While rotating the pinion shaft, tighten the retainer LH and loosen the retainer RH until the shaft can't be turned anymore. The backlash is “zero” when the pinion shaft comes to the point where it doesn't rotate. After the "zero” state is established, loosen the retainer LH by 3 notches and secure it with the lock plate. Retighten the retainer RH until it stops. Rotate the drive pinion 2 or 3 times. Tighten the retainer RH further 1-3/4 notches. This sets the preload. Finaly, secure the retainer with its lock plate.

![](images/292bce814ba9ea66728405b92e430b4fc8202ecac26d9f56e7e07191f58bf563.webp)

(A)Lock plate

NOTE: Turning the retainer by every one tooth changes the backlash approx. 0.05 mm (0.0020 in).

![](images/8a4e5e781bb86a4aecc6d3b702a4e570fe9aa90ea5fad8eee11b159e754d917d.webp)

(A) 1 tooth

Check the bearing for seizure or wear.   
Apply CVTF to bearing and rotate the bearing to check for noise or dragging etc.   
Check the oil pump chain cover for damage.   
Check for leakage of CVTF from the mating surface of oil pump chain cover.   
Check the oil seal for damage.

# c: CAUTION

Wear appropriate work clothing, including a cap, protective goggles and protective shoes when performing any work.'

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installtion or disassembly.

Do not place the oil pan with its inner side facing up until itis installed, to prevent intrusion of foreign matter into the control valve body.

Before removal, installtion or disassembly, be sure to clarify the failure. Avoid unnecessary removal, installation, disassembly and replacement.

When disassembling the case and other light alloy parts, use a plastic hammer to force it apart. Do not pry apart with screwdrivers or other tools.

Vehicle components are extremely hot after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

Use SUBARU genuine CVTF and recommended grease. Do not mix CVTF, grease etc. of different grades or manufacturers.

Be sure to tighten bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Place lifts, shop jacks or rigid racks at specified locations.

Apply CVTF onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation.

Apply CVTF onto the press-fitting surface of the part before press-fitting the part using a press.

Replace deformed or damaged snap rings with new parts.

Before installing O-rings or oil seals, apply suficient amount of CVTF to avoid damage and deformation.   
Be careful not to incorrectly install or fail to install O-rings, snap rings and other such parts.

Before securing a part on a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocks, aluminum plate, or cloth between the part and the vise.

Avoid damaging the mating surface of the case.

Before applying liquid gasket, completely remove the old liquid gasket.

After removing the sensors, breather hose and plugs, plug the holes to avoid foreign materials intruding a necessary.

During disassembly or assembly, be sure to use nylon gloves or paper towels. Do not use cloth gloves or waste cloth.

# CVT(TR690)-47

# 6Road Test

# A: INSPECTION

NOTE: Turn OFF the X mode switch and perform inspection.

# 1. GENERAL PRECAUTION

Road tests should be conducted to properly diagnose the condition of CVT.

CAUTION: Always observe the local traffic laws when performing the test.

# 2. D RANGE SHIFT FUNCTION

Make sure that the engine speed is 1,100 — 1,300 r/min while driving on the level road at 50 km/h (31 MPH) after accelerating from halting to 1/4 of accelerator opening angle. Then stop the vehicle. Check normal gear change has occürred while the vehicle speed changes from a constant speed to zero.

# 3.  KICK-DOWN FUNCTION

Check if engine speed wil rise by operating the accelerator opening angle to the ful from a constant speed of 50 km/h (31 MPH) or more.

# 4. ENGINE BRAKE OPERATION

Check down shifting operation, engine braking, and indicators inside the meters.

Drive in “6th speed of manual mode” [70 — 80 km/h (43— 50 MPH)], and shift down from 6th to 5th. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "6""5" At the same time, check the engine brake in 5th gear. Drive in "5th speed of manual mode" [60 —70 km/h (37 — 43 MPH)], and shift down from 5th to 4th. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "5" "4" At the same time, check the engine brake in 4th gear. Drive in "4th speed of manual mode" [50 — 60 km/h (31 — 37 MPH)], and shift down from 4th to 3rd. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "4"  "". At the same time, check the engine brake in 3rd gear. Drive in "3rd speed of manual mode" [30 — 40 km/h (19 — 25 MPH)], and shift down from 3rd to 2nd. Check if the indicator of combination meter switches "3"  "2". At the same time, check the engine brake in 2nd gear.   
Drive in "2nd speed of manual mode" [20 — 30 km/h (12— 19 MPH)], and shift down from 2nd to 1st. Check i the indicator of combination meter switches"At the same ime, check the engine brake n 1st gear.

# 5. LOCK-UP FUNCTION

When the accelerator is lightly depressed while driving on a flat road in “D" range, check that rpm does no change abruptly.

# 6. P RANGE OPERATION

Stop the vehicle on an uphill grade of 5% or more and shift to the "P" range and apply the electronic parkin brake. Check that the vehicle does not move when the parking brake is released.

# 7.  NOISE AND VIBRATION

Check for noise and vibration during driving at a constant speed, accelerating, decelerating and manual shi operation.

# 8 OIL LEAKAGE

After the driving test, inspect for leakage of CVTF and diferential gear oil from the transmission body.

# 7. Stall Test

# A: INSPECTION

CAUTION: Make sure no other person is around the vehicle during stall test measurement.

NOTE:

Stalltest is extremely important in diagnosing the condition of CVT and engine. The test is necessary to measure the engine stall speeds inR" and " range

Purposes of the stall test:

Operational check of forward clutch and reverse brake Operational check of the torque converter assembly Engine performance check 1) Place wheel chocks at the front and rear of all wheels and engage the electronic parking brake. 2) Turn the A/C OFF. 3) Using the Subaru Select Monitor, check if the throttle valve operates when you depress the accelerator pedal. <Ref. to EN(H6DO)(diag)-53, OPERATION, Subaru Select Monitor.> Check the engne oil evelRe. o LUD-GeneralDescription. 5 Check the coolant level. <Ref. to CO(H6DO)-13, Engine Coolant.> Adjust the CVTF level. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-38, ADJUSTMENT, CVTF.> 7 Increase the CVTF temperature to 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F) by idling the engine with the select lever shifted to"or "P" range. 8 Hold down the pre-collision brake OFF switch to turn OFF the pre-collision brake. (With EyeSight) Shif the select lever to " range. 1) Depress the accelerator pedal to the full while fully depressing the foot brake pedal with your left foot. 11 When the engine speed stabilizes, quickly record the engine speed and release accelerator pedal. Shift the select lever to "N” range. Let the engine idle for one minute or more to cool it down. 12) Shift to “R” range and perform the same stall test.

NOTE:

Do not perform a stalltest for over 5 seconds at a time. (From closed throttle, full open throttle to stall speed reading.) Failure to follow this instruction will cause the engine oil and CVTF to deteriorate and the clutch and brake to be adversely affected.   
Be sure to cool down the engine for at least one minute after each stall test with the select lever set in the "P"or "N" range and with the dle sped o 1,00 rmin or less.   
If the stall speed is higher than the specified range, attempt to finish the stall test in as short a time as possible, in order to prevent the CVT from sustaining damage.

Stall speed standard: 1,870 — 2,900 r/min (D range) 1,750 — 2,750 r/min (R range)

# CVT(TR690)-49

# Time Lag Test

# A: INSPECTION

NOTE:

When the select lever is shifted while the engine is idling, there willbe a certain time elapse or lag before shock is felt. This symptom helps to check the condition of forward clutch and reverse brake.

Perform the test at normal operation CVTF temperature of 60 — 80°C (140 — 176°F).   
Be sure to allow one minute or more interval between tests.   
•Make three measurements and take the average value.   
1) Apply the electronic parking brake.   
2 Start the engine. Check the idle speed. (A/C OFF)   
Shift the select lever from “N" to “D" range. Using a stop watch, measure the time elapsed from shifting the léver until the shock is felt.

# Time lag standard:

1.2 seconds or less

If “N” → “D” time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressuré) is too low.   
Forward clutch worn   
Piston malfunction   
Control valve body malfunction   
Learning incomplete   
4) In the same manner, measure the time lag when shifting from “N” range to “R” range.

Time lag standard: 1.5 seconds or less

If “N" → “R” time lag is longer than specified:

Secondary pressure (line pressure) is too low. Reverse brake worn   
Piston malfunction   
Control valve body malfunction   
•Learning incompléte

11) Remove the pressure pipe.

![](images/878f43acf8df40140f4a135f2d16c92e18ddd88805cbb1e3bb5eba98ca92187c.webp)

12) Remove the O-ring from oil strainer.

![](images/77d68c2e0a88b3184137770e3428db481f94f114acb9c775e5811de35dfb139e.webp)

13) Remove the O-ring from pressure pipe.

![](images/837d90bbc2b797f3ef6a0e666d4c9e9b8cd67ff2acd6b8b5f2ab959758e5e60b.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Clean the mating surface of oil pan and transmission case.   
2) Make sure that the CVTF filter is installed to the transmission case.

NOTE: Make sure that the CVTF fiter does not protrude from the transmission case.

![](images/5ee49cb702dfbcdcd9712ff524ae73da7d3db76f14e1c4cb0ab7ba6bbb1fc4d4.webp)

CVT00582

3) Check the control valve body for dust and other foreign matter.

4) Install the O-ring to the pressure pipe.

NOTE:

•Use new O-rings.   
Apply CVTF to the O-rings.

![](images/fd79145ecd0e144345b190f147f09512e91272353b0b8b68789be407ae7c2fcf.webp)

AT-05190

) Install the pressure pipe.

![](images/cf7156f8104af798dddda05359f935bba3090fe75d0a399673e701085966053e.webp)

6) Install he control valve body.

# CAUTION:

Beware of the transmission harness getting caught in between.   
Do not impact or bend the transmission harness because it has the oil temperature sensor inside.

# NOTE:

Engage the manual valve to the manual plate.   
Lead the transmission harness through from the point indicated by dashed line in the figure.

Tightening torque: 9 NбН (0.9 kgf-m, 6.6 ft-lb)

![](images/35e9307def64b02a6b4d210c2baefbd817ff9ebee260f0c6174f90a1d0b7c1c1.webp)

A)Short bolt (11 pcs) (BLong bolt (1 pcs)

7) Install the O-ring to oil strainer and install the oil strainer.

NOTE:

Use new O-rings.   
Apply CVTF to the O-rings.   
Let the transmission harness run between control valve body and oil strainer.

Tightening torque: 9 NбН (0.9 kgf-m, 6.6 ft-lb)

![](images/aba5066cfa8b45bfa4d52c23f54ff39c2c3d015d35365dd7a4c480c31f889557.webp)

8) Connect the control valve harness connector.

![](images/846772cf7fec0b44302b9ec8b41fd286af8bc95afeb35fa4f5f3f16f3e105f3d.webp)

AT-07378

9) Clean the magnet.   
10) Attach the magnet at the specified position of the oil pan.

![](images/1bb5ebe794a833fe579e1577d838e3135da70027105aab9492f6b01c8419796e.webp)

11) Apply liquid gasket all around the oil pan mating surface seamlessly.

Liquid gasket: THRуE BOND 1217B (Part No. K0877YA020) or equivalent

![](images/f678aaa9297cbdaf94d48d64424296fc926908802820bc87476b38c8bcd1757d.webp)

AT-07758

12) Install the oil pan by equally tightening the bolts.

CAUTION: Beware of the transmission harness getting caught in between.

![](images/71f7b57fdf5bf46e9fbd60de0b16629aacb1a55a6bb28057b77e37504e1172b9.webp)

13) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
14) Fill with CVTF. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-40, REPLACEMENT, CVTF.>   
15) Adjust the CVTF level. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-38, ADJUSTMENT, CVTF.>   
16) Perform the operation of AT learning mode. <Ref. to CVT(diag)-32, Learning Control.>

# C: INSPECTION

Check each part for damage or dust.   
Check oil strainer for clogging.   
Measure the resistance of each solenoid.

NOTE: Measurement should be performed at a temperature of 20°C (68°F).

# 21.Transmission Harness

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission from the vehicle. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-58, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
) Prepare for overhaul. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-156, Preparation for Overhaul.>   
3) Remove the transmission harness ground terminal and remove the harness connectors from front wheel speed sensor and secondary speed snsor.

![](images/45c3d708c6de5c7ee93cb1982051c789613ccdfd455293d5c6d0c6172a0a917f.webp)

4) Remove the harness connectors from inhibitor switch, primary speed sensor and secondary pressure sensor

5) Remove the transmission harness stay.

![](images/6ae77e2002ac72cbd34282b378a5624db938929f04fdf2643c3c2cf1e524e028.webp)

6) Remove transmission harness connector and inhibitor harness connector from harness stay. 7) Remove the control valve body. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-124, REMOVAL, Control Valve Body.> Remove the mounting bolt to pull out the bushing of transmission harness from transmission case round hole.

![](images/d6201f51718a3a5566a2fd4b4347b1c1b00488627cf3c02bdfdea3d722cd2b52.webp)

9) Remove the harness clip from transmission assembly.

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the harness clip to the transmission assembly.   
2) Insert the transmission harness bushing into the round hole on the transmission case and instal the bolt.

NOTE:

Use new O-rings.   
Do not impact or bend the transmission harness because it has the oil temperature sensor inside.

Tightening torque: 5 NбН (0.5 kgf-m, 3.7 ft-lb)

![](images/385708169dacd6e0f7fa6706bb69b5629490d9c685277e408d943ebe9bf4e71d.webp)

AT-05454

3) Install the control valve body. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-128, INSTALLATION, Control Valve Body.> Install the transmission harness connector and inhibitor harness connector to the harness stay. nstall the transmission harness stay.

Tightening torque: 16 Nm (1.6 kgf-m, 11.8 ft-lb)

![](images/106c4b3904a84144cb2bcb307c5171a076282c4bf75f6ee043f153b948811255.webp)

6 Connect the harness connectors to the inhibitor switch, primary speed sensor and secondary pressure sensor.

![](images/63bc31bd00c73e5edc1ce13c4ade9e535c8e83c4cd247f9bb673520a3d5f8c18.webp)

CVT00792

7) Connect the harness connectors to the front wheel speed sensor and secondary speed sensor

8) Install the transmission ground terminal.

NOTE: Install the transmission ground terminal at an approximately 45° angle (A).

Tightening torque: 16 NбН (1.6 kgf-m, 11.8 ft-lb)

![](images/b8947f9c94e09635859ac9bc64084854c4cb1a80fe02171829daa5362170ba40.webp)

9) Install the transmission cover.

Tightening torque: 8 NбН (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)

10) Install the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-75, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>

# C: INSPECTION

1) Visually check the harness and connector for damage or crack.   
2) Check the harness terminal for rust, disconnection or poor contact.   
3) Check the continuity between harness terminals and oil temperature sensor.

NOTE:   
Refer to WIRING SECTION for transmission harness terminal and oil temperature sensor terminal. <Ref. to WI-158, WIRING DIAGRAM, CVT ContrOl SyStem.

Harness continuity standard: Less than 12

Oil temperature sensor standard: Approx. 2.6 k2 (at 20°C)

# 28.Preparation for Overhaul

# A: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Before disassembling and assembling the transmission, follow the following procedures to prepare.

# B: PROCEDURE

1) Clean the transmission exterior.   
) Remove the torque converter assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-157, REMOVAL, Torque Converter Assembly.>   
3) Attach the ST on the transmission.   
ST 18632AA000 STAND ASSY

![](images/3ea78e9aa7248d517486d21caee24ac59f64e48094b294efdeccb527897f16db.webp)

4) Remove the transmission cover on the transmission upper side.

NOTE: Install using the following tightening torque.

Tightening torque: 8 Nm (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)

![](images/90fc10c345062658dd06bee2d01560a298cd1df55830a4315c2673a6a1451aa8.webp)

5) Place the transmission assembly on end.

# 29.Torque Converter Assembly

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly from the vehicle. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-58, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
2) Pull out the torque converter assembly horizontally.

CAUTION: Do not scratch the inside of engaging parts.

![](images/aadc5c3bf2b14382b5dd4748805599e899dc560674a56e7dd52155dd8e02f2fe.webp)

3) Remove the O-ring from the front reduction drive gear.

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the O-ring to front reduction drive gear.

NOTE: •Use new O-rings. Apply CVTF to the O-rings.

While holding the torque converter assembly by hand, carefully install t into the torque converter case.

NOTE:

Apply CVTF to the oil seal lip.   
Do not damage the oil seal and O-ring.   
3) Engage the splines while gently rotating the torque converter assembly by hand, and securely insert the assembly.   
4) Measure depth “A”, from converter case end surface to drive plate contacting surface.

Standard (reference): 6.8 mm (0.268 in) or less

![](images/e411611d9396b842a0700fb02ebce5cbc2cd6493afef34e0c304cc4e1ba9f35c.webp)

5) Install the transmission assembly to the vehicle. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-75, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmission Assembly.

# C: INSPECTION

Check the protrusion of torque converter center (front boss) is not deformed or damaged.   
Check the ring gear and exterior for break or damage.

# 30.Extension Case

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly from the vehicle. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-58, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
) Remove the front wheel speed sensor. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-120, REMOVAL, Front Wheel Speed Sensor.>   
3) Remove the harness clip, and remove the extension case.

NOTE:

The total number of extension case mounting bolts is 10.

![](images/8846fb79cbd6575c0bf2e657041adff6f521a4adea81ba49914f083bf52cdd45.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1 Clean the mating surface of the extension case and intermediate case.   
Select the thrust needle bearing. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-164, ADJUSTMENT, Rear Drive Shaft. Select the shim for transfer reduction driven gear. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-182, ADJUSTMENT, Transfer Reduction Driven Gear.>   
4) Install the selected thrust needle bearing to transfer clutch assembly.

NOTE: Install the thrust needle bearing in the correct direction.

![](images/565519a26bfc67c31b52a77f7f5da1ff8d4c0e67aaff02b454b1422f32802435.webp)

5) Attach the selected shim to transfer reduction driven gear assembly.   
6) Apply liquid gasket to extension case seamlessly.

Liquid gasket: THREE BOND 1215B or equivalent

![](images/16a974b550f845957c1fe50f0b4f7dbfc0d434d33a66b64ac6598163a6ebb79b.webp)

7) Install the extension case.

Tightening torque: 25 Nm (2.5 kgf-m, 18.4 ft-lb)

![](images/3775ce00064d23aeca6da9cd224ca5628bedb0d0a88e47a9d131ffbc9d6ed934.webp)

8) Install the front wheel speed sensor. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-120, INSTALLATION, Front Wheel Speed Sensor.>   
9) Instal the transmission assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-75, INSTALLATION, Automatic Transmission Assembly.

# C: DISASSEMBLY

1) Remove the dust cover from extension case.   
2) Remove the extension case oil seal from the extension case.

# D: ASSEMBLY

1) Press-fit the dust cover into extension case. 2) Install the extension case oil seal to extension case. ST 498057300 INSTALLER

# E: INSPECTION

Check there is no leak of CVTF from the joint between extension case and intermediate case.   
Check there is no damage or cracks on the extension case.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

NOTE:

When replacing the extension case, select the shims for rear drive shaft thrust needle bearing and transfer reduction driven gear. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-164, ADJUSTMENT, Rear Drive Shaft. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)- 182, ADJUSTMENT, Transfer Reduction Driven Gear.>

# 31.Rear Drive Shaft

A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly from the vehicle. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-58, REMOVAL, Automatic Transmission Assembly.>   
2) Remove the extension case. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-159, REMOVAL, Extension Case.>   
3) Remove the rear drive shaft.

Driven plate for discoloration (burnt color)

• Inspect the extension end play, and adjust it to within the standard value. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-178, AD JUSTMENT, Transfer Clutch.>

1) Before measuring clearance “A" between snap ring and pressure plate, place same thickness shims or both sides to prevent the pressure plate from tilting.

) When clearance “A" exceeds the limit for use, replace the drive plate and driven plate as a set, and seleci the pressure plate within the initial specified value.

Initial standard: 0.7 — 1.1 mm (0.028 — 0.043 in)

Limit thickness: 1.6 mm (0.063 in)

NOTE:

Turn OFF the X mode switch and perform inspection.

(1) With the steering wheel held at fully turned position, drive the vehicle in "D" range and with vehicle speed at approx. 5 km/h (3 MPH) in both clockwise and counterclockwise directions for approx. ten times each, while repeating acceleration and braking intermittently. () If the tight corner braking phenomenon stil persists, drivè the vehicle again in a circle for several laps.

Use a stiff board which does not bend against load as a flat board to be put on retaining plate.

11) Using the following formula, read the push/pull gauge and calculate "N". N = 84 N (8.6 kgf, 18. Ib) - Z   
84 N (8.6 kgf, 18.9 Ib) : Load applied to clutch plate   
Z: Flat board weight

12) Press the center of retaining plate by applying a force of "N” or more using push/pull gauge, and then measure and record the compression amount “A”.

NOTE: Measure at four points with a 90° interval and calculate the average.

![](images/428a4bee6c621778f36ca0d56a741a452446897aaae00e9e9774aad01aa34b2d.webp)

(A) Drive plate (B) Driven plate (C) Retaining plate (D) Dish plate

13) Install the dish plate, drive plate, driven plate, retaining plate and snap ring to intermediate case. NOTE:   
Install the dish plate in the correct direction.   
14Measure and record the clearance " between the retaining plate and snap ring. 15) Piston stroke calculation   
Calculate with A and B dimensions recorded before. I it exceeds the limit, replace with a new drive plate and adjust within the initial standard value.

![](images/2ff0649ec5226864187a192d9c3b270d4481eae226cc31195e5559cd10623a9c.webp)

S mm (in) = A + B

S: Piston stroke

A: Compression amount of drive plate and dish plate B: Clearance between retaining plate and snap ring

Initial standard: 2.88 — 3.18 mm (0.113 — 0.125 in)

Limit thickness: 3.38 mm (0.133 in)

# E: INSPECTION

Inspect the drive plate facing for wear and damage.   
Check the driven plate for discoloration (burnt color).   
Check for worn snap ring, fatigue or damaged return spring or deformed spring retainer.   
Make sure the clearance between retaining plate and snap ring of reverse brake is within the limit. it ex ceeds the limit, replace with a new drive plate and select and adjust the retaining plate within the initial standard value. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-195, ASSEMBLY, Reverse Brake Assembly.>

# E: INSPECTION

Check the forward clutch drum, internal gear, sun gear and forward clutch piston lip for wear or damage. Inspect the drive plate facing for wear and damage.   
•Check the driven plate for discoloration (burnt color).   
Check for worn snap ring, fatigue or damaged return spring or deformed spring retainer.   
Make sure the clearance between the retaining plate of forward clutch and the planetary carrier assembly is within the limit. f it exceeds the standard, replace the forward clutch assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-212, ASSEMBLY, Forward Clutch Assembly.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

1) Measure depth “A” from the ST upper face to the washer catch surface. ST 398643600 GAUGE

![](images/e5790f54b45503b8d19b5053f6021b17c98d60227fb177c0c766c42a00bd4605.webp)

![](images/9f341a680f6f19c26cb8527f2360e6ba486d6ea35f72be0c869955f75309f9df.webp)

4) Obtain the thickness of washer using the following formula.   
Calculation formula:   
T(mm)= (A - 15)-(B-15)-(0.75-0.95)   
[T (in) = (A - 0.591) − (B - 0.591) - (0.030 — 0.037)]   
T: Washer thickness   
A: Depth from the ST upper face to the washer catch surface   
B: Height from the upper surface of the ST to the mating surface of the intermediate case 15 mm (0.591 in): Thickness of ST   
0.75 — 0.95 mm (0.030 — 0.037 in): Clearance   
5) Select the washer to meet the value “T” obtained from step 4).

bly.≥

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Clean the mating surface of transmission case and converter case.   
2 Install he control device system. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-239, INSTALLATION, Transmission Control Device.>   
3) Install the O-ring to the lubrication pipe.

NOTE:

•Use new O-rings.

) Apply liquid gasket seamlessly to the mating surface of transmission case.

If the transmission case gets in contact with the lubrication pipe and support rod, do not install the transmission case forcibly.

If installing the transmission case is difficult, check if the lubrication pipe and support rod are bent. The total number of transmission case mounting bolts is 15.

Tightening torque: 41 NбН (4.2 kgf-m, 30.2 ft-lb)

7) Install the O-ring to CVTF pipe.

NOTE:   
Use new O-rings.   
8) The smaller opening of CVTF pipe should be inserted to transmission.

# E: INSPECTION

Check the transmission case for damage.   
Check for leakage of CvTF from the connection between converter case and transmission case.   
Check for leakae of CVTF from the connection between intermediate case and transmission case.   
Check the lubrication pipe for bend or damage.   
Check the bearing for smooth operation.   
•Check the bearing for seizure or wear.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

NOTE:

When replacing the transmission case with a new part, perform the following check and adjustment for the selection.   
Select the thrust bearing for the forward clutch assembly. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-228, ADJUSTMENT, Forward Clutch Assembly.>   
Select the snap ring for the reduction gear. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-236, ADJUSTMENT, Reduction Driven Gear.>

# D: ADJUSTMENT

# 1 procedure In replacement of primary And secondary pulley, or in rePLACEMENT OF PRIMARY PULLEY, SECONDARY PULLEY AND VARIATOR CHAIN

1) Measure depth “Lp" from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.

ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/2e562ace1584fc8edf19d4d9cee613d0370e0acb9da6bc0d2b20935c0f6b95ac.webp)

Measure height “Ls" from the drive pinion retainer upper face to the secondary pully bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.

![](images/bb8e57f594f6da9b340b6119463d0e087552c76f89b5ef4ba22493b5ae2d5b8b.webp)

3) Calculate the following formula.   
Calculation formula:   
T (mm) = B + (Lp − Ls) + 31.601 − A   
[T (in) = B + (Lp − Ls) + 1.224 − A]   
T: Pulley alignment   
A: Specified primary pulley dimension   
B: Specified secondary pulley dimension   
Lp: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface Ls: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface 31.601 mm (1.224 in): Constant

![](images/9c2aa21170550e58576cef25af36016aaeebefb59e137ce12de44b6aeae43911.webp)

4) Select one to two shims so that the total thickness meets the value obtained from step 3).

![](images/3be91f5bab3c5a7af81635b94b8f03413003325519afa2e9e3cd3430c496c5d6.webp)

# CVT(TR690)-269

# 2.  PROCEDURE WHEN REPLACING ONLY DRIVE PINION RETAINER OR CONVERTER CASE

1) Clean the mating surface of current drive pinion retainer and converter case. 2) Measure and record the shim thickness that is attached on the current converter case. Using the current drive pinion retainer, measure depth "Lp1" from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average.

![](images/6809b1a0067eb109951b1085d88d920c9179f730f8fa3caf706f4beab7c51fb6.webp)

4 Using the current drive pinion retainer or current converter case, measure depth “Ls1" from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average. ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/c464395afdefedc94f15b56966f35010a3b205c525deaec6a5dfece9f8dd5e15.webp)

5) Calculate the “LD1” using the following formula and record it.   
Calculation formula:   
LD1 mm (in) = Lp1 - Ls1   
LD1: Height from the primary pulley bearing catch surface to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Lp1: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface   
Ls1: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface

Using the new drive pinion retainer or new converter case, measure depth “Lp2" from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculate the average. ST 499575400 GAUGE

![](images/eb734fbc42abc677d3cb8ccf066d53a9a40a74968a3d711445d4759ffc4cb259.webp)

Using the new drive pinion retainer or new converter case, measure depth "Ls2" from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface at several points and calculáte the average. ST 49957540 GAUGE

![](images/70d2b2f9fee07584821b05c337a8ea6c7c3c88760cfffe352dc2e70f11822d93.webp)

8) Calculate the “LD2” using the following formula and record it.   
Calculation formula:   
LD2 mm (in) = Lp2 − Ls2   
LD2: Height from the primary pulley bearing catch surface to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Lp2: Depth from the ST upper face to the primary pulley bearing catch surface   
Ls2: Depth from the ST upper face to the secondary pulley bearing catch surface Calculate the recorded values of "“LD1" and “LD2" to obtain the positive number to select the shims. Calculation formula: T1 mm (in) = LD1 − LD2 or T2 mm (in) = LD2 – LD1   
T1, T2: Difference between new drive pinion retainer or new converter case and current drive pinion retainer or current converter case   
LD1: Calculated value of current drive pinion retainer or current converter case   
LD2: Calculated value of new drive pinion retainer or new converter case

![](images/8e4914a5db37595141eaf3839400a880f381a242fdf95470ef62e3c8507d76e0.webp)

![](images/a337f9dcb9926dd32f5965210b37b6bad2a84e83b71551cc5b6c354730cd8a29.webp)

![](images/178830db2ea77c883d7c2ac69acaabd366e8ccf89c85ec96567bae11726e1dc8.webp)

3) Install the O-rings.

# E: INSPECTION

Check each component for scratches, damage or other faults.   
Inspect the backlash of the pinion gear.

Specification: 0.13 — 0.18 mm (0.0051 — 0.0071 in)

![](images/171fea14ed7734b05d7a73f5efe364a7600a8596dad75bef2adf5e4efd863304.webp)

Measure the hypoid gear backlash, and then adjust it to be within specification. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-309, ADJUSTMENT, Front Differential Assembly.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

1) Using the ST, screw-in the retainer until resistance is felt.

NOTE:

RH side should be screwed-in more than LH side. ST 18658AA020 WRENCH COMPL RETAINER

![](images/e15355821c60d36ac2434609eedfa16f6cc44394c329774bd3c8a7a2fb7cb397.webp)

AT-05375

) Remove the remaining liquid gasket from the mating surface completely.

3) Using the ST, install the drive pinion assembly to converter case. ST 18270KA020 SOCKET (E20)

NOTE: Do not confuse the three different-length bolts when installing.

Tightening torque: 43 Nm(4.4 kgf-m, 31.7 b)

![](images/3d1807f68868e9229532d43f32be71f0da759001bbc31ccc4e25fcad9a51bbf3.webp)

4) Rotate the drive pinion shaft ten times or more using ST1 and ST2. ST1 18667AA010 HOLDER   
ST2 499787700 WRENCH

![](images/987daa4d1ae84d030358048a7692c9458f1a93c81f9d37560a92b5fcb87873c0.webp)

) While rotating the pinion shaft, tighten the retainer LH and loosen the retainer RH until the shaft can't be turned anymore. The backlash is “zero" when the pinion shaft comes to the point where it doesn't rotate.

# Front Differential Assembly

6) After the “zero state is established, loosen the retainer LH by 3 notches and secure it with the lock plate. Loosen the retainer RH and retighten until it stops. Rotate the drive pinion 2 or 3 times. Tighten the retainer RH further 1-3/4 notches. This sets the preload. Finally, secure the retainer with its lock plate.

![](images/3d0039a91c17733574099382e9b5d7bd0645449131e5bc11482bc48f337f04a4.webp)

(A)Lock plate

NOTE: Turning the retainer by every one tooth changes the backlash approx. 0.05 mm (0.0020 in).

![](images/a85d950836a68ef2cca48c73d6ddedbdbfba1a76ed258a2c298ee1e4055cbe24.webp)

AT-07908

(A) 1 tooth

# Front Differential Assembly

Wrap the drive shaft pinion shaft with cloth and pinch with vise pliers. Install the installation bolt into the boli hole of secondary pulley and secure the bolt and'vise pliers using a band or wire. Make sure the drive pinion shaft does not move.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

1) Measure height “A from the ST upper face to the bearing end face using the ST. ST 398643600 GAUGE

![](images/ff648c935420bc58d4ba930a9364c884dddd39dcbcfd89d76d9786f376b5d24f.webp)

) Measure depth “B” from the converter case cover upper face to the bearing catch surface.

![](images/27971699a498e7e01bf36a8882b92687a4253c32e54a6a4d722f5b66271671f2.webp)

3) Using the ST, measure height “C" from the ST upper face to the converter case cover mating surface ST 398643600 GAUGE

![](images/9af638517ea657bc25467b41af1bc68acf7a9c7d822d4ca539477ea3132d2ed1.webp)

4) Using the following formula, calculate clearance “T” to select shims.   
Calculation formula:   
T mm = (A - 15) - ((C-15) - B)   
[T in = (A − 0.591) — ((C − 0.591) − B)]   
T: Clearance   
A: Depth from the ST upper face to the bearing end surface   
B: Depth from the converter case cover upper face to the bearing catch surface C: Height from the ST upper face to the converter case cover mating surface 15 mm (0.591 in): Thickness of ST

![](images/09c702b27d31804ddc1fd7346525fb0b6fa4467c07b3402f95d1a0e3d2eec250.webp)
