Remove the snap ring.

![](images/dc079c492645f14ac9ce24a6f20b510bcebb42e49e1ab15e656cb696f9d0cefd.webp)

3) Remove the retaining plate, drive plate, driven plate and dish plate.

,r е , , 2

AT-05436

4) Remove the seal ring from front reduction driven shaft.

![](images/cb0a86110aa13a23ebecbe9f77e6186ca6920527b1d1414aa7c5a248488628d0.webp)

Remove the ball bearing, while tapping the entire circumference around the ball bearing outer race a litle at a time through the front reduction' driven shaft hole using the round bar with diameter of 7 mm (0.28 in).

![](images/921ba71d0cb6566e85c9530f2e7a5367358d746aebf7f3c3095018333e187add.webp)

# D: ASSEMBLY

1) Place the dish plate, driven plate, drive plate and retaining plate neatly in this order on surface table

NOTE: Make sure of the direction of dish plate. 2) Set the dial gauge to retaining plate, and read its scale.

NOTE:

The value, which is read in the gauge at this time, is zero point.   
3) Scale and record the weight “Z" of a flat board which will be put on retaining plate.

NOTE:

Use a stiff board which does not bend against load as a flat board to be put on retaining plate.   
•Use a flat board weighing less than 130 N (13.3 kgf, 29.2 Ib).

4) Put the flat board on retaining plate.

![](images/e5d46f8149d04d5d0b9d0852ff6e2535347744ff0909c671600f8edb2c0f289b.webp)

5) Using the following formula, calculate load "N", a force of pressing with push/pull gauge.   
N = 130 N (13.3 kgf, 29.2 b)- Z   
130 N (13.3 kgf, 29.2 b: Load applied to clutch plate   
Z: Flat board weight   
) Press the center of retaining plate by applying a force of “N” using push/pull gauge, and then measure an récord the compression amount “A”.

NOTE: Measure at four points with a 90° interval and calculate the average.

![](images/afd1fd90c416138032d0eb81a51e8163a6e744580ea31896cb5d1ddf39f7c189.webp)

(A) Drive plate (B) Driven plate (C) Retaining plate (D) Dish plate

7) Install the dish plate, driven plate, drive plate, retaining plate and snap ring. NOTE:   
Make sure of the direction of dish plate.

# CVT(TR690)-342

8) Measure and record the clearance “B" between the retaining plate and snap ring. NOTE: Before measuring, press down the whole circumference of retaining plate using your finger.

![](images/95f83670a18f2187e7f5cf58f755c31e8f94de4e35378f2984cd8c69e230773d.webp)

AT-06559

9) Piston stroke calculation   
Calculate with A and B dimensions recorded before.   
If out of standard, replace with a new drive plate and adjust it within standard. S mm (in) = A + B   
S: Piston stroke   
A: Compression amount of drive plate and dish plate   
B: Clearance between retaining plate and snap ring

Specification: 2.4 — 2.8 mm (0.094 — 0.11 in)

![](images/c3e61fd0350fbd2cc4b705b552f01b782fb0e9226f24161f7215359981d28dc8.webp)

10) Press-fit the ballbearing into front driven shaft.

NOTE: Use a new ball bearing.

![](images/f101ffdd01e71b4a1dd6ffa064cc47650e493783e77f3e0727f977cc89e2641e.webp)

11) Install the seal ring to the front driven shaft.

NOTE:

Install a new seal ring.   
Apply CVTF to the seal rings.

![](images/2a57b3e1fcbd699d880aa3fa6a1fa00aeffb23d16042503f0c999f65e60d3693.webp)

AT-05437

12) Instal the front reduction driven shaft to the front reduction driven gear.

13) Install the front reduction driven gear assembly to converter case cover.

![](images/78de19973a008a35f2eaaa7094b1faaa9541f5e40591f2ba2ec89b4f89d551c8.webp)

14) Apply compressed air intermittently to check the piston operation.

NOTE: Hold the arrowed area with a finger.

![](images/381dca125cafc051d62a4070a036cded0991ce0500b93d8c34462c789c12faa7.webp)

# E: INSPECTION

Check the drive plate for wear and damage.   
Check the driven plate for discoloration (burnt color).   
Check for worn snap ring, fatigue or damaged return spring or deformed piston retainer.   
Replace if its tooth surfaces are broken, damaged or excessively worn.   
Check the bearing for seizure or wear.   
Apply CVTF to bearing and rotate the bearing to check for noise or dragging etc.

# F: ADJUSTMENT

1 If the bal bearing is attached, remove the bearing and shims. <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-322, REMOVAL, Converter Case Cover.>   
Using the ST, measure height "A" from the ST upper face to the mating surface of the case.   
ST 398643600 GAUGE

![](images/cb5a837e71315bbef018e4b06b1bfbb547df09d686bf940695b2193cf0fd40f3.webp)

3) Measure depth “B” from the converter case cover upper face to the bearing catch surface.

![](images/a2a07c8b2886c7f505bd9f3421f5397965d7a79ccef86f754535ad3336f81a68.webp)

4) Install the ball bearing to the reduction driven gear.

NOTE: Use a new ball bearing.

![](images/aa1be180464a485c10b5043763fd5c919d413bab8de5eae6f90beb872a7561a3.webp)  
5) Measure depth “C” from the ST upper face to the bearing end face using the ST. ST 398643600 GAUGE

6) Calculate clearance “T” using the following formula.   
Formula: T mm = (C − 15) − ((A – 15) – B)   
[T in = (C - 0.591) - ((A - 0.591) - B)]   
T: Clearance   
A: Height from the ST upper face to the converter case mating surface   
B: Depth from the converter case cover upper face to the bearing catch surface C: Depth from the ST upper face to the bearing end face   
15 mm (0.591 in): Thickness of ST

![](images/f52bbd774185ec867ae7dfa9aa76483d7484d8adb22841d82903ecab5492a023.webp)

7) Select one to two shims so that the total thickness meets the value obtained from above.

![](images/9032105a86a28b09627e6fd91216eb6f906fb86240fac1e02bff0df99a49fc82.webp)

# General Description

A: CAUTION

1) The airbag system wiring harness is routed near the TCM.

# CAUTION:

All the airbag system wiring harnesses and connectors are colored yellow. Do not use an electric test equipment to check these circuits. Be careful not to damage the airbag system wiring harness when performing diagnostics or serviing the TCM.

2) When measuring the voltage or resistance of individual sensor or all electrical control modules, use a tapered pin with a diameter of 0.6 mm (0.024 in) or less and touch it to the tip of terminal. Never insert the tapered pin into the terminal because it deforms inside which may lead to malfunction.

# CAUTION:

If a taper pin or the like has been inserted into the connector terminal, replace the connector.

3) The TCM connector is waterproof. When measuring the TCM connector terminal voltage, or the resistance between the terminals, use the ST. ST 18460AA040 CHECK BOARD

# B: INSPECTION

Check the battery. <Ref. to SC(H4DO)-60, INSPECTION, Battery.> <Ref. to SC(H6DO)-60, INSPECTION, Battery.>

Standard voltage: 12 V or more

Specific gravity: 1.260 or more

# 2. TRANSMISSION GROUND

Make sure that the ground terminal bolt is tightened securely.

Tightening torque: ENGINE TYPE FB 14 NбН (1.4 kgf-m, 10.3 ft-lb)

# Inspection Mode

A: PROCEDURE

<Ref. to CVT(TR580)-48, Road Test.> <Ref. to CVT(TR690)-48, Road Test.>

CVT(diag)-26

# 10.Drive Cycle

# A: PROCEDURE

It is possible to complete diagnosis of the DTC by performing the indicated drive cycle. After the repair for the DT, perform a necessary drive cycle and make sure the fünction recovers and the DTC is recorded.

# 1.  PREPARATION FOR DRIVE CYCLE

1) Check that the battery voltage is 12 V or more and fuel remains approx. half [20 — 40 L (5.3 — 10.6 US gal, 4.4 — 8.8 Imp gal)].   
After performing the diagnostics and Clear Memory Mode, check that no DTC remains. <Ref. to CVT(diag)-25, Clear Memory Mode.>

NOTE:

Perform the drive cycle after warming up the engine except when the ATF temperature at engine start is specified.

# DRIVE CYCLE A

![](images/9ab4d1fd8e92e64dd56b4a06f3a744c694c8afda0a59534f32b04bbfebb0e0cf.webp)

# Diagnostic procedure:

1) Start the engine.   
2) Depress the brake pedal and move the select lever to each range at an interval of five seconds.

NOTE: Move the select lever in the following order: "P" → “R" → “N" → “D" → “N” → “R" → “P".

# 3 DRIVE CYCLE B

![](images/70619ed939461beaa9adda5f66d97cdf803478eabfff28c9a9598fbb59f3f8f8.webp)

# Diagnostic procedure:

1) Start the engine under condition that ATF temperature is at 20°C (68°F) or below. Drive in any driving patern for 20 minutes. (Include driving at a constant legal speed (for 20 seconds) at least once.)

NOTE: Repeat two or more driving cycles in this driving pattern.

# CVT(diag)-27

# 4DRIVE CYCLE C

![](images/ef93fe18eca46651f6603785f291205909c29478baa060fe08787952942d7dbe.webp)

# Diagnostic procedure:

1) Start the engine.   
2) Accelerate slowly to a legal speed, and then decelerate slowly to a stop.

# CVT(diag)-28

# 5DRIVE CYCLE D

![](images/0bb46e87023c27ddcc3ede731a8075ddc9e7c94f50f9bb704f01b048fe1e1f2a.webp)

# Diagnostic procedure:

1) Start the engine.   
Drive in any driving patern for 20 minutes. (Include driving at a constant legal speed (for 20 seconds) at least once.

# 6DRIVE CYCLE E

![](images/659244785593a52060676da3d39056797e18365d8f020a1c2d4ea7099f39f879.webp)

# Diagnostic procedure:

1) Start the engine.

# CVT(diag)-31

# 12.Learning Control

# A: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

Follow the messages displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor when working. When the following work is performed, perform learning work for the transmission. Replacement of TCM/Replacement or disassembly of transmission assembly/Replacement of control valve body/Clearing AT leaning value is executed.

# B: PROCEDURE

# 1.  PREPARATION FOR LEARNING

1) Warm up or coo down until the ATF temperature displayed on the Subaru Select Monitor is 40 — 65°C   
(104—149°F).   
2) After stopping the vehicle, shift the select lever to “P” range.   
3 Apply the electronic parking brake.   
4) Lift up the vehicle.

# CAUTION:

While working, be sure to keep the lower edge of the tires 30 cm or more above the ground as vehicle will vibrate.

5) Connect the Subaru Select Monitor to data link connector.   
6) Turn the ignition switch to ON.   
7) Turn off al switches causing an electrical load, such as headlights, A/C, seat heater and rear defogger, etc.

# 2. SIMPLE LEARNING

NOTE:

Simple learning is performed with the vehicle lifted, without actually running the vehicle.

CAUTION:

Do not turn the power of the Subaru Select Monitor OFF during work, and do not disconnect the data link connector.'

1) On «SФБТФе display, select «DЙБЗОПУЙУе.   
2) On «Vehicle УЕМЕГФЙПОе display, input the vehicle information and select «CПОЖЙТНЕДе.   
3) On «Main MЕОХе display, select «Each SЩУФЕНе.   
On Select SЩУФЕНе display, select Transmission Control SЩУФЕНе.   
On «Select FХОГФЙПОе display, select «Work SХРРПТФе.   
6 On Work SХРРПТФе display, select «AT learning НПДЕе.   
7) Follow the messages displayed on the screen when working.

NOTE:

During AT learning in progress, AT OIL TEMP light in the combination meter starts flashing at 2 Hz and the learing oeration start. When the AT OIL TEMP light which was fashing at  H oes off the following message is displayed on the screen.

# CVT(diag)-33

# 13.AT OIL TEMP Warning Light Display

# A: OPERATION

The AT OIL TEMP light illuminates or blinks, when the ATF temperature is high and malfunction occurs in CVT.

At normal condition   
After turning the ignition switch to ON, illuminates for 2 seconds then goes off.   
When ATF temperature is high   
AT OIL TEMP light illuminates when the ATF temperature is abnormally high with the ignition switch ON. When malfunction is detected   
AT OIL TEMP light blinks at 2 Hz when the TCM detects the malfunction of CVT with the ignition switch ON. In this case, inspect using "Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC".<Ref. to CVT(diag)- 4Diagnostic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code(DT).>   
When AT learning is not finished   
AT OIL TEMP light repeats "Blinking at 4 Hz Turning OFF" when the AT learning is not completed with the ignition switch ON. In this case, perform the “Learning. (During AT learning, the light blinks at 2 Hz or illuminates.) <Ref. to CVT(diag)-32, Learning Control.>

# 14.AWD Warning Light Display

# A: OPERATION

AWD lightiluminates or blinks, when the AWD is in special control condition and AWD has malfunction. At normal condition After turning the ignition switch to ON, iluminates for 2 seconds then goes off.

When FF mode is selected

AWD light illuminates when the AWD ON/OFF switching function is set to "FF mode" with the ignition switch ON.

When malfunction is detected

.WD light blinks at 2 Hz when any of the following malfunctions are detected with the ignition switch ON. When tire with different diameter is installed, or air pressure of any of four wheels is excessively low. When “Rear differential inspection mode" is judged as NG <Ref. to DI-83, Rear Differential Inspection Mode.>

# G: DTC PO711 TRANSMISSION FLUID TEMPERATURE SENSOR "A" CIRCUITRANGE/PERFORMANCE

DTC DETECTING CONDITION:

Detected when two consecutive driving cycles with fault occur.

# TROUBLE SYMPTOM:

Excessive shift shock Shift characteristics malfunction

NOTE:

For the diagnostic procedure, perform the diagnosis according to DTC P0712 and P0713. <Ref. to CVT(diag-60, DTC PO712 TRANSMISSION FLUID TEMPERATURE SENSOR "A" CIRCUIT LOW, DiagnOStic Procedure with Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC).> <Ref. to CVT(diag)-63, DTC P0713 TRANSMISSION FLD TEPERATURE SENSORA CIRCUIT HIG DiagiPrOCedue Wth Diaos Troubleode (DTC).>

# 1. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS (ENGINE TYPE FB)

Diagnosis 1

•Judge the malfunction of oil temperature sensor characteristics (stuck to low temperature side). Judge as NG if the amount of oil temperature change since ignition ON is equal to or below the predetermined value.   
Diagnosis 2   
Judge the malfunction of oil temperature sensor characteristics (stuck to high temperature side). Judge as malfunction when the difference between engine coolant temperature and C oil temperature is equal to or more than specified value at starting.

# 2.  EXECUTION CONDITION (ENGINE TYPE FB)

![](images/1485116d0b27ea405129a46dfde1f6b96e23ad3617bee44c21a051426cd03400.webp)

# Time Needed for Diagnosis:

Diagnosis 1: 600 s   
Diagnosis 2: 300 s   
Malfunction Indicator Light Illumination: Iluminates when malfunction occurs in 2 continuous driving cycles.

# 3. OUTLINE OF DIAGNOSIS

•Detect the abnormality in transmission gear ratio control function. Judge as NG if a discrepancy between the transmission target gear ratio (as internal data) and the actual gear ratio becomes the specified value or more. Standing start problems Shock occurs when engaging the lockup clutch. Shock occurs when selecting shift position.

Detect the malfunction of primary speed sensor signal characteristics.

# General Description

# c: CAUTION

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation or disassembly. Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.   
Before removal, installtion or disassembly, be sure to clarify the failure.Avoid unnecessary removal, installation, disassembly and replacement.   
When disassembling the case and other light alloy parts, disassemble by using a plastic hammer. Do not pry apart with screwdrivers or other tools.   
Vehicle components are extremely hot after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts. Use SuARU genuine transmission gear oil, grease or equivalent. Do not mix gear oil, grease, etc. of different grades or manufacturers.   
Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.   
Place shop jacks or rigid racks at the specified points.   
Apply transmission gear oil onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation.   
Replace deformed or damaged snap rings with new parts.   
Before installing O-rings or oil seals, apply sufficient amount of ransmission gear oil to avoid damage and deformation.   
Be careful not to incorrectly install or fail to install O-rings, snap rings and other such parts.   
Before securing a part on a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocks, aluminum plate, or cloth between the part and the vise.   
Avoid damaging the mating surface of the case.   
Before applying liquid gasket, completely remove and clean the old liquid gasket.   
Be careful of handing he oil sealring and gasket. he contact surface of themis damaged, oil leake may occur.   
When pressing-in the oil seal, make sure that the oil seal lip portion and outer surface are not damaged or tilted.   
When replacing the taper roller bearing, replace the outer race and inner race as a set.   
When replacing the hypoid gear, replace the hypoid driven gear and drive pinion shaft as a set. eplace the bolts if the seating surface or the thread surface is excessively rusted.

# Transmission Gear Oil

# A: INSPECTION

1) Park the vehicle on a level surface.

Turn the ignition switch to OFF, and wait until the engine cools.   
Remove the oil level gauge and wipe it clean.   
Reinsert the oil level gauge all the way.Be sure that the oil level gauge is correctly inserted in the proper direction.   
Pullut theil leel augagainand check theil leel f it belw he lower eelcheck forl leake and add transmission gear oil through the oil level gauge hole to bring the level up to the upper level.

# CAUTION:

The length of the oil level gauge varies depending on models and destinations. Make sure to use the appropriate oil level gaug.

![](images/980301fb8a28dfd0e175d3196e868761c303e236560efcf5704ba6c058672bf6.webp)

(A) Oil level gauge (B) Upper level Lower level

(1 Gray (215.8 mm (8.5 in)

# B: REPLACEMENT

Pull out the oil level gauge.   
Lift up the vehicle.   
Using the TORX bit T70, remove the drain plug, and drain the transmission gear oil completely.

CAUTION:

Immediately after the vehicle has been running or after idling for a long time, the gear oil willbe hot. Be careful not to receive burns.   
Be careful not to spill the gear oil on the exhaust pipe, to prevent emission of smoke or causing a fire. If gear oil is spilt, wipe it off cqmpletely.

4) Attach the drain plug using TORX" bit T70.

NOTE:

Install the drain plug after draining transmission gear oil.   
Use a new gasket.

# Tightening torque:

44 N.m (4.5 kgf-m, 32.5 ft-Ib) (aluminum gasket, silver)   
70 Nm (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-b) (copper gasket, brown)   
70 Nm (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-b) (metal gasket, black)   
5) Lower the vehicle.   
6) Fill with transmission gear oil through the oil level gauge hole.

# 3Manual Transmission Assembly

# A: REMOVAL

1 Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> Remove the air intake duct. <Ref. to IN(H4DO)-12, REMOVAL, Air Intake Duct.>   
Remove the clip (A) from the air intake boot.   
4 Loosen the clamp (B) connecting the air intake boot and air cleaner case (rear).   
5) Loosen the clamp (C) which connects the air intake boot and throttle body.

![](images/c25961e20988bf200a14338c03b5bc0f0cf5d881b78c2e17aa587047f66acf2d.webp)

6) Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body, and move it to the left side wheel apron.

![](images/d8701dff4c16e53e9b7c17635c978bbade61c8a650b656c78a381ea888f1e39c.webp)

7 Disconnect the back-up light switch and the neutral position switch connectors, then remove the transmission radio ground cord terminal.

![](images/9d7fc13701dc1280429be1a51401932001ea227140fdc3c62296e5609dce7d39.webp)

(A) Neutral position switch connector (2P, brown) (B) Back-up light switch connector (2P, gray) (C) Transmission radio ground cord terminal

8) Disconnect the throttle position sensor harness connector and manifold pressure sensor harness connec tor.

![](images/68bc4c5aa5a001396778414bfd7ec82ebc2eed58310b77dcc7cbfab5abb64d7d.webp)

9) Remove the starter. <Ref. to SC(H4DO)-7, REMOVAL, Starter.>

10) Remove the operating cylinder and suspend on a wire.

![](images/039f92300609347e44c5c05437bc63cd5f3618473abfbd05d3e86b0ce4f6bf9b.webp)

11) Remove the front tires.   
12 Lift up the vehicle.   
13) Remove the front under cover. <Ref. to El-29, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>   
14) Remove the center exhaust pipe (rear). <Ref. to EX(H4DO)-12, REMOVAL, Center Exhaust Pipe.   
15) Drain transmission gear oil completely. <Ref. to 6MT-26, REPLACEMENT, Transmission Gear Oil.>   
16) Remove the center exhaust cover.

![](images/a854560b28f8d05476041c06113e452e1af9fd31ad5d094389a5c0edac01216b.webp)

17) Remove the hanger bracket.

![](images/da974b6d2d600940e47338eb68c13b560a63da9f20d0e766840f932a3cd5ecc5.webp)

18) Remove the universal joint of the steering shaft. <Ref. to PS-24, REMOVAL, Universal Joint.> 19) Remove the propeller shaft. <Ref. to DS-10, REMOVAL, Propeller Shaft.>   
20 Remove the MT gear shift cable and MT gear select cable from MT gear shift lever. <Ref. to CS-56, REMOVAL, MT Gear Shift Lever.

# CAUTION:

Do not bend MT gear shift cable and MT gear select cable at a sharp angle. Disconnect the MT gear shift cable and MT gear select cable at the MT gear shift lever side. Always use new MT gear select cable if the cable is removed from selector lever COMPL of transmission side.

21) Disconnect the stabilizer link.

![](images/b862aa137700c26963955f52e7dcc9ba015c32a647ecb19446769cf11c09a81f.webp)

22) Remove the bolt securing the balljoint of the front arm to the housing, then separate the front arms and the housing.

![](images/e3ba1d85ddc48f1f9bb236c82ae2b47af95aa30c6faf5e85a188c0a8b880edfd.webp)

23) Using a crowbar, separate the left and right front drive shafts.

![](images/011ee604c33c0b6a11a832e228db6ec213d18205067d9f02116615d7275d89cb.webp)

24) Lower the vehicle.

25) Remove the nuts connecting the engine mounting and the transmission main mounting bracket.

![](images/f1cde868f94098a9fdc382af7c31f1658ac737539b692a4a32ab234183df7356.webp)

26) Remove the V-belt covers.

![](images/0f428bbb98bfc8d919be9047ba75c9aee54ff4d4349eb431ef57a9ab963c4a0e.webp)

7) Using the ST1, install the ST2 to the engine unit. ST1 18363AA050 BOLT   
ST2 18360AA040 HANGER

Oil Seal

# A: INSPECTION

Check for leakage of transmission gear oil from the oil seal. If there is oil leakage, replace the oil seal with the new part and check the propeller shaft.

# B: REPLACEMENT

1 Disconnect the ground terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.> Lift up the vehicle.   
3 Remove the front under cover. <Ref. to El-29, REMOVAL, Front Under Cover.>   
4) Clean the transmission exterior.   
Using the TORX bit T70, remove the drain plug, and drain the transmission gear oil completely.

# CAUTION:

Immediately after the vehicle has been running or after idling for a long time, the gear oil will be hot. Be careful not to receive burns.   
Be careful not to spill the gear oil on the exhaust pipe, to prevent emission of smoke or causing a fire. If gear oil is spilled, wipe it off completely.

6) Attach the drain plug using TORX° bit T70.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

# Preparation for Overhaul

# A: PROCEDURE

1) Clean oil, grease, dirt and dust from the transmission.

When transmission gear oil remains in the transmission, using the TORX@ bit T70, remove the drain plug, and drain the gear oil completely.   
Attach the drain plug using TORX® bit T70.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 44 NбН (4.5 kgf-m, 32.5 ft-lb) (aluminum gasket, silver) 70 Nm (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-b) (copper gasket, brown) 70 NбН (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-lb) (metal gasket, black)

![](images/1f03d0cc87e2fb861ac8fc029961c187ebf98b384b4c24b42c7c731300a761c1.webp)

![](images/d131f03830efe7e7101d4734ac1df8855cb6232edd120b45c6d546cf64fd556b.webp)

5) Apply transmission gear oil to rotating parts before assembly.   
6) Ail disassembled parts, if to be reused, should be reinstalled in the original positions.   
7) Gaskets, lock washers and lock nuts must be replaced with new ones.   
8) Apply liquid gasket to the specified areas to prevent leakage.

4) Install the taper roller bearing (extension case side) outer race to the transfer driven gear.   
) While pressing the taper roller bearing (extension'case side) outer race horizontally rotate the transfer driven gear for ten turns.   
Measure the height “W" between transfer case and taper roller bearing (transfer case side) on the transfer driven gear.

![](images/56a3314e01d154cf6da0c0dc7d44748ba39e1f0bb34afcc08ef2ea9ac2c4d7da.webp)

8) Calculate the adjusting washer thickness “t” using the following calculation.   
t = X - W + (0.15 — 0.2 mm (0.006 — 0.008 in))   
X: Depth of taper roller bearing insertion part of extension case   
W: Height between transfer case and taper rollr bearing (transfer case side) on transfer driven gear 0.15 —0.20 mm (0.006 — 0.008 in): Amount of standard protrusion 9) Select the adjusting washer with the nearest value in the following table. NOTE:   
Be sure that it is always within the preload.

# Preload of taper roller bearing (extension case side) (amount of standard protrusion): 0.15 — 0.20 mm (0.006 — 0.008 in)

![](images/55f4d2e838bddb4fb51eea6087b2e7d59917da286d9fcbb369dc6d6777911939.webp)

13) Calculate the adjusting washer thickness “U” using the following calculation. U = S + T - 30 mm (1.18 in) - (0.15 — 0.35 mm (0.0059 — 0.0138 in))

T: Depth between the extension case + ST and the transfer drive gear   
30 mm (1.18 in): Thickness of ST (× 2 pieces)   
0.15 — 0.35 mm (0.0059 — 0.0138 in): Clearance

# 15.Transmission Case

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the manual transmission assembly from the vehicle. <Ref. to 6MT-27, REMOVAL, Manual Transmission Assembly.>   
) Remove the clutch release lever and the release bearing. <Ref. to CL-13, REMOVAL, Release Bearing and Lever.   
3) Remove the transfer case together with the extension case assembly. <Ref. to 6MT-61, REMOVAL, Transfer Case and Extension Case Assembly.>   
4) Remove the bearing mounting bolt.

![](images/f2e18ebeb3ee4766ad5c79ddedd7a5e4871d1ca4835d63871420de53d16210cb.webp)

5) Remove the main shaft rear plate.

![](images/c26769850bd641ce3a3e3324e630abfc31d78d292e7d5a359e108b576f63533f.webp)

6) Remove the bolts and nuts, and separate the transmission case into the right and left cases.

![](images/f444009064c395028787ec4f51231601e0fe35556c51f694e24ebcdaba698cc6.webp)

7) Remove the drive pinion shaft assembly. NOTE: Use a hammer handle, etc. to remove if too tight.

![](images/eac643888d6cb579dcbde357657dcf14d1317162eed7fb0558157a1c3f3f3b84.webp)

(A) Main shaft ASSY (BDrive pinion shaft ASSY

8) Remove the main shaft assembly.   
9) Remove the front differential assembly.

![](images/21495c74cc80e6ee07ae41fc3a9485a97b6ba99e04bd344163185e2b9c128043.webp)

10) Remove the diferential side retainers and taper roller bearing outer races on the left and right sides. <Ref. to 6MT-134, REMOVAL, Front Differential Assembly.>

NOTE:

Do not confuse the right and left taper roller bearing outer races.   
11) Remove the reverse idler gear. <Ref. to 6MT-146, REMOVAL, Reverse Idler Gear.> 12) Remove the shifter fork and rod. <Ref. to 6MT-158, REMOVAL, Shifter Fork and Rod.> 13) Remove the front oil guide.

![](images/24d82f9fdaf11884df677ad4a40c24b9cc1e89e0f3a3e17b824f0c4f5f17b689.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Wipe of grease, oil and dust on the mating surfaces of transmission cases with cleaning solvent. ) Install the shifter fork and rod. <Ref. to 6MT-160, INSTALLATION, Shifter Fork and Rod.> ) Install the reverse idler gear. <Ref. to 6MT-148, INSTALLATION, Reverse Idler Gear.> 4) Select the drive pinion shim. <Ref. to 6MT-115, INSTALLATION, Drive Pinion Shaft Assembly.> ) Install the taper roller bearing outer race to the transmission case LH side, and install the differential side rétainer with the O-ring removed.

6) Install the front differential assembly.   
7) Install the main shaft assembly.

NOTE: Align to install the needle bearing knock pin hole to the transmission case knock pin. 8) Install the selected drive pinion shims and drive pinion shaft assembly.

NOTE: Install the transmission case knock pin into the roller bearing knock pin hole. 9) Tighten the left and right side of the transmission case with the 17 mounting bolts.

NOTE:

•Insert bolts (11) and (16) from the LH side of the transmission case.   
Match the cases together so that the drive pinion shims are not caught between the cases.

Tightening torque: 8 mm bolt 25 NбН (2.5 kgf-m, 18.4 ft-lb) 10 mm bolt 40 NбН (4.1 kgf-m, 29.5 ft-lb)

![](images/818b0ffd2e1a4c1861e61e8410606fca7a7503edaa78056479cecdadb5411e2d.webp)

10) Install the taper roller bearing outer race to the RH side of the transmission case.   
11) Tighten the bearing mounting bolts.

Tightening torque: 30 NбН (3.1 kgfm, 22.1 ft-lb)

![](images/991ef19b113b1b2504a873c3df22400bf919426f14ddaefa70c34f810fcbf62d.webp)

12) Perform backlash adjustment of the hypoid driven gear and preload adjustment of the taper rollr bear  
ing. (1) Attach the ST on drive pinion shaft assembly.   
ST 18667AA020 HOLDER (2) Place the transmission case with the LH side facing downward, and put ST1 on the taper roller bearing outer race.   
(3) Screw in the differential side retainer from the bottom into left case using ST2. Fit the ST3 on the main shaft of the transmission. Shift the gear into 4th or 5th, and turn the shaft several times. Screw in the differential side retainer while rotating the ST3 until a slight resistance is felt on ST2.   
This is the contact point of the hypoid driven gear and the drive pinion shaft. Repeat the above sequence several times to ensure the contact point.   
ST1 399780104 WEIGHT   
ST2 18630AA010 WRENCH COMPL RETAINER   
ST3 499927100 HANDLE

![](images/9efd8b7813678e01d83d51feb29391f8bfb07bb231cfb4da400dbcb9257d7df1.webp)

![](images/a9a13e95c849420e4c8bd6287b160e6cde84400b853ea61a1fc10a44532fef12.webp)

(4) Remove the WEIGHT, and screw in the differential side retainer without the O-ring into the RH side of the transmission case, and stop at the point where a slight resistance is felt. NOTE: In this condition, the backlash between hypoid driven gear and drive pinion shaft is zero. ST 18630AA010 WRENCH COMPL RуTAINER

![](images/34dd1cd8a7e27ad4307465d8ca7df9cd1a400a0907810de8a39a8899799f00bb.webp)

() Loosen the differential side retainer on the LH side of the transmission case by 3 notches, and turn the differential side retainer on the RH side of the transmission case by 3 notches in order to apply backlash. (6) Screw in the differential side retainer of the RH side of the transmission case additionally by 1 notch in order to apply preload on taper roller bearing.

(7) Tighten temporarily both the retainer lock plates LH and RH, and put marks on both the differential side retainer and retainer lock plate for later readjustment.

NOTE:

/hen it is difficult to attach the retainer lock plate, turn over the retainer lock plate and attach.

(8) Turn the transmission main shaft several times while tapping around the differential side retainer lightly with a plastic hammer. 13) Inspect and adjust backlash and tooth contact of the hypoid driven gear. <Ref. to 6MT-140, INSPECTONFront Differential Assembly. 14) Separate the transmission case into left and right parts. <Ref. to 6MT-93, REMOVAL, Transmission Case.> 15) Check each shifter fork. <Ref. to 6MT-162, INSPECTION, Shifter Fork and Rod.> 16) Select a main shaft rear plate. <Ref. to 6MT-114, ADJUSTMENT, Main Shaft Assembly.> 17) Install the front oil guide.

NOTE: Fit in all the way.

# A: REMOVAL

(2) Rotate the alignment mark on the reverse idler sub gear side in the arrow direction by two teeth, and secure it with a wire.

# E: INSPECTION

Disassembled parts should be washed with cleaning solvent first, then inspected carefully. 1 Bearing

Replace the bearings in the following cases.

When the bearing balls, outer races and inner races are broken or rusty.

When the bearing is worn.

When the bearings fail to turn smoothly or emit noise in rotation after transmission gear oil has been applied.

When bearing has other defects.

2) Bushing (each gear) Replace the bushing in following cases.

When the sliding surface is damaged or abnormally worn.

When the inner wall is abnormally worn

3) Gear Replace gears in the following cases.

Replace the gear with new part if is tooth surfaces are broken, damaged or excessively worn.   
Correct or replace if the cone that contacts the baulk ring is rough or damaged.   
Repair or replace i the inner surface or end face is damaged.

4) Baulk ring, synchro cone Replace the baulk ring and synchro cone in the following cases.

When the inner surface or end face is damaged.

When the baulk ring inner surface is abnormally or partially worn down.

When the contact surface of the baulk ring insert section is cracked or abnormally worn.

f the gap between the end faces of the baulk ring and the gear splined part is excessively small, check the clearance (A) while pressing the ring against the cone.

Clearance (A): 0.5 mm (0.020 in) or more Single cone

# Main Shaft Assembly

Apply transmission gear oil to the cone of the gear and while press-fitting the baulk ring, check there is no rotation in the circumfrential direction.

![](images/182865252492c67621f125f963f48a03942a29dd45ca1f3e777dd062c3d1bb92.webp)

5) Coupling sleeve and synchronizer hub   
•"Check the slipping condition of the coupling sleeve.   
Check the splines on the coupling sleeve and synchronizer hub for wear.   
6) Shifting insert   
Replace the shifting insert if there is deformation, excessive wear on the ball section or any defectiveness. 7) Oil seal   
Replace the oil seal if the lip is deformed, hardened, worn or defective in any way.   
8) Gearshift mechanism   
Repair or replace the gearshift mechanism if excessively worn, bent or defective in any way.

# E: INSPECTION

Disassembled parts should be washed with cleaning solvent first, then inspected carefully.   
1) Bearing   
Replace the bearings in the following cases.   
When the bearing balls, outer races and inner races are broken or rusty.   
When the bearing is worn.   
When the bearings fail to turn smoothly or emit noise in rotation after transmission gear oil has been applied.   
The double ball bearing of the drive pinion shaft should be checked for smooth rotation before the drive pinion shaft assembly is disassembled. In this case, because a preload is working on the bearing, its rotation feels like it is slightly'dragging unlike other bearings.

![](images/372df257790d3dde5c7c433a73c12ccc82ce9e69b8a4ae0f8c12665a3b5b815c.webp)

(ADrive pinion shaft BDouble ball bearing

When bearing has other defects.   
2) Bushing (each gear) Replace the bushing in following cases.   
When the sliding surface is damaged or abnormally worn.   
When the inner wallis abnormally worn.

3) Gear

Replace gears in the following cases.

Replace the gear with new part if its tooth surfaces are broken, damaged or excessively worn.   
Correct or replace if the cone that contacts the baulk ring is rough or damaged.   
Correct or replace if the inner surface or end face is damaged.   
4) Baulk ring, synchro cone   
Replace the baulk ring and synchro cone in the following cases.   
When the inner surface and end face are damaged.   
When the baulk ring inner surface is abnormally or partially worn down.   
fthe gap between the end faces of the baulk ring and the gear splined part is excessively small, check the clearance (A) while pressing the ring against the cone.

Clearance (A): 0.5 mm (0.020 in) or more

![](images/d9fec9d439cf81ab23f60d5bb4b385c3f63c64d746c9e0591296f657fe927f92.webp)

When the contact surface of the baulk ring insert section is damaged or abnormally worn.   
Apply transmission gear oil to the cone of the gear and while press-fitting the baulk ring, check there isno rotation in the circumferential direction.   
5) Coupling sleeve and synchronizer hub   
•"Check the slipping condition of the coupling sleeve.   
Check the splines on the coupling sleeve and synchronizer hub for wear.   
6 Shifting insert   
Replace the shifting inser if there is deformation, excessive wear on the balsection or any defectiveness.

# E: INSPECTION

Repair or replace the differential gear in the following cases:

When the hypoid driven gear and drive pinion shaft tooth surfaces are damaged, excessively worn, or seized.

When the roller bearing on the drive pinion shaft has a worn or damaged roller path.

When there is damage, wear or seizure of the diffrential bevel pinion, differential bevel gear, adjusting washer, pinion shaft or straight pin.

When the differential case sliding surfaces are worn or damaged.

# 3.  TOOTH CONTACT OF HYPOID DRIVEN GEAR

Check tooth contact of hypoid driven gear as follows: Apply a thin uniform coat of red lead on both teeth surfaces on 3 or 4 teeth of the hypoid gear. Move the hypoid driven gear back and forth by turning the transmission main shaft until a definite contact pattern is déveloped on the hypoid driven gear, and judge whether face contact is correct. When the contact pattern is not correct, adjust. <Ref. to 6MT-142, ADJÜSTMENT, Front Differential Assembly.>

# C: CAUTION

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation or disassembly. Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.   
Before emoval staltion o disasembly, esure to clarify the failure.Avoid unnecessary emoval istallation, disassembly and replacement.   
Vehicle components are extremely hot after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts. Use SUBARU genuine fluid, grease etc. or equivalent. Do not mix fluid, grease, etc. of diferent grades or manufacturers.   
Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.   
Apply grease onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installtion.   
Before instaling -rings or snap rings, apply sufficient amount of fluid to avoid damage and deformation. Before securing a part in a vise, place cushioning material such as wood blocksalminum plate or cloth between the part and the vise.   
Keep fluid away from the vehicle body. If any fluid contacts the vehicle body, immediately flush the area with water.

# . Flywheel

# A: REMOVAL

1) Remove the transmission assembly. <Ref. to 6MT-27, REMOVAL, Manual Transmission Assembly.>   
2) Remove the clutch cover and clutch disc. <Ref. to CL-9, REMOVAL, Clutch Disc and Cover.> 3) Attach the ST.

# ST 498497100 CRANKSHAFT STOPPER

![](images/4f007affdf7a1df5d6d083b70443dfaba2ac7bb52ede2ea4028ba1de77fb0de0.webp)

(AFlywheel

4) Remove the flywheel and crankshaft position sensor plate. 5) Drive out the pilot bearing from the flywheel.

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Press in a new pilot bearing to the position where it is flush with the flywheel surface or up to 0.4 mm (0.016 in) deeper than that.

CAUTION: Do not press the bearing inner ring.

![](images/064205abc2f66b64d5ea7283604aca1062a8b77b965613708f864c94dcea7ee4.webp)

A Pilot bearing

2) Temporarily tighten the crankshaft position sensor plate and flywheel.

NOTE:

Align the knock pin hole of the crankshaft position sensor plate to the knock pin of the crankshaft to secure the knock pin.

![](images/02ee3f587a14e20e11fc622b17de12fd54c60d6e465527b2a3deea20a217332e.webp)

4) Tighten the flywheel mounting bolts in two stages.

(1) Tighten the flywheel attachment bolts.

Tightening torque: 30 Nm(3.1 kgf-m, 22.1ft-b)

![](images/f092398c11339c2399c0851df3b6f3a021d401b994969cb7e0b8e20e88ca6371.webp)

(2) While checking the tightening angle with the angle gauge, further tighten the flywheel mounting bolts.

# Tightening angle: 30°-35°

5) Install the clutch disc and clutch cover. <Ref. to CL-9, INSTALLATION, Clutch Disc and Cover.> 6) Install the transmission assembly. <Ref. to 6MT37, INSTALLATION, Manual Transmission Assembly.>

1) Install the clutch pipe to the mass damper, clutch damper, master cylinder and pipe grommet.

NOTE:   
Temporarily tighten the clutch pipe (D) to the clutch damper.

Tightening torque: T: 15 NбН (1.5 kgf-m, 11.1 ft-lb)

![](images/e322b648f4cd69224b95389e951d680ff7025e7877c8de1af36c6e8761fc3566.webp)

(A) Clutch pipe (B) Mass damper (C) Clutch pipe grommet Clutch pipe

2) Install the pedal assembly. <Ref. to CL-26, INSTALLATION, Clutch Pedal.> 3) Install the tank hose to the clutch pipe.

# CAUTION:

Be sure to install the tank hose with the marking side facing upward.

4) Engage the clutch pipe with the connector attached to the clutch bracket.

Tightening torque: T1: 7.5 Nm (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 ft-b) T2: 18 Nm (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-ib)

![](images/ef0561cb052abe92bef98e0054996b73af569c5bcb1d76dad147d39724cfc25a.webp)

6) Install the steering column. <Ref. to PS-32, INSTALLATION, Steering Column.> 7) Install the clutch hose to the operating cylinder.

# CAUTION:

Be sure to install the clutch hose with the marking side facing upward.

NOTE: Use a new gasket.

Tightening torque: 18 NбН (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

8) Install the clutch hose to the clutch hose bracket, and install the clamp.

# CAUTION:

Be sure to install the clutch hose with the marking side facing upward.   
Install the clutch hoses while making sure that there is no twisting.

(A) Clamp (B Clutch hose (Clutch hose bracket

9) Install the clutch pipe.

Tightening torque: T: 15 Nm (1.5 kgf-m, 11.1 ft-lb)

(A)Clutch pipe

10) Fill the recommended brake fluid. <Ref. to CL2, Clutch Fluid.>   
11) Bleed air from the clutch system, and ensure thát no fluid leaks. <Ref. to CL-24, PROCEDURE, Clutch Fluid Air Bleeding.>   
12) Install the instrument panel lower cover. <Ref. to EI-79, INSTALLATION, Instrument Panel Lower Cover.>   
1) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H4DO)- 10, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>   
14) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>

# C: INSPECTION

Check the clutch pipe, tank hose and clutch hose for breaks and damage. Check the joint for brake fluid leakage. If crack, breakage or damage is found, repair or replace the faulty clutch pipe, tank hose or clutch hose.

# Clutch Fluid

# Clutch Fluid

# A: INSPECTION

CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill the brake fluid. Brake fluid spilled on the vehicle body will harm the paint surface; wash it off with water and wipe clean quickly if spilled.

1) Park the vehicle on a level surface. 2) Check the brake fluid level using the scale on the outside of the reservoir tank. If the level is below "MIN", fill the brake fluid up to "MAX" level, and make sure that there is no leakage.

# CAUTION:

This reservoir tank has the brake fluid chamber and the clutch fluid chamber. When checking the fluid level, always check the fluid from th clutch fluid chamber side where the tank hose is connected.

Recommended brake fluid: New FMVSS No. 116 DOT3 or DOT4

![](images/2952d1ef42ff28af0b48173831909c55765adf3bece56363c097657b7e8f57a1.webp)

(A) Reservoir tank   
(B) Clutch fluid chamber   
(C) MAX. level   
(D) MIN. level   
(E) Tank hose

# B: REPLACEMENT

CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill the brake fluid. Brake fluid spilled on the vehicle body will harm the paint surface; wash it off with water and wipe clean quickly if spilled.

Use new FMVSS No. 116 DOT3 or DOT4. Cover the air bleeder with cloth to prevent brake fluid from being splashed on surrounding parts when loosening the bleeder. Avoid mixing brake flüid of different brands to prevent fluid performance from degrading. Be careful not to allow dirt or dust to enter the reservoir tank.

NOTE:

During the bleeding operation, keep the reservoir tank filled with brake fluid to prevent entry of air.

Clutch pedal must be operated very slowly.   
Bleed air from the oil line with help of a co-worker.   
The required amount of brake fluid is approximately 165 mL (5.6 US fl oz, 5.8 Imp fl oz) for total clutch system.   
1) Remove the clip (A) from the air intake boot. 2) Loosen the clamp (B) connecting the air intake boot and air cleaner case (rear).   
3) Loosen the clamp (C) which'connects the air intake boot and throttle body.

![](images/2f22a4fdb98be5c183cc08c3b34899c39679ecb216ac1de9c431e1dbe76569e1.webp)

4) Remove the air intake boot from the throtle body, and move it to the left side wheel apron.

![](images/ffe2e621449b3a39ab79e0fb8223bff8c4bbe02e97e331ff407926a24af1e7ff.webp)

5) Drain the brake fluid from the reservoir tank. 6) Refill the reservoir tank with recommended brake fluid.

# Recommended brake fluid: New FMVSS No. 116 DOT3 or DOT4

7) Bleed air from brake fluid. <Ref. to CL-24, Clutch Fluid Air Bleeding.> a hee ooe10 INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>

# Clutch Fluid Air Bleeding

# A: PROCEDURE

CAUTION:

Be careful not to spill the brake fluid. Brake fluid spilled on the vehicle body will harm the paint surface; wash it off with water and wipe clean quickly if spilled.

# NOTE:

Bleed air from the oil line with help of a co-worker. 1) Remove the clip (A) from the air intake boot. 2) Loosen the clamp (B) connecting the air intake boot and air cleaner case (rear). 3) Loosen the clamp (C) which' connects the air intake boot and throttle body.

![](images/ee22a5bad2aadc510a9ae5eaf834db653e94137df825985f59f054bdcb8ff2d0.webp)

4) Remove the air intake boot from the throttle body, and move it to the left side wheel apron.

![](images/aacd4480d19999b6776c77ae84be53cdc9520456bbf7776ce876f26f02258742.webp)

5) Fit one end of a vinyl tube into the air bleeder of the operating cylinder, and put the other end into a container.

![](images/799aa4bb60b97523e0d571a1400fbe5a61f1efda94ef2a0b0586c123560ed96c.webp)

(AAir bleeder

6) Slowly depress the clutch pedal several times and keep it depressed. Then open the air bleeder to discharge air together with the brake fluid. Release the air bleeder for 1 or 2 seconds. Next, close the air bleeder, and slowly release the clutch pedal.

# CAUTION:

Cover the air bleeder with cloth to prevent brake fluid from being splashed on surrounding parts when loosening the bleeder.

![](images/488e06b35b297ec3963fe688deeda97c7ca7a8133b0be6e190c56cbde599c8af.webp)

AOperating cylinder (BVinyl tube

) Repeat procedure 6), until there are no more air bubbles appearing from the air bleeder. 8 Tighten the air bleeder.

Tightening torque: T: 7.8 NбН (0.8 kgf-m, 5.8 ft-lb)

![](images/41f9172be29f59ee013604f02c14ad0e9a2ee98d2286a3f099996eaf92bb30d9.webp)

9) After stepping on the clutch pedal, make sure that there are no leaks evident in the entire clutch system. 10) After bleeding the air from clutch system, ensure that the clutch operates properly. 11) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H4DO)- 10, INSTALLATION, Air Intake Boot.>

# 10.Clutch Pedal

# A: REMOVAL

CAUTION:

Before handling _the airbag system components, refer to "CAUTION" of "General Description'" in "AIRBAG SYSTEM". <Ref. to AB-10, CAUTION, General Description.>

1) Turn the ignition switch to OFF.   
2) Disconnect the ground terminal from the battery sensor, and wait for at least 60 seconds before starting work. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
3) Remove the clip (A) from the air intake boot. 4) Loosen the clamp (B) connecting the air intake boot and air cleaner case (rear).   
5) Loosen the clamp (C) which'connects the air intake boot and throte body.

![](images/391bfdac63f05b1b4432923dbd465fbd18555a2bae4fd178c92ddd98dd37c036.webp)

6) Remove the air intake boot from the throtle body, and move it to the left side wheel apron.

![](images/8565e04ae31b6292166777f6cb15f3762c315c9d6395f065e8fd99076aafae66.webp)

7) Drain the brake fluid. <Ref. to CL-23, Clutch Fluid.>   
8) Disconnect the clutch pipe.

![](images/b369efec5e7a69e26ae9ad1bb247aab9d31590f18413c07edf568008a8529ef0.webp)

9) Remove the clutch bracket.

![](images/78cd2a4e6af597eef2b0586f1efab0a1598a8937701096f0ecec9304aa16cd64.webp)

10) Disconnect the tank hoses.

![](images/e5025ab2fa5336ff36cd9a13974ad935b615a9a52df5d5c31c86fc72f5787ebe.webp)

11) Remove the instrument panel lower cover. <Ref. to EI-78, REMOVAL, Instrument Panel Lower Cover.>   
12) Remove the steering column. <Ref. to PS-30, RуMOVAL, Steering Column.>   
13) Disconnect the connector from the clutch switch and clutch start switch.   
14) Disconnect the connector from the brake switch.   
15) Remove the snap pin and clevis pin connecting thé operating rod and brake pedal.

16) Remove the pedal assembly.

NOTE:

Place vinyl, etc. in order not to drop the brake fluid to the floor carpet.

![](images/1fd4acf3d735be5527341977b8b5e832f06141082fbdbc3ce85b49e39ccc8def.webp)

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the pedal assembly.

Tightening torque: T: 18 Nm (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/fc00d5143838607cd4c318bb62313af0697bce510ff61c09b6bc8c8799a2289d.webp)

2) Instal the snap pin and clevis pin connecting the operating rod and brake pedal.

# CAUTION:

# Always use a new clevis pin.

3) Connect the connector to the brake switch. 4) Connect the connector to the clutch switch and clutch start switch. 5) Install the steering column. <Ref. to PS-32, INSTALLATION, Steering Column.> 6) Connect the tank hose to the clutch pipe.

![](images/95631adfe0bee2f6a3b3ef3ef009cc89a19d94bd23d4dad26202dd17741c84c2.webp)

7) Install the clutch bracket.

Tightening torque: T1: 7.5 Nm (0.8 kgf-m, 5.5 f-lb) T2: 18 NбН (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/7254cc6746bb7099ef43c70675090b6d09a5f5bbebf264afc3e65e7e4430ad97.webp)

8) Install the clutch pipe.

Tightening torque: 15 NбН (1.5 kgf-m, 11.1 ft-lb)

![](images/60b203404a4b424eba4fda39ac44b054f9cbf07cceb9e62e01074dce0541ed01.webp)

9) Fill the recommended brake fluid. <Ref. to CL  
23, Clutch Fluid.>

10) After bleeding air from the clutch system, ensure that no fluid leaks and the clutch operates properly. <Ref. to CL-24, PROCEDURE, Clutch Fluid Air Bleeding.   
11) Install the instrument panel lower cover. <Ref. to EI-79, INSTALLATION, Instrument Panel Lower Cover.>   
12) Install the air intake boot. <Ref. to IN(H4DO)- INSTALLATION Air Ie oot.   
13) Adjust the clutch pedal. <Ref. to CL-29, ADJUSTMENT, Clutch Pedal.>   
14) Connect the ground terminal to battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
15) Check the clutch start system.

# C: DISASSEMBLY

1) Disconnect the clutch pipe.

![](images/5b440cb975f26430c41261d0deb42e207d4ebea3eadbc9246aebf74c56749c7f.webp)

2) Remove the clutch damper mounting nut, and disconnect the clutch pipe from the clamp.

![](images/7905ac186eaede434fe2c769d8dd148506d14fa32e14ac7a473c1d1838fde475.webp)

3) Remove the clutch switches.

4) Remove the clip and pull out the clevis pin.

![](images/0acde68a8875be0bbf2b0fc9fbc917f33dd80767b0ba98172e8944c5524a30aa.webp)

(A Clevis pin (B) Clip

5) Disconnect the connector from the clutch stroke sensor, and then remove the sensor harness. 6) Remove the master cylinder.

CAUTION:   
The clutch stroke sensor cannot be disassembled.

NOTE:

Secure the push rod with a tape etc. to prevent it from falling off.

![](images/a41fcfe74b3ddf7179bc656f44d7935d11ee8438262d423d7ad509af7d7c7dda.webp)

(A Master cylinder

7 Remove the torsion spring and assist bushing.

![](images/e5b8d11229164f6e1cb9ff6c4ba8a132b174d7d58e6ed5af9997c5ac59841816.webp)

(ATorsion spring (BAssist bushing

8) Remove the clutch pedal.

![](images/c2564260ef17ee10b686cabd23943521bfdcbaa0be89ab9f0a9ebe5ba6b638eb.webp)

(AClutch pedal

9) Remove the bushing, spacer, bushing A, clutch pedal stopper, torsion spring bushing and clutch pedal pad.

![](images/113ee07d6839d7312923f7c04a929548c10b9c1b139793689395a597cd4a5fe3.webp)

(A) Bushing   
(B) Spacer   
(C) Bushing A   
(D) Clutch pedal stopper   
(E) Torsion spring bushing   
(F) Clutch pedal pad   
(G) Clutch pedal

# D: ASSEMBLY

1) Clean the holes in the sliding surface between the clutch pedal and bushing, and apply grease. 2) Attach the clutch pedal pad, clutch pedal stopper, bushing A, torsion spring bushing, spacer and bushing to the clutch pedal.

NOTE:

Clean the inside of the bushings and apply grease before installing the spacer.

3) Install the clutch pedal.

Tightening torque: T:30Nm(3.1 kgm22.1b)

![](images/340721939c56f55d12737a2ce2099f7d53e56f1bc33bc62f48d1cb0ab1625bd7.webp)

(AClutch pedal

4) Install the assist bushing and torsion spring to the pedal assembly.

NOTE:   
Before installing the torsion spring, apply grease to the assist bushing and torsion spring bushing. 5) Install the master cylinder. NOTE:   
Secure the push rod with a tape etc. to prevent it from falling off.

Tightening torque: T: 18 Nm (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/72b94b5387bcbc8a4227153efeb50c957ea939658878867b0073c76a0c83b536.webp)

(AMaster cylinder

6) Secure the clevis pin with mounting clip.

# CAUTION: Always use a new clevis pin.

NOTE: Before installing the clevis pin, apply grease.

![](images/a2301e7565b644cfd9ff43b12b77c18b79623a703a4f06d2c33908648b6fa250.webp)

(A Clevis pin (B Clip

7) Attach the sensor harness, and connect the connector to the clutch stroke sensor.

8) Install the clutch switch. 9) Install the clutch damper to the pedal assembly, and connect the clutch pipe to the master cylinder.

Tightening torque: T1: 15 Nm (1.5 kgf-m, 11.1 ft-lb) T2: 18 NбН (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/a17080143a8854a2748c4617112edae324928fa10a38c56172141275a3bf615c.webp)

# E: INSPECTION

Move the clutch pedal pads in the lateral direction with a force of approximately 10 N (1 kgf, 2 Ibf) to check that the clutch pedal deflection is within the service limit.

CAUTION: If it exceeds the service limit, replace the clutch pedal assembly with a new part.

Deflection of the clutch pedal: Service limit 4.0 mm (0.157 in) or less

![](images/189b8c84b9e15d45abe1622e50894a9c80bdea7d552d5d3c071a301114ab9a3d.webp)

A) Clutch pedal BBrake pedal

# F: ADJUSTMENT

1) If the full stroke of the clutch pedal is not within the specified value, loosen the lock nuts of the clutch switch and adjust the full stroke of the clutch pedal with the clutch switch.

# CAUTION:

When adjusting the full stroke of clutch pedal, do not turn the clutch switch.

Clutch pedal full stroke A: 130 — 135 mm (5.12 — 5.31 in)

Tightening torque: T: 8 Nm (0.8 kgm, 5.9 -b)

![](images/c3fa277320fb3ef8865e7c001a0a6ce78f980b34497719d447e4c5633d14daad.webp)

2) Depress and release the clutch pedal two or three times to ensure that the clutch pedal and release lever operate smoothly. If the clutch pedal and release lever do not opérate smoothly, bleed air from the clutch hydraulic system. <Ref. to CL24, Clutch Fluid Air Bleeding.>   
3) Measure the clutch pedal full stroke length again to ensure that it is within specifications. If it is not within specifications, repeat adjustment procedures again from the beginning.

# Clutch pedal full stroke: 130 — 135 mm (5.12 — 5.31 in)

4) Push the release lever until the operating cylinder push rod retracts. Check that the brake fluid level in the reservoir tank increases.

![](images/c332a7ced48bb5177d789c1f3cfa39380f2d0814c56901d87d87eeca8194419c.webp)

(A) Push rod (B) Release lever (C) Operating cylinder

5) If the brake fluid level increases, hydraulic clutch play is correct.

6) If the brake fluid level does not increase or push ród does not retract, readjust the clutch pedal.

7) Check the brake fluid level using the scale on the outside of reservoir tank. <Ref. to CL-23, INSPECTION, Clutch Fluid.>

# 11.Clutch Switch

# A: REMOVAL

1) Disconnect the ground _terminal from battery sensor. <Ref. to RC-4, BATTERY, NOTE, Repair Contents.>   
2) Remove the instrument panel lower cover. <Ref. to El-78, REMOVAL, Instrüment Panel Lower Cover.>   
3) Disconnect the connector from the clutch switch and clutch start switch.   
4) Remove the clutch switch and clutch start switch.

# B: INSTALLATION

# 1.  CLUTCH SWITCH

1) Install the clutch switch. 2) Move the clevis pin of push rod to left and right, retain it at the position where it moves smoothly, and measure the clutch pedal stroke.

Clutch pedal full stroke A: 130 — 135 mm (5.12 — 5.31 in)

Tightening torque: T:8 Nm (0.8 kgf-m 5.9fb)

![](images/f38919f899e93d2073b17f28b8aaf886495c1f78fa46cae6141089aeb85781d4.webp)

3) If the clutch pedal stroke is out of specification, adjust the stroke. <Ref. to CL-29, ADJUSTMENT, Clutch Pedal.>   
4) Connect the connector to the clutch switch. 5 Thereafter, install in the reverse order of removal.

# 2. CLUTCH START SWITCH

1) Install the clutch start switch.   
2 Fully depress the clutch pedal and hold it.   
3) Install so that gap (A) of the clutch pedal plate and clutch start switch is 2.9 mm (0.11 in), and tighten the lock nut.

Tightening torque: 8 NбН (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)

![](images/3303e09eff4d698d5b3d0331d782541e384539e5542027d0bc70597ba88f262a.webp)

(A) 2.9 mm (0.11 in) (B) Clutch pedal plate (C) Clutch start switch (DLock nut

4) Connect the connector to the clutch start switch. 5) Make sure that engine does not start with clutch pedal not depressed.   
6) Make sure that engine starts with clutch pedal fully depressed.   
7 Thereafter, install in the reverse order of removal.

# C: INSPECTION

# 1. CLUTCH START SWITCH

1) Perform the following inspections. If the clutch start switch does not operate normally, adjust the switch, and check it again. <Ref. to CL-33, ADJUSTMENT, Clutch Switch.>

Make sure that engine does not start with clutch pedal not depressed.   
:Make sure that engine starts with clutch pedal fully depressed.   
2) When the clutch start switch does not operate normally even if it is adjusted, check the clutch start switch for continuity.

(1) Remove the clutch start switch. <Ref. to CL31, REMOVAL, Clutch Switch.>

(2) Measure the resistance between terminal 1 and 2 of the switch. If the resistance is not at the standard value, replace the switch.

![](images/7079189a60864ea41cbd53a62d2548f917edf5b35cd46027233fc65e62650436.webp)

![](images/67563b03345cc7a6f149eae3e64e0d634a7c41dc4bd66464a292fa96a2525d26.webp)

(3) Check that the switch is turned on and off in dimension L.

Dimension L: 4 — 5.5 mm (0.16 — 0.22 in)

![](images/c887f6f309300f4d63bf2e9706266ae92f2d5c30bd628be8e540dfc25359bad0.webp)

(A) ON (B OFF

(4) Install the clutch start switch. <Ref. to CL31, CLUTCH START SWITCH, INSTALLATIэN, Clutch Switch.>

# 2. CLUTCH SWITCH

1) Check the clutch switch for continuity. (1) Disconnect the connector of clutch switch. (2) Measure the resistance between terminal 1 and 2 of the switch. If the resistance is not within the specification, check the clutch stroke and installation condition, and check the clutch switch again.

![](images/a718fd80dd219892b7e3629ee3fa71fea51cd4ac6e67cc339d73c3b2cae1f2f3.webp)

![](images/b022d14db63d602c6bbb3417a7c712e35ee96edf1999d917cc3935be501b8e6e.webp)

2) When the clutch switch does not operate normally even if the clutch stroke and installation condition are normal, check the clutch switch for continuity.

(1) Remove the clutch switches. <Ref. to CL31, REMOVAL, Clutch Switch.> (2) Measure the resistance between terminal 1 and 2 of the switch. If the resistance is not at the standard value, replace the switch.

![](images/094cbddc9473ac5106d3321a3fcc75b855bffb3a16fb5744698925dfd42b6bd3.webp)

![](images/fe3ae9fb48bf7fa23446311025aaacf544f39b4dcdd1b499eb1b06af2bf0128d.webp)

(3) Check that the switch is turned on and off in dimension L.

Dimension L: 5 — 6.5 mm (0.2 — 0.26 in)

![](images/6a9a2c6c95565b736b445f1360db522c11b78c0881c4a73757451f9d81b6e5e3.webp)

(A) ON (B) OFF

(4) Install the clutch switch. <Ref. to CL-31, CуUTCH SWITCH, INSTALLATION, Clutch Switch.>

# D: ADJUSTMENT

1) Loosen the lock nut of the clutch start switch. 2) Fully depress the clutch pedal and hold it. 3) Adjust the gap (A) of the clutch pedal plate and the clutch start switch to be 2.9 mm (0.11 in).

![](images/329766d6f5329642091586f24b8c4eac470ade03749fbbf31470de26b9175bce.webp)

(A) 2.9 mm (0.11 in) (B) Clutch pedal plate (C) Clutch start switch (DLock nut

4) Tighten the lock nut.

Tightening torque: 8 NбН (0.8 kgf-m, 5.9 ft-lb)

This service manual has been prepared to provide SUBARU service personnel with the necessary information and data for the correct maintenance and repair of SUBARU vehicles.

This manual includes the procedures for maintenance, disassembling, reassembling, inspection and adjustment of components and diagnostics for guidance of experienced mechanics.

Please peruse and utilize this manual fully to ensure complete repair work for satisfying our customers by keeping their vehicle in optimum condition. When replacement of parts during repair work is needed, be sure to use SÜBARU genuine parts.

# c: CAUTION

When performing any work, always wear work clothes, a work cap and protective shoes. Additional, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary.

When disposing of strut COMPL -front, be sure to bleed the oil or gas out completely. Also, do not expose o flames or fire.

When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement.

Use SUBARU genuine grease, the recommended or equivalent. Do not mix grease etc. of different grade or manufacturers.

Do not secure a part in a vise directly. Place cushioning materials such as wood pieces, blocks, aluminum plates, or waste cloth between the part and the vise.

Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle.

When the suspension-related components have been removed, installed or replaced, perform the followng adjustment.

- Lane keep assist learning value clear (model with EyeSight): <Ref. to ES(diag)-49, OPERATION, Clear Active Lane Keep System Learning Value.>   
-VDC sensor midpoint setting mode: <Ref. to VDC-16, ADJUSTMENT, VDC Control Module and Hydraulic Control Unit (VDCM&H/U).

For parts which are not reusable, always use new parts. Other parts should be replaced with new parts a: requiréd.

When handling oil or fuel, adhere to the following to prevent unexpected accident. — Be careful with fire. Prepare a container to catch grease or oil, etc. If any grease or oil spills, wipe it off and clean immediately to prevent from penetrating into floor or flowing outside. —Follow all government and local regulations concerning disposal of refuse when disposing.

Be sure that the surface of brake disc or brake pad is free from grease or oil.

Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. Some vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

# Wheel Alignment

# A: INSPECTION

Check the following items before performing the wheel alignment measurement.

Tire inflation pressure   
Uneven wear of RH and LH tires, or difference of sizes Tire runout Excessive play and wear of ball joint Excessive play and wear of tie-rod end Excessive play of wheel bearing   
Right and left wheel base imbalance   
Deformation and excessive play of steering link   
Deformation and excessive play of suspension parts   
Check, adjust and measure the wheel alignment in accordance with the following procedures.

![](images/1ae4681492c5d8280815e69048214eef5ff4870d2e603c7f1948d88bbb8144a7.webp)

# 1.  WHEEL ARCH HEIGHT

1) Park the vehicle on a level surface.   
2) Empty the vehicle so that it is at "curb weight”.

NOTE:

Empty the trunk or luggage room, load the spare tire, jack and service tools, and fillup the fuel tank. 3 Set the steering wheel in a straight-ahead position, and stabilize the suspension by moving the vehicle in a straight line for 5 m (16 ft) or more.   
4) Suspend a thread from the wheel arch (point “A" in the figure below) and afix at a position directly above the center of wheel.   
5) Measure the distance between the point “A” and the center of wheel.

![](images/79909ab266faef0c081ab4752529c2c5a6d7de84d88b2e2ccf5fa1a2c9c709cf.webp)

# 5.  FRONT WHEEL TOE-IN

Toe-in: Inspection value 0±3 mm (0±0.12 in)

1) Set the toe-in gauge in the position at wheel axis center height behind the right and left front tires.   
2 Place a mark at the center of both left and right tires, and measure distance “A" between the marks.   
3) Move the vehicle forward to rotate the tires 180°.

NOTE:   
Be sure to rotate the tires in the forward direction.   
4) Measure the distance “B" between the left and right marks. Find toe-in using the following calculation:

# A -B = Toe-in

# 7. THRUST ANGLE

1) Park the vehicle on a level surface.   
2) Move the vehicle 3 — 4 meters (10 — 13 feet) straight forward.   
3) Draw the center of loci for both the front and rear axles.   
4) Measure distance “L" between the center lines of the axle loci.

Thrust angle: Inspection value 0°±30 Less than 30' when “L" is 23 mm (0.9 in) or less

When adjusting the toe-in, adjust it to the following value. <Ref. to FS-17, ADJUSTMENT OF DIFFERENCE BETWEEN RIGHT AND LEFT STEERING ANGLES, ADJUSTMENT, WhEl AligNMNT.

Toe-in: Adjustment value 0±2 mm (0±0.08 in)

1) Check that the left and right wheel steering angles are within specification.   
Loosen the left and right side steering tie-rod lock nuts (a).   
3) Turn the left and right tie-rods by equal amounts until the toe-in is at the specification.

NOTE:

Both the left and right tie-rods are right-hand threaded. To increase toe-in, turn both tie-rods clockwise by equal amount (viewing from the inside of vehicle).   
4) Tighten the steering tie-rod lock nut (a).

Toe-in: Adjustment value 3±2 mm (0.12±0.08 in)

1) Loosen the self-locking nut after holding the bolt head section of lateral link assembly - front.

NOTE: When loosening or tightening the adjusting bolt, hold the bolt head and turn the self-locking nut.

:Tighten the cradle and main mounting to the specified torque first before tightening the universal joint assembly - steering to avoid the steering effort from becoming heavy. Always install the universal joint assembly - steering after installing the steering column to avoid damage to the universal joint assembly - steering. Be sure to follow the tightening order and tightening torque of the universal joint assembly - steering to avoid the steering effort from becoming heavy. After confirming that the steering column position is in the neutral position, tighten the universal joint assembly - steering. Always place the tilt lever to the lock position after the steering column is adjusted.

# C: CAUTION

When performing any work, always wear work clothes, a work cap and protective shoes. Aditionally, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary.

When disposing of shock absorbers, be sure to bleed the oil or gas out completely. Also, do not expose tc flames or fire.

When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement.

Use SUBARU genuine grease, the recommended or equivalent. Do not mix grease etc. of different grade or manufacturers.

Do not secure a part in a vise directy. Place cushioning materials such as wood blocks, aluminum plates, or waste cloth between the part and the vise.

Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the vehicle.

When the suspension-related components have been removed, installed or replaced, perform the followng adjustment.

– Lane keep assist learning value clear (model with EyeSight): <Ref. to ES(diag)-49, OPERATION, Clear Active Lane Keep System Learning Value.>   
-VDC sensor midpoint setting mode: <Ref. to VDC-16, ADJUSTMENT, VDC Control Module and Hydraulic Control Unit (VDCM&H/U).

For parts which are not reusable, always use new parts. Other parts should be replaced with new parts a requiréd.

When handling oil or fuel, adhere to the following to prevent unexpected accident. — Be careful with fire. Prepare a container to catch grease or oil, etc f any grease or oil sill, wipe it off and clean immediately to prevent from penetrating into floor or flowing outside. —Follow all government and local regulations concerning disposal of refuse when disposing.

Be sure that the surface of brake disc or brake pad is free from grease or oil.

Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. Some vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

# Tire and Wheel

A: REMOVAL

1) Lift up the vehicle.   
2) Remove the wheel nut.   
3) Remove the wheels.

When removing the wheels, be careful not to damage the bolt - hub.

B: INSTALLATION

1) Install the wheels to vehicle.   
2) Tighten the wheel nuts to the specified torque.

Tightening torque: 120 NбН (12.2 kgf-m, 88.5 ft-lb)

C: INSPECTION

1. TIRE

CAUTION:

When replacing a tire, make sure to use tires of the same size, construction and load range as orig inally installed.

# Temporary Tire

A: NOTE

“T-type” or “Temporary” tire for temporary use is equipped as a temporary tire.

CAUTION:

•The "T-type” or "Temporary" tire is only for temporary use. Replace with a standard equipment sized tire as soon as possible.   
Do not use standard sized tire chains for "T-type" or "Temporary" tires. Because tire size is small, tire chains can not be installed and will damage the vehicle and tires.   
Do not drive at a speed greater than 80 km/h (50 MPH).   
Drive the vehicle as slowly as possible and avoid bumps on the road.

# B: REPLACEMENT

Refer to “Tire and Wheel" for removal and installation of the “T-type" or "Temporary" tire. <Ref. to WT-6, Tire and Wheel.>

# C: INSPECTION

Refer to “Tire and Wheel" for inspection of the "“T-type" or "Temporary" tire. <Ref. to WT-6, TIRE, INSPECTION, Tire and Wheel.>

If the transmitte is replaced, ID registration for the transmitter is required. <Ref. to TPM(diag)-12, OPERATION, Register Transmitter (iD).> When adjusting tire pressure indoors in winter, there is a big temperature diference between the indoor fa cilities and outside. # TPM(diag)-14

# Tire Pressure Warning Light / Trouble Indicator Light Illumination Pattern

1 When the tire pressure warning light does not iluminate in accordance with this illumination pattern, there must be an electrical malfunction. ) If the tire pressure warning light does not go off check the TPMS & keyless entry CM or TPMS CM/warning light circuit and the combination meter circuit. <Ref. to TPM(diag)-15, TIRE PRESSURE WARNING LIGHT DOES NOT COME OFF, Tire Pressure Warning Light / Trouble Indicator Light Illumination Pattern.>

NOTE:

If the problem is fixed while driving at approximately 40 km/h (25 MPH) after the tire pressure warning light blinks/lights, the warning light goes out and the tire pressure monitor system operates normally. (If there is a decrease in tire pressure, or a malfunction of the system, the malfunction history is displayed.)

# B:  TIRE PRESSURE WARNING LIGHT DOES NOT COME ON

# Detecting condition:

Defective combination meter   
Trouble symptom:   
When the ignition switch is turned to ON, the tire pressure warning light does not turn on (for approx. 2 seconds).

# C: CAUTION

When performing any work, always wear work clothes, a work cap and protective shoes. Additional, wear a helmet, protective goggles, etc. if necessary.

Remove contamination including dirt and corrosion before removal, installation, disassembly or assembly Keep the disassembled parts in order and protect them from dust and dirt.

When performing a repair, identify the cause of trouble and avoid unnecessary removal, disassembly and replacement.

Use SUBARU genuine grease, the recommended or equivalent. Do not mix grease etc. of different grades or manufacturers.

•Do not secure a part in a vise directly. Place cushioning materials such as wood pieces, blocks, aluminum plates, or waste cloth between the part and the vise.

Be sure to tighten fasteners including bolts and nuts to the specified torque.

Always use the jack-up point when the shop jacks or rigid racks are used to support the ve

Apply grease onto sliding or revolving surfaces before installation.

Before instaling the O-ring or snap ring, apply a suffcient amount of gear oil to avoid damage and deformation.

Avoid damaging the mating surface of the case.

For parts which are not reusable, always use new parts. Other parts should be replaced with new parts as requiréd.

When handling oil or fuel, adhere to the following to prevent unexpected accident.

—Be careful with fire.   
Prepare a container to catch grease or oil, etc. If any grease or oil spill, wipe itoff and clean immediately to prevent from penetrating into floor or flowing outside.   
-Follow all government and local regulations concerning disposal of refuse when disposing.

Before disconnecting connectors of sensors or units, be sure to disconnect the ground cable from battery. Some vehicle components are extremely hot immediately after driving. Be wary of receiving burns from heated parts.

# Differential Gear Oil A: INSPECTION

1 Lift up the vehicle.

Remove the filler plug, and then check the gear oil. Replace the gear oil if it is contaminated, deteriorated or cloudy. <Ref. to DI-22, REPLACEMENT, Differential Gear Oil.>

3) Check that the gear oil level is within —5 mm (–0.2 in) from the bottom of the filler plug hole. If the level is low, make sure that there is no oil leakage and refill up to the bottom of filler plug hole.

# NOTE:

On VA1-types at factory settings, the oil level may be within –14 mm (−0.6 in) from the bottom of the filler plug. This is at normal level, requiring no oil refill

# B: REPLACEMENT

CAUTION:

Gear oil is extremely hot just after driving. Be wary of receiving burns.

Be careful not to spill the differential gear oil on exhaust pipe. If gear oil is spilled, wipe it off completely.

1) Lift up the vehicle.   
2 Remove the drain plug and filler plug, and drain the gear oil.

# Rear Differential (T-type)

# A: REMOVAL

1) Shift the select lever or gear shift lever to neutral. Release the electronic parking brake.

4 Lift up the vehicle.   
Remove the rear wheels.   
6) Drain differential gear oil. <Ref. to DI-22, REPLACEMENT, Differential Gear Oil.>

# B: INSTALLATION

1) Attach the rear differential member plate to the réar differential.

![](images/6228dba9dc1a2b11ed274a59a55f3d12b7197c7d89e2c6d647b11b1d4c7f58a0.webp)

A)Rear differential member plate (2.5 L OUTBACK model) (BRear differential member plate

) Set the rear differential to transmission jack. 3) Set the ST to the rear differential. ST 28099PA090 OIL SEAL PROTECTOR

![](images/8f0ef90d7bffdb7905c52dff3fa4a980e144ce8e2a73deb358c8be6a9595760b.webp)

4) Insert the rear drive shaft until the spline portion of the rear drive shaft exceeds the side oil seal.

![](images/81cab946e29fb81406e7f2197e624eca50db441a8ff687a0784040337815fc4a.webp)

5) Remove ST from rear differential.

6) Push the rear differential from side to side to insert the DOJ into rear differential completely.

![](images/c7c7e91de724366b56bc2d0f1a288b0b0e04a262aad8fec65f6cef2687b2ded1.webp)

7) Adjust the transmission jack, if necessary, and insert the rear differential stud bolt into the rear differential mount bushing properly.

![](images/da00b52b74d5ba8357754ea19c420e4ebc007b6328fbe7452399da8ab7d5fa8c.webp)

8) After inserting the rear differential stud bolt into the rear differential mount bushing, lift up the transmission jack and align the rear differential to its attachment position.

![](images/86622c96bf8569ef3b71d39b1afbdb151c6f6dfcc5067f7a8316211f6e4ce537.webp)

9) Tighten a new self-locking nut temporarily to the rear differential stud bolt.

![](images/b646b438d5b79a9f0617757e3aff0e6a8e61aa688c0c4c767cb078782683b592.webp)

10) Install the rear differential front member with a new self-locking nut.

Tightening torque: T1: 50 Nm (5.1 kgf-m, 36.9 ft-lb) T2: 110 Nm (11.2 kgf-m, 81.1 ft-lb)

![](images/b908c558d4ee09f98c5c332b2ea5fb17e7ee4659c7b5797c448411918b897561.webp)

11) Install the mass damper with a new self-locking nut. (2.5 L OUTBACK model)

Tightening torque: 50 NбН (5.1 kgf-m, 36.9 ft-lb)

![](images/41f4e09684e81732de12565b113463b000756c773cc7138b4a493e9fd576b2aa.webp)

12) Tighten the self-locking nut.

NOTE: For models other than OUTBACK model, tighten the self-locking nut using the ST. ST 41399YC000 SOCKET WRENCH (17)

Tightening torque: 70 NбН (7.1 kgf-m, 51.6 ft-lb)

![](images/48474298eae114d4326e89b22d37923aa1c94a31a0f1329ec74f52046be29555.webp)

13) Remove the transmission jack. 14) Install the propeller shaft.' <Ref. to DS-12, INSTALLATION, Propeller Shaft.>

15) Install the center exhaust cover.

Tightening torque: 18 NбН (1.8 kgf-m, 13.3 ft-lb)

![](images/bc5d11a94b4fc548e81366fddae206ec2da318d2142adf0ef0aaa497e1d0e9f1.webp)

16) Install the rear exhaust pipe.   
2.5 L model   
<Ref. to EX(H4DO)-17, INSTALLATION, Rear Exhaust Pipe.>   
3.6 L model   
<Ref. to EX(H6DO)-12, INSTALLATION, Rear Exhaust Pipe.>   
17) Fill differential gear oil. <Ref. to DI-22, REPLACEMENT, Differential Gear Oil.>   
18) Installing procedure hereafter is in the reverse order of removal.   
19) Perform “Rear differential inspection mode” using the Subaru Select Monitor. (VT model) <Ref. to DI-83, Rear Differential Inspection Mode.>

# CAUTION:

Be sure to perform rear differential inspection mode when the following work has been performed.

Replacement of rear differential   
Replacement of rear differential hypoid gear

Replacement of front differential hypoid gear

# C: DISASSEMBLY

To detect the real cause of trouble, inspect the following items before disassembling.

Tooth contact and backlash between hypoid driven gear and drive pinion   
Hypoid driven gear runout on its back surface Total preload of drive pinion   
1) Set the ST on vise and install the differential assembly to ST.

ST 398217700 ATTACHMENT SET

![](images/95f9532ba8e4ff487a0e1c15dfd551391d12b8f095ada8617384b6485ee17d5e.webp)

Remove the drain plug and filer plug.   
3) Remove the air breather cap.

NOTE:

Do not attempt to remove the air breather cap unless necessary.   
Whenever the air breather cap is removed, replace it with a new part.

![](images/4fc12b75f328135b106e440b90b2d34d091545313fcbd3f221097eb5baf4c5e3.webp)

4) Remove the bolts, and then remove the rear cover.

6) Remove the side retainer attachment bolts, set the ST to differential case, and extract the side retainers RH and LH with a puller.

NOTE:

Side retainer shim of each side should be kept together with its mating retainer. Keep the side retainers separate by attaching tags or in similar ways to make it possible to identify RH and LH sides during reassembly.

ST 398457700 ATTACHMENT

Do not attempt to disassemble the parts unless necessary.
